Owning the consequences doesn't mean doing penance: it is enough to understand what to do differently, and do it.

items.title: Seeing where the wheel turns

captions.B: Thoughtfulness and meaning amid the whirl

items.meaning: Each turn of life is something you learn to understand rather than just live through — that is why you met.
text: Something is always happening to you, and friends are long used to your unexpected news. The Wheel of Fortune keeps your life spinning; the Hermit asks you now and then to step off the merry-go-round and think: why this, what keeps repeating, what is it teaching. Your union is about not just living through changes but understanding them, so that on the next turn you choose with open eyes.

For the third time in five years you change rented flats, and for the third time it all repeats: delight at first, then the neighbours, the noise, the rows. This time, before looking for a new one, you set down on paper what you really need. It turns out to be not the centre or the view, but quiet and a patch of land of your own. The next move is the last. **Together you can stop the merry-go-round and make out a pattern in what seemed chance.**

Wheel and lantern argue when one lives on impulse and the other on reflection. The first is bored by waiting, the second afraid of rushing, and each sees the other as a hindrance. Or thoughtfulness turns into resignation: “it was meant to be”, and instead of conclusions there is only a sigh. Take stock together — what repeated, what to change — and only then spin the wheel on.

items.title: Two turns of one wheel

captions.A: A couple whose life is in full swing
captions.B: A shared rhythm of luck and gratitude

items.meaning: Your life goes in circles: you give thanks for the climbs and hold on to each other on the way down.
text: The Wheel of Fortune stands twice in your chart: in how you are seen and in what you are to create together. Your life together goes in circles: a rise, a fall, a turn, a new round, and friends can't keep track of your changes. This merry-go-round does not frighten you as long as you hold hands: you met to learn from the wheel — to be grateful for every turn, even the lowest.

You keep a shared notebook in which at the end of each year you write down everything that happened, good and bad, without picking and choosing. Rereading it one December, you notice that every hard page is followed a couple of months later by a lucky one — and each time the luck grew out of what had seemed a failure. **Your couple exists to see the whole circle and not mistake the lowest point for the end of the road.**

A double wheel rocks you harder. Your shared mood jumps with circumstances: today all is wonderful, tomorrow all is lost, and each blames the other for the downturn. Things are left to drift — “it'll pull through somehow” — while debts and promises pile up. The wheel always turns; what you must hold on to is not luck but each other.

items.title: A backbone at a sharp turn

captions.B: An inner core stronger than any luck

items.meaning: Your wheel turns often, and what holds you is a backbone you grow together.
text: Change comes to you often: a new job, a new city, a sudden chance that must not be missed — from outside it looks like luck. The Wheel of Fortune keeps your life spinning, and Strength makes sure you don't get seasick: endurance, persistence, the ability to keep hold of yourselves when everything is turned upside down. You are meant to become, together, stronger than any good luck or bad.

Your small business is having its worst season: orders have vanished, money is melting away. One of you snaps; the other silently takes a sheet of paper and works out how many months you can hold out if you cut everything unnecessary. It comes to seven. You hold out those seven months, and in the eighth a big order arrives that pulls everything through. **The wheel can turn any way it likes: together you hold on to what does not depend on luck — each other.**

Strength turns into a fight with fate when every turn is taken as a personal challenge. It didn't work — so push harder; it went downhill — so someone didn't push enough. Reproaches rain down on whoever proved weaker at a hard moment, and instead of support they get an exam. The wheel does not care how hard you dig in; what matters is whether you hold each other while it spins.

items.title: Waiting for the wheel to turn

captions.A: Lucky and quick off the mark
captions.B: Patience in the pauses between strokes of luck

items.meaning: Your luck learns patience: you see a pause not as a failure but as preparation for the next turn.
text: From outside you look lucky: you change jobs and cities easily, and it all works out. But the Wheel of Fortune turns downwards too, and the Hanged Man explains what to do at the bottom: stop, accept, look differently. You learn to wait together — without giving up or rushing about, trusting that the turn will come and noticing that a pause gives something of its own as well.

For two years you try to sell your old country cottage, and nothing comes of it: buyers turn up and vanish. Instead of cutting the price, you decide to spend the summer there — and unexpectedly fall in love with the place all over again: you mend the veranda, plant apple trees. When a year later a buyer arrives with a good price, you turn them down. **For you a stop turns out to be not a failure but a turn that simply hasn't shown its face yet.**

Patience becomes inaction when you start waiting for everything: the right year, a sign, someone to decide for you. Decisions hang for months, chances go by, and each secretly blames the other for not taking the first step. The Hanged Man is good as a pause before a leap; if the pause drags on, the wheel turns without you.

items.title: Luck around the bend

captions.B: A new chapter at every turn of fate

items.meaning: Luck comes to you at the turns, and you never mourn a closed door longer than you need to.
text: Luck comes to you not when everything stands still but at the turns. The Wheel of Fortune brings you chances and sudden changes; Death teaches you to let go of the old to make room for them. Others think you are simply lucky, but your luck lies in not clinging to the old once fate has turned, and not mourning a closed door longer than you need to.

The café you ran for five years closes: the rent has doubled. The first week is hard; you take the tables apart in silence. Then a friend offers to sell you a van for serving breakfasts at festivals, and you argue until midnight about what menu will fit in it. **The point of your meeting is that no closed door becomes a dead end: behind each one you find the next.**

The wheel spins idly when you chase change for the thrill of it. It seems the next turn is bound to carry you to the top, and you drop what had only just begun to bear fruit. Or the reverse: luck turns away, and instead of letting the failure go you spend years blaming fate and each other for it. An ending that has not been lived through stops anything new from starting: the wheel turns, and you stand still.

items.title: The still centre of the wheel

captions.A: Lucky, light and always on the move
captions.B: An even flow amid change

items.meaning: You need each other to keep your balance in luck and in bad luck, however the wheel spins.
text: Your couple rocks more often than most: the Wheel of Fortune brings now a rise, now a fall, now a sudden move, and to friends you seem lucky people who are always changing something. Temperance gives this merry-go-round an axle — a place at the centre of the wheel where it hardly shakes. Your shared skill is to stand in that middle: enjoy luck without getting dizzy and meet bad luck without panic.

One of you gets a big bonus, and the first impulse is to buy a car, fly to the islands, celebrate in style. The other suggests splitting it: a third for joy, a third into reserve, a third for what you have long put off. In the evening you celebrate at your favourite restaurant rather than on the islands, and it seems to you both that the party is no smaller for it. **Luck doesn't turn your heads and bad luck doesn't knock you down: together you hold the axle of the wheel.**

The middle is lost when one keeps the balance alone. They save, smooth things over, calm things down, while the other lives from high to low and does not notice who keeps the peace. Or you are both so afraid of the rocking that you stop accepting fate's turns: you turn down chances just so nothing changes. The wheel goes on turning anyway, only now without you.

items.title: Catching luck by the tail

captions.A: Lucky ones to whom everything comes
captions.B: Prosperity caught at a lucky turn

items.meaning: Together you sense the right moment and turn lucky chances into lasting prosperity.
text: Luck is on your side, and others notice: a job turned up, you sold at the right time, found a flat through an ad that was up for an hour. The Wheel of Fortune brings chances; the Devil gives you the grip not to miss them. Together you know how to want and how to take, and fate brought you together so that luck becomes lasting prosperity rather than a string of wins and losses.

One partner's friend is moving abroad and urgently selling a tiny studio flat in the centre — cheap, but she needs the money within a week. Others would hesitate; you work it all out in one evening, borrow from your parents and sign the contract. You get the keys on Saturday, and on Sunday you are already standing in the empty room with a tape measure, arguing about who your first tenant will be. **A chance doesn't slip through your fingers: you seize it together and make it yours.**

Grip turns into gambling when you start believing your luck will last forever. One lucky risk pushes you to the next, bigger one; loans are taken for a “sure thing”, and a loss makes you want to win it back at once. The wheel turns downwards, and then the reproaches begin: who talked whom into it, who failed to stop it. Luck favours the bold, but it is luck itself that punishes a grip without measure.

items.title: Luck grown from the rubble

captions.A: A couple for whom everything is sudden
captions.B: A new start after a sudden blow

items.meaning: Sharp turns happen to you more often than to others, and in the rubble you find a chance.
text: Everything in your life happens suddenly: moves, finds, losses. The Wheel of Fortune keeps your life spinning, and the Tower sometimes knocks you off your feet without warning, so to others it seems you are now carried up, now thrown down. But your task is something else — not to freeze at the moment of the blow: accept that the old is gone and see together what can be built from the rubble.

Your landlord suddenly sells the flat you rent, and you have a month to move out. Panic, boxes, quarrels. Then the other finds an ad for an old house in the suburbs, let cheaply if the tenants do it up themselves. You agree out of desperation — and on the very first evening, sitting on the porch among the boxes and neglected apple trees, you realise that for the first time in years you can hear silence. **A trouble that falls on you out of nowhere becomes, for the two of you, a door you would otherwise have walked past.**

It is dangerous to get used to expecting the worst. After a couple of blows every turn looks like a new disaster, and you start living on the defensive: no risks, no changes, anything so long as nothing collapses. The other way out is to blame fate and each other: “nothing ever goes right for us”. Bad luck becomes a role you play together, though the wheel turned the other way long ago.

items.title: Make a wish and wait

captions.A: Lucky, open, quick to change their lives
captions.B: A hope that comes true in its own time

items.meaning: Your hope is shared and doesn't go out as the wheel goes down — so your dreams wait for their hour.
text: People often tell you that you were born under a lucky star — and it is almost true. The Wheel of Fortune spins your life, and the Star helps you keep hope while it heads downwards. Your faith is shared: that the dream will come true, that luck will return, that things will work out for the other. And that faith in itself helps you wait for the turn in the right direction.

For five years you dream of a house by the sea, and for five years you save, now a little, now nothing. There were years when the dream seemed silly, but every winter you still scroll through listings and choose where to hang the swing. Then the other gets a job that can be done from anywhere — and that same evening, for the first time, you don't scroll the listings but ring one of them. **Your hope doesn't go out between turns of the wheel, and so the dream waits for its hour.**

Hope becomes waiting for a miracle when faith is all that is left and the steps are gone. “We'll get lucky sometime” — and debts are paid off with new debts, and the dream is put off until a lottery ticket. Or this: the wheel turns down, and one partner's faith irritates the other as naivety. The Star shines for those who walk: keep the dream alive not only in talk but in small steps every month.

items.title: Sensing the turn ahead of time

captions.B: A feel for the turns of fate

items.meaning: Together you sense fate's turns before they happen: your luck listens to instinct.
text: You are lucky, and you know it: change comes often, and more often for the better. The Wheel of Fortune spins your life, and the Moon teaches you to hear it creak in advance — in dreams, in a vague unease, in a sudden “let's not go”. Your shared intuition is stronger than either of yours alone: together you sense when to seize a chance and when to wait it out.

A week before signing a contract one of you dreams that you are lost in an unfamiliar house. In the morning they say: “Let's wait.” The other, usually bold, suddenly agrees. A month later the company you were about to work with goes bust. You don't make a mystery of it, but since then you listen to mornings like that. **Luck comes to you when you heed not only calculation but the quiet inner voice.**

Instinct goes astray when anxiety starts passing itself off as premonition. Every turn looks like an omen of trouble, moods jump with your dreams, and decisions are put off out of fear. Or this: you rely so much on luck and signs that you stop thinking with your heads. Intuition is reliable when a sober eye backs it up: listen to your feelings, but check them against the facts.

items.title: Catching a sunny turn

captions.B: Joy and success that last

items.meaning: Every lucky break becomes a lasting joy for the whole family.
text: Fortune smiles on you: light and decisive, you change your lives and come out ahead. The Wheel of Fortune brings the turns, and the Sun makes sure they don't pass without trace. From luck you build a lasting joy — a home, a family, a business where everyone is warm — instead of burning through it in one season.

One of you wins a small but noticeable sum in the lottery. You buy nothing showy: you pay for a family trip to the sea, where one partner's parents have not been for thirty years. A week of laughter, photos and long dinners on the terrace stays in the family memory longer than any purchase. **Your luck turns into a sun that warms everyone around you, not just the two of you.**

Luck and joy spoil you if you take them for granted. When the wheel turns downwards you are at a loss: there is nothing left to be glad about, and you have little experience of getting through hard times together. Give thanks for the good while it is here, and learn to enjoy small things — then even the wheel's descent will not put out your light.

items.title: What the wheel brought back

captions.B: A return to what matters and a rebirth

items.meaning: The wheel brings you back to what matters and gives you a second birth.
text: Your life is a series of turns, and you are usually lucky in them. The Wheel of Fortune carries you round in circles, and Judgement shows where the circle leads: to a return. To people, places and dreams that seemed lost. You are to recognise these returns and not walk past them: each is a chance to be born again.

Your first shared venture, a small publishing house, went under many years ago, and for a long time you could not talk about it. Then life carried you through different jobs and cities. Suddenly a former author rings and offers to reissue that very series of books — this time with a serious partner. You agree and do everything differently, remembering past mistakes. **The wheel gives back what you thought was lost, and you meet it as different people.**

Returns can be hard. The past comes with old grievances, and you argue again about who was to blame back then. Or the wheel brings not what you wanted but what you need, and that disappoints. Take a second chance as something new, not a continuation of the old: Judgement wakes you so that you live on, not so that you look back.

items.title: A circle brought to a close

captions.A: Lucky, flexible, quick to change their lives
captions.B: Wholeness and a sense of a journey complete

items.meaning: Every circle is brought to its end, and out of the turns you have lived through you build a shared world.
text: Turns come to you often, and you are lucky in them: a new job, a new city, a new passion. The Wheel of Fortune turns, and the World reminds you that every circle has its completion. Together you are to see what you start through to the end and assemble the turns you have lived into a whole picture — a life where everything is connected and everything is in its place.

Going through ten years of photographs, you lay them out by year on the floor and suddenly see a pattern: every move, every change of job led to what you have now. Nothing was in vain. You stick the photos together into a big map of your life and hang it in the hallway. **Every turn of the wheel turns out to be part of a whole, and from these turns the two of you assemble your world.**

The wheel can carry you away so much that the circles never close. You start new things without finishing old ones, and life turns into a scattering of things begun. The other trap: luck turns away, and the sense of wholeness falls apart along with it. Complete each turn together: take stock, give thanks, and only then turn onwards.

items.title: Trusting the wind

captions.B: Carefreeness and trust in life

items.meaning: Life has your trust, and you meet change with a smile.
text: The Wheel of Fortune often turns your way, and change goes well for you. And the Fool suggests you stop watching it anxiously and simply trust it. Not planning every turn, not fearing the downswing, but meeting life with a smile, like wind in your face. Luck becomes light when you stop trying to control it.

Your train is cancelled, and you are stuck in a small town for a day. Instead of fuming you go for a walk, find a tiny flea market and buy an old camera for next to nothing. In the evening you photograph the sunset over the river with it, without knowing whether it even works, and the stallholder invites you home for dinner. **You trust the wind, and it carries you somewhere better.**

Trusting the wind easily slides into frivolity. You trust the wheel so much that you stop preparing for the downswing, and failure catches you with no reserve. Trust life, but keep an umbrella handy: the Fool enjoys walking in the rain more when he knows where his dry clothes are.

items.title: Strength that accepts weakness

captions.B: Accepting weaknesses, and quiet wisdom

items.meaning: Strong and used to winning, you protect each other's weakness rather than fixing it.
text: Winning is a habit for you: strong, forceful, with character. Strength holds the fire, and the High Priestess teaches something else — acceptance. Your partner's weak sides, dark corners, fears and insecurity don't need to be defeated; they need to be understood. You are meant to learn a quiet wisdom in which strength doesn't crush but protects.

One of you never showed weakness and expected the same of the other, and for years joked in front of friends about the other's fear of driving on the motorway. At yet another get-together someone starts retelling how the other failed their driving test for the third time — and the first, who used to tell this story themselves, cuts them off: “Enough. It's not funny.” At home they don't say “pull yourself together” but ask: “Shall I help, or just not hurry you?” **Your strength learns to accept weakness, and beside each other it becomes safe.**

Strong people find it hard to show vulnerability. One opens up, the other answers out of habit with advice or reproach, and the door closes again. The reverse imbalance is possible too: softness becomes a game of “I'm weak, pity me”. Accept weaknesses but don't exploit them: the Priestess sees the truth in both strength and weakness.

items.title: A strength that nurtures

captions.B: Care, plenty and a family you raise

items.meaning: You direct your strength not into fighting but into raising a family and abundance.
text: There is a lot of strength in you: forceful and with character, you are used to breaking through walls. Strength can fight or it can nurture, and the Empress chooses the second. Care, comfort, family, a garden, a shared venture take strength too, only of another kind — patient, careful, generous. You are meant to direct your power into making everything around you bloom.

Your energy used to go into competing and arguing about who was in charge. One summer you take on the neglected shared courtyard: you grub out stumps, mend benches, plant lilac, and the neighbours' children bring you seedlings in little buckets. By autumn you are both surprised at how long it has been since you quarrelled: your strength has found something to work on. **Your strength nurtures rather than fights, and things start to bloom around you.**

Strength in caring can turn into control. One nurtures, but by their own rules, and loved ones suffocate under the fussing. Sometimes the trouble is different: each wants to be head gardener, and the argument moves to the vegetable beds. Grow things together and let others grow: the Empress cares, but she doesn't smother.

items.title: Two leaders, one fortress

captions.B: Clear roles and a shared, solid footing

items.meaning: Two leaders, you divide roles and build a shared fortress instead of fighting for the throne.
text: You are both used to leading: strong, commanding, energetic. Strength strives for first place, and the Emperor offers a different solution — order. Clear roles, divided areas of responsibility, rules that suit you both. Instead of a fight for the throne — a shared fortress, where each has a tower of their own.

Once every decision turned into an argument: who is in charge, whose word is final. In the end you divide everything into zones: one is responsible for money and the home, the other for holidays, children and relations with the family. In their own zone each decides alone; on shared questions, only together. The arguments halve, and the respect doubles. **Your strength finds its order, and two leaders stop fighting over one fortress.**

Order between strong people is fragile. One starts straying into the other's zone, and the old struggle flares up again. There is another risk too: roles harden, and someone feels locked in their tower. Review the zones once a year and thank each other for each holding your part.

items.title: A strength that teaches

captions.B: Shared convictions and wise authority

items.meaning: You know how to lead — not by pressure but by example and shared belief.
text: You are born leaders, and people follow you. But every strength faces a question: lead where? The Hierophant answers: towards what you believe in together. He needs not pressure but an authority freely recognised. You are to find shared convictions and lead by example — so that people follow you not out of fear but out of respect.

Each of you coaches a different sport, and for a long time you argued over whose method was right. Tired of arguing, you write down what you both believe: no humiliation, respect for the weaker, winning is not the main thing. You pin the sheet up in the changing room, and at the very first session a boy used to laughing at the weak reads it aloud and blushes. **Your strength becomes a teaching when you lead not by volume but by shared values.**

Strength armed with convictions can become fanaticism. “We know what's right” — and you start pressing those who think differently, each other included. Or each keeps to their own truth and demands the other accept it. The Hierophant's authority rests on free agreement; if it has to be forced, it is no longer teaching but power.

items.title: The strong need tenderness too

captions.A: Strong, vivid and used to leading
captions.B: Tenderness and decisions made together

items.meaning: Two strong people, you choose not to lead but to decide together and speak openly of love.
text: Decisive people can be spotted from afar, and so can you: energetic, with character, used to leading. The Lovers translate this strength into another language — the language of tenderness and equal choice. Here there is no need to win or prove anything; it is enough to say “I want to be with you” and ask “do you?”. Your union is to become a place where the strong allow themselves to be soft.

You have been used to deciding for everyone since your youth — at work, in the family, among friends. At home this first meant arguments over every trifle. Tired of arguing, you agree: important decisions only together, and only after each says what they themselves want rather than what is right. It turns out you want the same thing far more often than you argued. **Your love is a place where two strong people don't need to win.**

Strength easily crushes tenderness. One gets used to deciding, the other to giving way, and the choice stops being shared. Or passion turns into a test of who loves whom more, and jealousy grows from pride. It is hard for a strong person to say “it hurts” or “I'm scared”, but these are the very words that keep your love alive.

items.title: Strength given a direction

captions.B: A shared course and wins taken together

items.meaning: Two strengths in one chariot, you channel the energy of two into a single goal.
text: There is a lot of strength in you, and people feel it: energetic, with character, used to overcoming things. The Chariot gives this strength what it most lacks — direction. Strength without a course is squandered on arguments and outbursts; with a course it becomes victory. Choose a shared goal — and put all your energy into it.

Your energy once went into endless arguments: about the renovation, holidays, relatives. You decide to open a swimming school for children together — one has coaching experience, the other business sense. The first lesson is held in one rented lane with six little ones, and now you argue only about who claps louder when someone swims without a float for the first time. **Your strength is finally heading one way, and what once went into arguments becomes victories.**

Two strengths in one chariot fight for the wheel. Who leads, whose strategy, who is in charge — and instead of a shared course a struggle begins. Or you get so carried away by the goal that you stop noticing each other and your own tiredness. Divide roles clearly: one is responsible for direction, the other for pace — and swap when you tire.

items.title: Strength on honest scales

captions.B: Equality between two strong people

items.meaning: Two strong people can only be together as equals — and that is the union you are building.
text: You are a vivid, strong couple, and people quickly understand who sets the tone here. The only question is which of you. Strength tends to lead; Justice demands that you lead in turns and fairly. You are to create a union in which power belongs to neither alone: decisions are weighed, duties shared, and respect does not depend on who is louder.

Once one of you decided the big things and the other everything else, and both thought this normal until the other was worn out. Now you have a table: who runs the budget this quarter, who is responsible for the parents, who for the renovation, and every three months you swap. At first it was clumsy, and then it turned out each could do more than they thought. **In your couple one's strength does not crush the other's: you keep power on honest scales and pass it back and forth.**

The scales tip when strength starts thinking it is justice. “I know better”, “I earn more, so I decide” — and honesty becomes an excuse. The other either resigns themselves and stores up hurt or joins the fight, and every argument becomes a lawsuit. Justice is measured not by who is right but by whether you are both well.

items.title: Strength that went deep

captions.B: The wisdom of silence and self-knowledge

items.meaning: Your strength goes deep and stops needing an audience: you grow a power that comes from within.
text: In public you are loud, energetic, used to being at the centre of things. But the Hermit pulls you the other way — inwards. Strength that has depth needs no proof: it does not have to win every argument or come first in every venture. You are to discover this quiet power — self-knowledge, from which calm and precise decisions are born.

Deciding in a minute and acting in two is your usual style. One of you is offered a big position, and instead of an instant “yes” you take a week for the first time: you drive out of town, stay silent, talk, fall silent again. It turns out the position is needed by pride, not by you, and saying no comes easily. **Your strength grows up in silence: there it stops proving and starts understanding.**

Silence comes hard to strong people. One sits in thought, and the other takes it for weakness and pushes: “just decide”. Or reflection becomes a way to avoid an argument — they withdraw, “I need to think” — and the other is angry at a wall. Agree that silence for you is neither punishment nor escape but part of the decision, and that it has a time limit.

items.title: Giving fate the reins

captions.A: A driven couple, used to deciding everything
captions.B: Trust in life and ease at the turns

items.meaning: Pushing through comes easily; beside each other you learn to let go of control and catch a following wind.
text: You are a couple used to getting results: drive, organisation, everything under control. Strength gives you this backbone, but the Wheel of Fortune comes with a lesson force cannot take: part of life does not yield to effort. Together you are to trust the course of events and let go of what is not in your hands, and then luck starts helping where you used to force your own way.

For three years you stormed one goal — to open a studio in exactly this area, in exactly this building — and everything fell through. At last you decide to let go: let it be as it will be. A month later you are offered premises on the next street, bright, cheaper and with clients already in place. **Your strength truly opens up when you stop fighting the current and let it carry the two of you.**

Control has a tenacious grip. When the wheel turns the wrong way, strong natures push even harder, and stubbornness comes into play: “I'll get there anyway.” Failure feels like a personal defeat, and anger spills onto the person closest. Luck does not like being fought: it goes to those who can nimbly catch a new turn.

items.title: Two lions under one roof

captions.B: A strength that grows from gentleness

items.meaning: Two strong natures, you met to charge each other and learn that real power lies in gentleness.
text: Strength stands both in your image and in what you are to create, so you are hard to ignore: two vivid wills, energy, a habit of leading. People see the drive, but your task goes deeper — to learn the tamer's kind of strength: calm, gentle, the kind a beast obeys without fear. Each of you knows how to push; for the other's sake you learn to give way, and you only grow stronger for it.

One decides to quit smoking, the other to start running in the mornings. Instead of lectures you agree to back each other up: whoever slips is not shamed but taken by the hand for a walk until the urge passes. By the end of the first month the smoker comes out for the morning run too — for company, with no cigarettes in their pocket — and you both know neither would have managed alone. **Two strong natures side by side need not fight: in your couple they charge each other and do more than either could alone.**

Two lions in one cage are a test. If neither admits that today the other leads, every trifle becomes a battle for first place: who decides, who is right, who gave way last time. Demands on each other grow, praise grows scarce, and instead of a strength that is shared you are left with two tense people waiting for a blow. A strength that cannot give way sooner or later breaks what it set out to protect.

items.title: Strength that can give way

captions.A: A couple with drive and a loud voice
captions.B: Patience and help for those who are weaker

items.meaning: Your strength finds its meaning in helping others, and your drive knows when to give way.
text: Wherever you turn up, things start to happen: people see you as energetic, decisive, used to leading. Strength is your shared drive and endurance; the Hanged Man is what that strength is worth spending on. He teaches you to give it to those who can't manage alone, and to let go in time of what persistence can no longer shift. Your couple is about a strength that knows when to push and when to wait humbly.

At weekends the two of you run a free sports club for teenagers from the next block. One puts them through their paces, the other listens to who has fallen out with whom and whose home life is in trouble. There is no pay, but the whole block knows you by name. **That is why you met: so that your strength works not for victory over others but for those who lack it.**

Drive and giving way are easily shared out unequally: one always pushes, the other always yields. The one who yields calls it patience but in fact stores up hurt and waits for the sacrifice to be noticed. The one who pushes sincerely believes all is well — after all, nobody argues. Strength without yielding becomes power, yielding without strength becomes submission, and neither will hold you together.

items.title: Strength to shed a skin

captions.A: A couple with a voice and a firm grip
captions.B: A renewal you have the strength for

items.meaning: A change one person lacks the nerve for is within reach for the two of you — that is why you met.
text: A change one person lacks the nerve for is within reach for the two of you. From outside you are a couple with everything under control: energetic, organised, used to taking charge. The Strength behind this image is not pressure but staying power, a gentle, stubborn hold on the course, and Death gives it work to do. Beside each other you drop what drags you down and hold on to the new until it becomes yours.

One of you decides to leave a profession of fifteen years and go back to study. The first term is hard: less money, less energy, doubts every evening. The other neither persuades nor pities but keeps the rhythm: wakes them for classes, tests them on exam questions, celebrates every topic passed. **Fate brought you together so that the changes in your life have support — a strength that does not break but holds on while the new takes root.**

Strength turns into pressure when one starts renewing the other against their will. “It's high time you changed” — and soon one is reshaping the other's habits, routine and circle of friends. The other resists, and every change becomes a battlefield over who is in charge. A change imposed by force does not take: it is dropped at the first chance, and trust goes with it.

items.title: Fire in a steady lamp

captions.B: A calm strength that does not burn out

items.meaning: There is fire enough in you for four, and you spend it evenly: enough for your work and for love.
text: You both have energy enough for four, and people feel it: you organise, lead and are not afraid of a heavy load. Strength is your shared heat; Temperance is the glass of the lamp, inside which the fire does not devour everything around it but shines steadily. Together you master a calm strength: one that does not snap or burn out but holds for a long time.

You both used to take on everything: work, renovation, relatives, other people's problems. After a particularly hard year you divide things honestly: what matters and what can be let go, who is responsible for what, when you rest. A word unusual for you appears in the house — “no” — and suddenly you have more strength, not less. **Your couple is about how strong people stay strong: spend the fire evenly and keep it going for years.**

Measure comes hard when each is used to being in charge. Strength wants to decide, Temperance asks you to agree, and the argument over who gives way burns hotter than the question itself. Sometimes one damps themselves down for the sake of peace at home and quietly seethes, while the other takes it for agreement. A flame that is constantly turned down one day flares up where nobody expected it.

items.title: Desire, tamed

captions.A: A couple with status and a strong will
captions.B: Great success and a passion you are master of

items.meaning: You want things in a big way and remain masters of your desires, not their servants.
text: To others you seem people who can handle anything: status, drive, a loud voice. The Devil has given you powerful desires — money, standing, each other — and Strength gives what makes those desires safe: the ability to rein them in. Not to crush them but to tame them, like a beast that becomes a friend. That is why you met: to want in a big way and stay masters of your desires.

You both once liked living well on credit. Together you set a goal — a flat of your own in five years, with no loans — and you hold to it: you give up the extras, take on extra projects and greet every payment made as a victory. On the day of the last instalment you throw a party right on the bare floor of your new kitchen. **Together you prove to yourselves that a strong desire can be not a chain but an engine.**

Taming turns into power when it is not the desire but the partner that is being tamed. Strength sees in the other a beast to be held; the Devil whispers that it can be held tighter. One commands the money and decides for both, the other submits or wages a quiet war. The passion remains, only around it there is no longer love but a struggle over who is on the leash.

items.title: Standing firm when all shakes

captions.B: A support that holds through any collapse

items.meaning: Collapses test your strength, and at those moments you hold on to yourselves and to each other.
text: You seem hard to knock off course — and it's true. Strength gives you endurance and self-possession; the Tower, trials where they are needed. Your union was made not for a quiet harbour but to stand firm when what seemed solid collapses, and at that moment to lose neither yourselves nor each other.

One of you learns of being made redundant on a Friday evening, by email. The other does not start by asking how the mortgage will be paid now. They put the kettle on, sit down beside them and say: “We decide nothing today. Tomorrow we'll make a plan.” By morning the plan is ready: three months of reserve, a list of contacts, a new CV. By Saturday evening the first is already joking about an “unscheduled holiday”, and on Monday goes to the first interview. **Collapses don't scatter you but put you back to back: each holds their side until it quietens down.**

Strength fails when you start putting it on. One carries on as if nothing has happened, doesn't cry, doesn't complain, and the other has no idea how to reach them. Low spirits are hidden under a cheerful mask, and irritation breaks out on the one closest. Self-control that allows itself no weakness one day collapses on its own — louder than any Tower.

items.title: Strength that shines for others

captions.A: A couple with a voice, drive and status
captions.B: A talent that becomes an example

items.meaning: You do the work you love at full strength, and your example kindles the talents of those around you.
text: People see and hear you: a strong, visible couple people trust to lead. Strength is your energy and endurance; the Star directs them into creativity and hope. This is not about power but about example: you do what you love at full strength, and others, watching you, dare to do their own thing. It seems that is exactly why you met — to shine not only for yourselves.

Together you run a small theatre studio for adults: one directs the plays, the other teaches people not to fear the stage. Accountants, drivers and pensioners arrive stiff, and the first month goes on getting them to stop apologising for every word. At the show for family, an elderly driver's voice trembles, but he plays it through to the end, and in the audience his grandson stands up. **Your strength shines at its fullest when it kindles other people's talents.**

Light turns into pride when what matters is no longer inspiring but dazzling. One jealously counts who gets more applause, the other demands that their partner live up to their status — in looks, speech, achievement. Inflated expectations press down, and the Star dims under the weight. Support each other as stage partners, not as rivals for the front row.

items.title: Taming the night-time fears

captions.A: Strong, confident, fearless to look at
captions.B: Courage to face your own fears

items.meaning: Fearless to look at, you met to face your fears together and tame them.
text: From outside you seem fearless: energetic, confident, used to taking things on. But the Moon reminds you that everyone has a night they are afraid to look into. Strength here lies not in pretending there is no fear but in reaching out to it, as to a wild animal, and calmly taming it. Your union is a place where you can be afraid aloud and not be ashamed of it.

One of you, strong and loud, has been afraid of the dark in an empty house all their life, and nobody knows. One night when the other is away, they call and simply say: “I'm scared.” The other doesn't laugh. They stay on the line until the first falls asleep, and in the morning they talk about their own fear — of heights — which they had hidden even from themselves. **Your strength grows where you allow each other to be weak.**

Fears break out when they are hidden behind drive. Anxiety turns into aggression, jealousy into control, and instead of the admission “I'm scared” comes “where were you this time?”. Strength bears down on the other's shadows and fails to notice its own. A tamer must not fear the beast, but must not pretend there is no beast either: name your fear, and it will stop steering you from the dark.

items.title: Strength that knows joy

captions.B: Joy, warmth and a happy family

items.meaning: You spend your strength not only on victories but on the warmth of home — that is the point of your meeting.
text: Strength shows in you at once: energetic, responsible, with a voice and a position. The Sun reminds you what that strength is for — for joy. For a home that is fun, children who laugh, celebrations friends gather for. Strength is worth spending not only on achievements but on a happiness that is not measured in victories.

You are both used to being in charge and lived by a schedule of meetings. Your son asks why you never play football with him. That same Saturday you buy a ball, and a month later a whole team of neighbourhood children gathers in your yard, and you, grown-up and important, run about with them until dark. **Your strength becomes light when you spend it on the joy of those around you.**

Strength and the Sun together tend towards rivalry: who is brighter, more successful, more recognised. Another danger: work eats up all your strength, and only crumbs are left for joy, which you make up for with expensive presents instead of time. Put not only goals but celebrations in your plans — and defend them as stubbornly as you defend your work.

items.title: Strength that heard the call

captions.B: A calling and responsibility for your kin

items.meaning: You find work worth spending your strength on and become a pillar for your family.
text: There is no lack of strength in you: decisive and forceful, you are used to breaking through walls. But strength without a goal looks for something to aim at, and sometimes aims the wrong way. Judgement gives it a call: work worth living for, responsibility for family and kin, a second birth for what seemed lost. You are to hear that call and answer it with all your strength.

You have both done well in your professions, but have long felt an emptiness. One partner's father asks for help with his old workshop, which is about to close. You take it on for a month — and stay for years: you pull the business through, hire young people and teach them the trade. **Your strength finally hears the call, and it leads you to work that will outlive you both.**

Strong people hear the call loudly and sometimes impose it on others. “It's our duty” — and relatives, children, partner must fall in line. Another risk: each hears their own call, and you pull in different directions. Test a calling by the joy it brings: if it rests only on duty and force, it is not a call but a chore.

items.title: Strength the size of the world

captions.A: Strong-willed, visible, with energy to spare
captions.B: Wide horizons and a whole shared world

items.meaning: Your goals are the size of the world, and your shared life has room enough for you both.
text: Between you there is strength enough for great things, and you know it. Strength gives drive and endurance, and the World shows where to direct them — towards a wide horizon. Not into fighting each other but into a big shared world: travel, projects, a life without cramped frames. Your power finds peace when it has room to unfold.

Your first mountain trek together breaks off halfway: one of you is exhausted, the other is angry. That evening in the tent you honestly go over what went wrong: you walked too fast, each proving their stamina. You go back by the same route but at a shared pace, and on the pass, for the first time on the trek, you fall silent not from anger but because it is beautiful. **Your strength finds its place when you take on horizons together instead of fighting over who comes first.**

Two strengths in a big world can go off to different summits. Each sets their own goal and doesn't notice the other heading the other way. And rivalry easily carries over into travel too: who has more stamina, who is faster. Choose shared summits and celebrate them together — the world becomes yours when you enter it together.

items.title: The strong may play too

captions.B: Lightness, laughter and the right to be carefree

items.meaning: You let go of tension and laugh at yourselves: your responsibility becomes lighter.
text: Between you there is responsibility enough for a whole town: strong and active, you take everything on. Strength holds the tension, and the Fool suggests letting it go. Strong people may play too, fool around, make mistakes, laugh at themselves. Carefreeness doesn't make you weaker — that is what you discover together.

After a particularly tense month one of you brings home two water pistols. The other stares in bewilderment, and a minute later you are both racing round the flat, soaked and laughing like children. The neighbours bang on the wall, and you laugh even louder. Since then you have a “silly evening” once a week. **Your strength learns to play and only grows stronger for it.**

Lightness may seem irresponsible to strong people. One fools around, the other frowns: “what about the work?” Or the Fool becomes a way of avoiding a serious conversation, and problems pile up. Play when the work is done: strength and lightness don't get in each other's way as long as each knows its time.

items.title: Say it, don't endure it

captions.B: Honest feelings and the words to share them

items.meaning: You speak of feelings directly rather than storing them up as grievances.
text: Patience is your strength: gentle and accommodating, you keep much inside for the sake of peace. The Hanged Man endures, and the High Priestess teaches something else — honesty of feeling. Not storing up hurt, not playing on pity, not hinting, but saying straight out what hurts, what you need, what doesn't suit you. Your gentleness becomes strength when it has a voice.

In choosing holidays, in the renovation, in whose parents to visit, one of you always gave way in silence. The hurt built up and came out as sighs and reproaches. Before yet another holiday they say straight out for the first time: “It matters to me that I decide this time.” The other is surprised — they never knew it mattered. The first chooses the mountains, and the other learns for the first time that all these years their partner went to the sea only for their sake. **Your feelings are finally spoken aloud, and patience stops being a silent sacrifice.**

Words come hard to those used to enduring. One makes up their mind but speaks as if apologising, and isn't heard. And what has built up, if you go on keeping quiet, bursts out as a reproach: “I put up with so much for you”. Speak at once, while the hurt is small: the Priestess teaches words that bring you closer, not words that wound.

items.title: Sacrifice that became a garden

captions.B: Abundance, comfort and care for yourselves

items.meaning: You grow your own garden and allow yourselves prosperity: your self-sacrifice comes into bloom.
text: Everything for others is your motto: self-sacrificing and accommodating, you give yourselves without reserve. The Hanged Man hangs in giving, and the Empress invites you to receive: comfort, prosperity, beauty, care. Your abundance takes nothing from anyone — it fills you so that you have something to share. You are meant to allow yourselves to blossom.

Giving everything to children, parents and friends, for twenty years you lived in a flat where nothing changed. At last the other brings home a roll of new wallpaper and says: “Let's do the place up. For ourselves.” You choose colours you like, buy the armchair you have long dreamed of and put flowers on the windowsill. For the first time in years the home becomes yours. **Your self-sacrifice blossoms into abundance, and you learn to receive as generously as you give.**

Abundance brings guilt to those used to sacrificing. Every purchase for yourselves feels selfish, and conscience spoils the joy. Grow the garden together: the Empress is generous to everyone, including those who tend her.

items.title: Softness that needs walls

captions.B: Firm boundaries and dependable order

items.meaning: You set boundaries and build order: your gentleness gains a footing.
text: There is a great deal of gentleness in you: accommodating and caring, you rarely say no. The Hanged Man gives himself to others, and the Emperor builds walls — not to shut you in but to protect what is dear to you. Boundaries, order, responsibility, a steady income give gentleness a footing. Your kindness grows stronger when it has a home.

Your relatives are used to dropping in unannounced, borrowing money without paying it back and deciding for you how to live. Together you write simple rules: guests by arrangement, loans only against a written note, decisions about your life yours alone. The first month is hard: hurt, phone calls. By spring the relatives get used to it, and for the first time you feel masters of your own life. **Your gentleness gets walls, and kindness no longer turns into a convenience for others.**

Boundaries come hard to those used to giving way. One sets them but gives in at the first pressure, and everything goes back to how it was. Build not only walls but gates: the Emperor protects, but he also lets his own in.

items.title: A faith nurtured by patience

captions.B: Values of your own and a like-minded circle

items.meaning: Your care stops being sacrifice once it rests on a faith and people of your own — you met to find them.
text: You give a lot of strength to others: gentle, caring, patient. The Hanged Man teaches you to see the world differently, and the Hierophant gives that view a footing — values you choose yourselves and a circle of like-minded people. Your care stops being a sacrifice when behind it stands not “that's what you have to do” but what you truly believe in.

For a long time you helped everyone indiscriminately, and sometimes it wore you out. You come across a neighbourhood help club at the local library: people take turns visiting lonely old people, swap things, teach each other. You go to one meeting and stay. Now your help is part of a shared cause; it has meaning and a shoulder beside it. **Your kindness finds its faith and its people, and sacrifice turns into service.**

Values taken up out of despair can become a new cage. You dissolve so completely in the community that you forget yourselves again. Or the group's rules start dictating how you live, and your own view gets lost. The Hierophant is good when the teaching helps you breathe: check whether you are serving people or someone else's rules.

items.title: Stop waiting and choose

captions.B: A bold choice of the heart and open love

items.meaning: Decisions come slowly to you, and you met not to wait for a push from outside but to choose each other yourselves.
text: Decisions come slowly to you: gentle and caring, you take a long time to look, wait, doubt. The Hanged Man hangs in a pause, and the Lovers demand a choice. Not “someday”, not “when everything falls into place”, but now: to choose each other, say so aloud and make the decision together.

You have been together a long time, and everyone around keeps asking when you will finally decide — on a wedding, a home of your own, anything. You don't know yourselves: things seem fine as they are. In the queue for coffee the other suddenly turns and asks straight out: “Do you want to be with me always?” The first says “yes” faster than they can think, and a month later you are already looking for a flat together. **You learn not to wait for a push from outside but to choose each other — boldly and aloud.**

Saying “yes” can be scarier than waiting for years. One makes up their mind, the other still doubts, and the pause turns into hurt: “you're not choosing me”. Worse, when the choice is made out of pity or duty rather than love. Choose with your hearts and honestly: the Lovers need a “yes” said out of desire, not out of tiredness of waiting.

items.title: Off the branch and on the road

captions.B: Resolve, movement and a shared goal

items.meaning: Waiting is your strong suit, and now you set goals and drive towards them without waiting for a push.
text: You know how to wait: patient and calm, you are homebodies who need no extra noise. The Hanged Man spends a long time looking at the world from another angle, and the Chariot says: enough looking, time to go. Resolve is what you are learning together: setting goals and moving towards them, without waiting for life to give you a push.

Your dream of a long trip to a faraway lake has lived with you for five years and keeps being put off: money, work, the weather. Tired of putting it off, the first silently buys tickets for the coming weekend and puts them on the table. The other takes fright at first, then laughs and goes to pack a rucksack. Since then you have a rule: if a dream is put off twice, the third time the tickets are bought without discussion. **Your patience gets wheels, and at last you travel where you have looked for so long.**

Getting going from a standstill is the hardest part of the road. One picks up speed, the other tires and wants to go back to the quiet, and you start irritating each other. Or one partner's resolve turns into pressure: “you're dragging your feet again”. Move at your own pace, but move: the Chariot need not race, it just mustn't stand still.

items.title: An honest measure of care

captions.B: A fair balance and honest boundaries

items.meaning: You share care fairly and do not sacrifice yourselves beyond measure.
text: You are better at giving than taking: accommodating and caring, you often put others above yourselves. The Hanged Man sacrifices, and Justice takes up the scales: how much do you give, how much do you get, is it fair? Together you are to find the measure at which care does not become sacrifice, nor kindness a convenience for others.

One Sunday you add up how many hours a week you spend helping relatives and friends, and at first you laugh, then take fright: nearly thirty. On yourselves and each other — under five. You honestly decide whom you will go on helping and whom you will politely refuse. Refusing feels shameful, but a month later you have free evenings, and with them conversations you have not had for a long time. **You learn to weigh your kindness honestly, and it starts to stretch to yourselves as well.**

Justice can become a ledger of grievances. One starts counting how much they have given the other and presenting the bill: “I've done so much for you.” Weigh not to reproach but to understand: the scales need honesty, not pettiness.

items.title: Finding yourselves in silence

captions.A: Kind, quiet, always ready to help
captions.B: Wisdom, solitude and self-knowledge

items.meaning: You guard your solitude and find wisdom in it, which you then share.
text: Your kindness is known to all: you always listen and help. The Hanged Man gives himself to others, and the Hermit brings you back to yourselves — to silence, to your own thoughts, to questions there was never time to ask. You are to learn solitude: not a selfish kind but a wise one, in which an understanding of what you yourselves want is born.

Your phone never stops: neighbours, relatives, friends, all with requests. You bring in a rule: Thursday evening with no calls, just the two of you, tea and books. At first your consciences nag, then peace comes. Six months later you notice you help others even better than before, because now you have somewhere to draw strength from. **The silence you keep for yourselves becomes a spring from which you give to others.**

To someone used to being needed, solitude feels like selfishness. One feels guilty over every refusal, the other feels abandoned when the first withdraws. And silence can turn into a flight from people, and the kindness that was your strength dries up. Withdraw together, but not from each other: the Hermit needs a light, not a wall.

items.title: When waiting is rewarded

captions.B: Luck and the nerve to seize your chance

items.meaning: You know how to wait, and together you find the nerve to seize your chance in time.
text: You can wait as few others can: patient and gentle, you rush neither people nor events. The Hanged Man hangs long in a pause, and one day the Wheel of Fortune turns and offers a chance. The main thing is not to miss that turn. Waiting is valuable when a step follows it, and the step must be taken in time.

For five years you walk past an old house with bay windows and dream of a flat in it. No ads ever appear there; you don't rush fate, but you know all the neighbours' cats by name. Then suddenly the woman from the third floor stops you at the entrance herself: she is moving to her children's and wants to sell the flat to people who have “long had their eye on the place”. A decision is needed within a week, and you, usually so unhurried, agree in an evening. **Your patience one day meets luck, and you turn out to be ready to step towards it.**

Waiting becomes a habit, and then the chance goes by. The wheel turns, and you have not yet decided whether you have waited long enough. Or one is ready to act while the other hangs in doubt, and the missed opportunity becomes a quiet reproach. Decide in advance what you are waiting for — then you will recognise your chance when it comes.

items.title: Learning to say no

captions.B: The strength to stand up for yourself, gently

items.meaning: There is no shortage of gentleness, and together you learn to say “no” calmly and firmly.
text: Your gentleness is a gift, but sometimes a trap. The Hanged Man makes you accommodating, caring, ready to help anyone who asks, and people take advantage. Strength teaches something else: to mark boundaries calmly and firmly. Not rudely, not with a scene, but the way a tamer holds a lion — gently, yet so that the line cannot be crossed.

For years one partner's boss loaded them with weekend work, and they agreed. The other suggests: “Let's rehearse.” In the evening in the kitchen you act out the conversation: the other plays the boss, the first plays themselves. A week later they turn down a Saturday shift for the first time — calmly, without excuses. The boss is surprised but agrees. **You help each other find a backbone in gentleness and say “no” where once there was a forced “yes”.**

Strength found after long accommodation can overshoot. Whoever put up with things for years starts taking it out on others — the boss, relatives, their partner. Learn strength together and test it for gentleness: it is there to protect, not to punish.

items.title: Two who turned the world over

captions.B: A view of life all your own, and patience

items.meaning: Others think your life is upside down, but you know that this is how it stands on its feet.
text: A double Hanged Man is a rare combination, and it explains a lot. People know you as kind, hospitable people who will always help. And together you create something larger — your own view of life, turned upside down relative to the usual one. What others see as a waste of time — a slow life, caring for someone, a long wait — is full of meaning for you.

You leave the city for a village where you have neither work nor acquaintances, and soon your house becomes a place friends come to in hard times: to stay a week, catch their breath, talk by the stove. You have less money than your former colleagues, but you have never once regretted it. **Others think your life is upside down, but you know that this is how it finally stands on its feet.**

A double Hanged Man can get stuck in suspension. Both give way, both wait, both sacrifice — and neither dares to want something for themselves. Decisions are put off because each is afraid of imposing their will, and years pass waiting for a push from outside. Learn to ask and to take as easily as you give: in a couple of two givers, someone must also know how to receive.

items.title: Let go in order to begin

captions.A: Caring, peaceable, always ready to help
captions.B: A new life after a long wait

items.meaning: Much of your life rests on endurance, and you met to stop enduring out of duty and begin anew.
text: People love you for your kindness: hospitable, never refusing anyone, always ready to help. The Hanged Man is pause and giving; Death is the end of the pause. Much in your life rests on endurance: a job you put up with, obligations that have long been a burden, waiting for things to change by themselves. One day you are to stop hanging and take a step after which something new begins.

For many years you have spent every summer at one partner's parents' country house: digging, mending, listening to complaints that everything is wrong. One Sunday among the vegetable beds you admit to each other that you hate these weekends, and for the first time you tell the parents an honest “no”. A week of hurt and phone calls — and then it turns out the parents had long wanted to sell the plot and couldn't bring themselves to. Everyone is set free. **You need each other to stop waiting, stop enduring and make room for the new.**

Letting go is harder than enduring. You are both used to sacrifice, and giving up old roles feels like betrayal: how can you stop helping, stop waiting? One makes up their mind, the other clings to the old and takes offence. And self-sacrifice may simply change address: the old is gone, and the new is again built on “I'll put up with it”. Death comes to set you free — let it take the habit of suffering too.

items.title: Giving in equal measure

captions.B: A balance between care and self

items.meaning: Your readiness to give finds its measure: you care for each other without forgetting yourselves.
text: People value your gentleness: you are accommodating, caring and always ready to help. The Hanged Man gives himself to others easily, sometimes entirely. Temperance sets a condition — measure: to blend care for your partner with care for yourself in the right proportion. You are learning what comes hardest to generous people: to give in equal measure and to receive without guilt.

For years one of you got up before everyone else, cooked, saw people off and met them, and the other took it for granted, sincerely not noticing. One Saturday morning the first simply doesn't get up: “This morning is mine.” The other is at a loss, then makes breakfast themselves — clumsily, but with pleasure. Since then you take turns, and it turns out the other had long wanted to look after someone; they were just never given room. **Care flows both ways between you, like water between two cups, and neither runs dry.**

An imbalance appears when one gets used to giving and the other to taking. A silent sacrifice stores up resentment, and one day “I've done so much for you” sounds like a verdict. Talk about what you yourselves want: measure is born when both people's wishes are visible.

items.title: Allowing yourselves to want

captions.B: Bold desires and plenty for yourselves

items.meaning: Your kindness gains the courage to want: you wish for yourselves and take your share from life.
text: You are loved for always being ready to help and give way. The Hanged Man makes you a couple who live for others and often forget themselves. The Devil is an unexpected teacher here: he suggests that at last you want something. Passion for each other, money, pleasures, a business of your own — not out of greed, but because you too have a right to them.

You have always given everything away: helped your parents, paid for younger siblings' education, gone without holidays. You sit down to write a list of “what we want” — and for a long time can't begin, because you have lost the habit. The first item comes out funny: a red car. A week later you are already going round car showrooms “just to look” and climbing into every red car like teenagers. **You teach each other to want for yourselves as boldly as you once gave to others.**

Desire that has long been suppressed can break out without measure. One, having allowed themselves for the first time, wants more and more, while the other takes fright and pulls back into familiar modesty. The other trap: passion turns into an attachment in which each sacrifices for the other and demands the same in return. Wanting is allowed, even necessary; just make sure the desire belongs to you, and not you to it.

items.title: Cutting the rope

captions.B: Freedom from roles long outgrown

items.meaning: You met to bring down the roles you got stuck in out of patience — and build a life where you choose for yourselves.
text: You are patient and caring, and people are used to you always helping and always waiting. The Hanged Man can hang for years — in a job you put up with, in a role that has long pinched. The Tower snaps that rope. You are to live through the collapse of the old order and find that beyond it lies freedom, not disaster.

Every New Year the whole family gathers at your place: you cook for twenty, wash up until morning and hear that last year's salad was better. In November the other, having consulted only the first, writes in the family chat: “This year we're going away.” Hurt, phone calls, “how could you”. You see in the New Year in a sleeper compartment on a train heading north, with tangerines and one mug between you, and for the first time in ten years you laugh on New Year's Eve. **You bring down what rested on patience and build in its place a life where you choose for yourselves.**

A collapse after long patience can be too loud. What built up over years bursts out all at once, and along with the false roles goes what was worth keeping. Don't wait for your patience to snap: better to loosen the old a little at a time and out loud than to wait for it to fall on your heads.

items.title: Time to dream for yourselves

captions.B: A dream and hope of your own, not just others'

items.meaning: You are used to shining for others, and now you find your own dream and let yourselves hope for yourselves.
text: You are used to giving: caring, waiting, sacrificing for others. The Hanged Man makes you gentle and patient, but sometimes forgetful of yourselves. The Star reminds you that you have a light too: dreams of your own, talents of your own, desires that have waited a long time. You are to help each other find them and at last allow yourselves to hope not only on others' behalf.

For twenty years one of you has worked at a nursery school and given every evening to other people's children and their own parents. Over dinner the other asks: “And what did you dream of yourself?” The first is silent for a long time and admits: the cello. On Saturday the other brings home a hired instrument, and that evening the would-be cellist sits over the first scale so absorbed that they miss their mother's call. **The star you hid for years behind caring for others at last gets the right to shine.**

A dream of your own can bring guilt. One starts living for themselves, and the other is jealous of this new life or can't dare one of their own. Or the dream is put off again for others' sake: first the children, then the parents, then the grandchildren. Allow yourselves at least a little light now: the Star doesn't wait until everyone is settled.

items.title: A world invented for two

captions.B: A shared inner world and play of imagination

items.meaning: Together you create a world of your own that only you understand: your gentleness befriends imagination.
text: A little otherworldly — that is what people say about you, and you like it. The Hanged Man looks at life from an unusual angle, and the Moon fills that view with imagination. Together you are meant to create a world of your own: games, pet words, invented traditions, fantasies only you understand. In this world you rest from the rules and understand each other without words.

You have an invented country with its own map, inhabitants and history that you have been making up in the evenings for many years. Sometimes you write each other letters in the name of its inhabitants. You don't tell friends about it — they would laugh. But when things are hard, one writes on a napkin: “It's raining in the Northern Province today”, and the other understands everything. **Your invented world is the most real of refuges, and it belongs to the two of you alone.**

An imaginary world can become an escape. When reality is hard, you retreat into fantasy and put off what needs deciding here and now. The other trap: one lives in dreams while the other has to hold up daily life alone. Come back from your country bearing gifts: let fantasy help you live rather than replace living.

items.title: Allowing yourselves joy

captions.B: Joy, warmth and a success of your own

items.meaning: You know how to endure and give, and now you allow yourselves joy — for no reason and without guilt.
text: Your patience would do for ten: you care, give way, wait, often live for others. The Hanged Man knows the price of sacrifice, and the Sun reminds you of what you may have forgotten — joy. Happiness is something you can allow yourselves: celebrations for no reason, success without guilt, rest without excuses.

On your first holiday in five years you go to the sea and on the very first day catch yourselves phoning your mother and your boss. On the second day you lock your phones in the safe. By the end of the week you are laughing and tanned, and one admits: “I can't remember when I last felt this good.” At home you stick a photo from that beach on the fridge — as a reminder. **You teach each other to rejoice, and the light at last reaches those who always shone for others.**

Joy can bring guilt. “We're on holiday and Mum is on her own”, “we're happy while our friends are in trouble” — and the celebration breaks off mid-sentence. Sometimes the trouble is different: one has learned to rejoice while the other clings to the role of martyr and resents the other's happiness. Joy is not betrayal: those who glow have more strength to help others.

items.title: Waking after a long pause

captions.B: Awakening, a call and a new life

items.meaning: After a long pause you wake up and together begin to live anew.
text: You can wait for a long time: patient and gentle, you live for years in a pause, not rushing life. The Hanged Man hangs, looking at the world upside down, and Judgement sounds the call to wake. One day the call will come — work, a place, a decision — and you are to answer it, climb down from the branch and begin to live as you have long wanted to.

For ten years you put off moving to the countryside you dreamed of: work, parents, “later”. One spring the other wakes up and says: “Today I realised that ‘later’ might never come.” By evening you are ringing the owners of the house by the river you spotted three years ago, and to your surprise it is still for sale. **Your patience one day hears the call, and you wake up in the life you put off for so long.**

A pause drags you in. The call sounds, and you find yet another reason to wait. Another danger: one wakes while the other is still asleep, and the new life begins without them. If you both hear the call, don't put it off: Judgement doesn't sound forever.

items.title: From waiting to the whole world

captions.B: The wide world and a full life

items.meaning: From long waiting you step out into the world and live a full life.
text: Home and caring for those close to you are your familiar world: patient and gentle, you live for others and rarely venture beyond the country cottage. The Hanged Man looks at the world from his corner, and the World flings the horizon open. Travel, new people, another life are waiting for you, and fullness comes when you allow yourselves to step over the threshold.

All your lives you dreamed of seeing the ocean but always put it off: parents, children, work. When the youngest leaves to study, the other brings home two tickets: “Now or never.” You stand on the shore holding hands, both in tears. Since then every year brings a new place, and a life that seemed quiet becomes enormous. **Long waiting ends in a whole world, and it turns out to be just your size.**

Open space is frightening at first. One is eager to travel, the other worries how those close to them will manage without them. And stepping out into the world can bring guilt: “we're enjoying ourselves while Mum is on her own”. Allow yourselves space: caring for others doesn't cancel the right to a life of your own.

items.title: Breaking loose

captions.B: Freedom, lightness and the nerve to leap

items.meaning: You live for others and are learning to break loose, remembering how light life can be.
text: You know how to wait and to care: patient and gentle, you are homebodies who live for others. The Hanged Man is frozen in a pause, and the Fool leaps: freedom, lightness, travel, new beginnings — everything you have long put off for others' sake. One day you will break loose and find that the world doesn't collapse without your care.

All your lives you have looked after parents, nephews and nieces, friends, and never once gone on holiday as two. In September, when at last everyone is settled, the other buys two tickets for a week in the mountains — without warning. The first takes fright at first, then laughs all the way to the airport. It is the best week in many years. **You allow yourselves to break loose and remember how light life can be.**

Freedom brings guilt to those used to caring. “How will they manage without us?” — and the leap is put off again. Or one breaks loose while the other stays out of duty and feels hurt. Free yourselves a little at a time: the Fool doesn't ask you to drop everything — one free day is enough for him.

items.title: Not parting in silence

captions.A: Changing their lives easily, saying little
captions.B: An inner footing and accepting the dark

items.meaning: You close chapters easily, and you met so as not to carry their shadows alone and to share what is hard.
text: From outside you change your lives easily: a new job, a new city, without complaint or long explanations. What goes on inside nobody knows — sometimes not even the other. Death makes you a couple who can close chapters, and the High Priestess asks you not to close them in silence: to accept each other's dark sides, talk about what is hard, find a footing to return to after any fall. Closeness grows deeper when it has no forbidden rooms.

Sometimes one of you turns quiet and closed for no visible reason, and the other long took it personally. At last they simply ask: “What happens to you on days like this?” After a long silence the first explains that every change you are praised for as brave costs them more than it seems: they can't say goodbye, so they do it silently, alone. You talk until morning. Now, when it comes over them, the first says one word — “shadow” — and the other simply sits down beside them. **You accept each other's shadows, and the past stops being a locked room.**

Shadows are easily shifted onto the one beside you: longing for a closed chapter comes out as irritation with the person in the new one, who pays for what isn't their fault. Or one opens up and the other, not knowing what to do with someone else's pain, pulls away. Accept the dark gently: the Priestess keeps secrets but doesn't let them run the present.

items.title: Spring on cleared ground

captions.A: Beside you, people believe in a new spring
captions.B: New growth, warmth and plenty

items.meaning: You let go of the outworn easily, and you met to grow a home, a garden and prosperity on the cleared ground.
text: From outside you are a couple who know how to end things without drama: you let go of the outworn, and something is already growing in the space it leaves. Death is your winter: it clears away the superfluous. The Empress brings spring — growth, warmth, abundance. You are meant to grow things on cleared ground: a home, a garden, prosperity, shared ventures. Land cleared of the old yields more generously.

You sell your cramped city flat and rent an old house with an overgrown plot for a year. The first month goes on hauling away other people's junk: rusty buckets, rotten boards, forty jars without lids. In spring the other plants seedlings, then blackcurrants along the fence, and by August the neighbours are coming to you for courgettes and asking how you managed it all. **Your winter ends, and everything you plant together begins to bloom.**

Growing can be more frightening than letting go. To those used to parting easily, every new shoot seems vulnerable, and you are slow to rejoice in it.
