There is one locked room fewer between you. **Your secrets collapse, but in their place grows a trust that has nothing left to fear.**

The collapse of secrets can wound more than the secrets themselves. The truth is used as a weapon, and what came out as a reason for revenge. Or after one wreck each starts to suspect there are other secrets, and trust does not return. Reveal your secrets yourselves, one at a time and in good time: that is better than waiting for life to bring them crashing down.

items.title: Telling a dream from a mirage

captions.B: A clear hope and the courage to create

items.meaning: Dreaming till morning is easy for you; together you tell a dream from a mirage and make it into a road.
text: Between you there is imagination enough for a whole workshop of storytellers: night-time talks, fantasies, dreams you want to write down. The Moon weaves these worlds, but in her light it is easy to mistake a mirage for a star. The Star gives a different light — a clear one you can walk by. Together you learn to tell which dream is yours and calls you to act, and which only leads you into fog.

At night on the balcony one tells, for the umpteenth time, of the house on an island where you will live “someday”. The other listens and suddenly asks: “And what part of that could we do this year?” A pause. Then you laugh and start listing: learn the language, go on a scouting trip, start saving. For the first time in years the dream grows a list. **Your imagination gains a guiding star, and fantasy turns into a road.**

Fog is dangerous when you live in it instead of living. Dreams become a refuge from what is hard, and talk about the future replaces steps towards it. Or one believes in castles in the air while the other tires of being the only one with feet on the ground. Test a dream with a simple question — what can be done tomorrow? — and the one that holds up will turn out to be real.

items.title: Two shores of one night

captions.A: A secretive couple wrapped in legends
captions.B: A deep intuitive bond and trust

items.meaning: You understand each other without words, and in your night there is calm, not fear.
text: The Moon is doubled in your chart, and it can be felt at once: you are a secretive, mysterious couple about whom legends circulate. Between you is a bond that is hard to explain: guessing thoughts, seeing similar dreams, knowing what has happened before it is said. You turn this bond into support: you trust each other so deeply that in your night there is calm rather than fear.

One wakes from a bad dream and before they can say anything the other, eyes still closed, whispers: “It's just a dream, I'm here.” In the morning it turns out they dreamed almost the same thing. You have long since stopped being surprised by such coincidences and simply hold hands when it is dark outside. **Your closeness lives in the depths daylight never reaches, and there you are lighthouses for each other.**

Double Moon easily frightens itself. One's guesses feed the other's, and a small anxiety grows into great suspicion. Secrets that once drew you together begin to divide you. Check night-time fears in the morning, in daylight, and talk about them aloud: the Moon is strong as long as there is trust in its light.

items.title: From night into a sunny morning

captions.B: Clarity, openness and the joy of living

items.meaning: From night-time anxieties you come out into morning: into clarity, an open home and joy spoken aloud.
text: Night is familiar to you: a secretive couple with secrets, anxieties and fears that come uninvited. The Moon keeps you in twilight, and the Sun promises morning — clear, warm, without shadows. Your path leads from suspicion to trust, from anxiety to joy, from closedness to an open home where you are not afraid to invite friends.

For years one of you has “not celebrated” their birthday: switching off the phone and hiding at home. This year, for the first time, they agree to invite people — just ten, to a small café. In the morning they can't eat for fear, and in the evening they stand in the middle of the room in a paper crown, laughing. On the way home you are both silent, but it is quite a different silence — a bright one. **You come out of the moonlit night into a sunny morning and find that the light suits you very well.**

After a long twilight the light hurts the eyes. Sudden openness turns into anxiety: “why did we tell everyone everything”. Or one steps into the sun while the other stays in the shade and feels abandoned. Come out into the light gradually and together: morning doesn't arrive in a single minute.

items.title: Wake up and forgive

captions.B: Awakening, truth and forgiveness

items.meaning: Secrets are brought into the light and forgiven: your awakening comes after a long time of things left unsaid.
text: There is much left unsaid between you: secretive and mysterious, you don't tell each other or yourselves everything. The Moon keeps you half asleep, and Judgement wakes you. When what was hidden comes out — old grievances, unspoken desires, the truth about yourselves — you are not only to hear it but to forgive. Your couple is about an awakening after which it is easier to breathe.

For many years one of you carried a grievance against the other — over words said early in the relationship and long forgotten by the other. On a walk they finally speak of it. The other is shaken: they never knew. They are silent for a long time, then sincerely ask forgiveness. A hurt carried for years leaves in a single evening. **You wake each other from old dreams and forgive, and it grows light.**

Awakening can be painful. A truth revealed wounds, and forgiveness doesn't come at once. And if only one reveals their secret while the other keeps theirs, trust isn't restored. Tell the truth gradually and be ready to wait: Judgement wakes, but forgiveness ripens in its own time.

items.title: From a narrow shade to the world

captions.A: Secretive, anxious, living in their own bubble
captions.B: Openness, space and wholeness

items.meaning: From your little world you step out into the wide open one and find more light there.
text: Your little world is cramped and dim: secretive and anxious, you keep to the shadows and let few people in. The Moon hides, and the World flings the horizon open — new places, people, views beside which your fears suddenly turn out to be small. You are meant to step out of your shadow and discover that the wide world is not hostile: it has been waiting for you.

One of you has always been afraid of flying, and you spent all your holidays within an hour's drive of home. The other quietly suggests: let's try it together — and holds their hand the whole flight. A week later you stand on the shore of a warm sea, and the first laughs at their fear. Since then you have discovered seven countries. **From a narrow shade you step into the wide world and find it brighter and roomier there.**

The open world can frighten you anew. After the first success anxiety returns: “what if something happens out there, so far away”. And if only one goes out into the world while the other stays in their shade, distance grows between you. Go out into the world in small steps and together: breadth comes gradually.

items.title: Letting fears go on the wind

captions.B: Lightness, laughter and fearless trust

items.meaning: You imagine the worst easily, and together you learn to laugh at your night-time monsters.
text: Anxieties are never far away: sensitive and secretive, you often imagine the worst. The Moon draws shadows, and the Fool laughs at them. Not everything that frightens you in the dark exists, and many fears crumble at a single joke. You are meant to learn lightness: to trust life, let go of control and laugh at your own night-time monsters.

Before every trip one of you draws up a list of what could go wrong — three pages long. The other suggests a game: for every fear on the list you invent the most absurd outcome. “What if we miss the train?” — “We'll live at the station and open a coffee shop there.” By the end of the evening you are roaring with laughter, and the list goes into the bin. **You laugh at your fears, and they lose their power over you.**

Lightness can become a mask. One jokes so as not to show anxiety, and the real fear goes unspoken. The other trap: one partner's carefreeness irritates the other: “you don't care”. Laugh together, but also talk seriously: the Fool chases away shadows when he knows where they come from.

items.title: A sun that can be quiet

captions.B: Quiet understanding, gentleness to weakness

items.meaning: You accept each other's weaknesses and understand without words: your demands soften.
text: You know how to dazzle: vivid and successful, you demand a lot of yourselves and each other. The Sun lights up everything, shortcomings included, and the High Priestess teaches a gentler view: to accept your partner's weaknesses, ease demands, understand without words when they are struggling. Your sun becomes warm when it knows how to be quiet.

One of you has long been used to the other succeeding at everything — and doesn't notice them running out of breath. The other says nothing: ashamed to admit weakness. Only when they happen to see them sitting motionless in the car outside the house, eyes closed, does the first understand. That evening they ask nothing — they simply cancel all the weekend plans and take the other out of town. **Your light learns quiet, and in it you notice what the glitter used to hide.**

Demands are hard to let go of for those used to success. Gentleness seems weakness, acceptance indifference to results. Sometimes one eases their demands and the other hears disappointment in it: “you don't believe in me any more”. Talk about what you feel, not only about what you have achieved: the Priestess hears what the Sun misses.

items.title: Sun over a full house

captions.B: A big family, plenty and comfort

items.meaning: You grow family and abundance in a way that keeps everyone warm.
text: Your warmth is enough for everyone: successful and hospitable, you know how to enjoy and give joy. The Sun shines, and the Empress gives that light soil: a home, a garden, a family, an abundance that grows and bears fruit. Your success finds its meaning when it turns into a full house where loved ones gather.

For a long time your success lived in restaurants and holidays, while at home there was only a fridge with yoghurts. This year for the first time you lay the New Year table for the whole family yourselves: you roast a goose from grandmother's notebook, argue about salads, chop until three in the morning. The goose comes out dry, but the table is so loud and warm that no one notices, and the nephews and nieces demand a repeat next year. **The sun shines over your full house, and everything you love grows in it.**

A full house takes strength. You give so much to guests, children and the household that you have no time to rest yourselves. Or else: one goes off into work while the other carries the home, and the sun shines on only one. Share the cares equally: a garden blooms when both gardeners tend it.

items.title: Sunlight within sturdy walls

captions.B: A solid base that keeps success

items.meaning: Solid order is what lets your sun shine for a long time.
text: Success comes to you: vivid and generous, you earn easily and spend easily. The Sun shines brightly, but not forever, and the Emperor builds sturdy walls for it: a system, reserves, clear roles, plans for years. You are meant to turn today's success into a lasting well-being that will outlast any weather.

Your first big contract brings in more money than you have ever seen. The first impulse is to spend it all on a party. Instead you divide the money into three baskets — living, reserve, future — and celebrate more modestly. You still celebrate — in a small restaurant where they know you, with a toast “to the third basket”. **Within sturdy walls your sun doesn't go out, even in bad weather.**

Walls can shade the sun. Order becomes strict, and the joy of success drowns in reports and plans. The other trap: one is generous while the other controls everything, and celebrations turn into arguments about the budget. Leave room for joy in your plan: the Emperor builds so that the Sun has somewhere to shine.

items.title: Sunny traditions

captions.B: Family traditions and shared values

items.meaning: Joy turns into customs in your home, and its warmth is passed on.
text: Your doors are always open: vivid and hospitable, you can make a celebration out of nothing. The Sun gives joy, and the Hierophant gives it form — traditions, values, a way of life. Your warmth becomes lasting when it turns into customs that children and grandchildren remember, not just into cheerful evenings.

Every New Year the whole family writes letters to themselves a year ahead, and then solemnly reads last year's. Every summer — a trip to the same place by a lake, where the youngest already know every path. Every anniversary — dinner with those who were at your wedding. Friends have long known: on your anniversary there's no point inviting you anywhere, you're busy. **Your joy becomes tradition, and the warmth of your home will outlast the years.**

Traditions can become a chore. The party you throw year after year turns into work, and the joy goes. Or your way of life becomes a yardstick for others: “we do it right, you don't”. Let traditions stay alive: change them when they stop giving joy.

items.title: Love amid success

captions.B: Tenderness and time just for two

items.meaning: Successes are many, but amid work and victories you don't lose each other.
text: Work, friends, projects, travel — almost everything works out for you. The Sun shines on your successes, and the Lovers remind you that in this light it is easy to lose the main thing — each other. Tenderness, dates, conversations alone should not be put off until the holiday. Your success is valuable when there is love behind it, not only achievement.

From morning till night — work, and your conversations have long come down to schedules. In the middle of a working day the other sends the first a message: “Date. Tonight. Eight o'clock. No phones.” The first cancels a meeting. That evening you sit in a small café you went to long ago and talk about everything except work. **Your success becomes warm when there is still room beside it for love.**

The Sun can eclipse tenderness. One partner's success becomes more important than the other's feelings, and love starts being measured in presents rather than attention. Or you compete over who has achieved more and forget you are on the same team. Put dates in the calendar on a par with meetings: the Lovers need time, not just sun.

items.title: The sun's victory chariot

captions.A: Successful, warm, always on the rise
captions.B: New goals and wins you drive to together

items.meaning: Your success never stands still: you turn every summit into a springboard and drive on together.
text: Success is familiar to you: warm and vivid, you are used to things working out. The Sun shines, and the Chariot doesn't let that light stagnate: new goals, new routes, new victories. You turn every success into a springboard for the next — and drive on together, in one harness.

You have only just opened your second shop and celebrated it, and the next morning one is already drawing a map: where the third will be. The other laughs — “let me at least get some sleep” — but a week later they find premises themselves and are the first to sign the lease, declaring that this time they choose the sign. **Your success never stands still: the sun's chariot carries you from one victory to the next.**

A race of victories can burn out the joy. Every success is at once devalued by the next goal, and you stop noticing how good things already are. Or one races ahead while the other wants to stop and live. Celebrate every summit as if it were the last: the chariot drives on, but the joy is here.

items.title: Glory shared equally

captions.A: Successful, vivid and in the public eye
captions.B: Fair credit for what both contribute

items.meaning: Recognition is shared equally and well-being built honestly: your success is fair to you both.
text: Success loves you, and it shows: vivid and successful, you are in the public eye. The Sun lights up victories but does not always share the light fairly: one ends up in the centre, the other in the shade. Justice takes up the scales. You are to see each one's contribution, share recognition equally and build success you can be proud of without reservations.

At an awards ceremony for your joint company the host names only one of you — the one who gives interviews more often. The other smiles, but that evening says nothing. Next day the first rings the organisers and asks them to correct it: “This is our joint work.” Since then you go on stage together every time. **Your sun shines brighter when its light falls fairly on you both.**

Success is easy to appropriate. The brighter one starts to think the victories theirs, while the other stores up hurt and compares. And fairness can turn into a petty tally of merits, and the joy of a shared victory drowns in arguments. Thank each other publicly and often: it is the most honest currency in your couple.

items.title: A quiet hour for a bright couple

captions.A: Vivid, sociable, always at the centre
captions.B: Depth and quiet for the two of you

items.meaning: Even in a noisy life you find quiet to understand what matters to you.
text: Guests, friends, work, celebrations: your home is always full. The Sun draws people, and you are rarely alone together. The Hermit quietly closes the door: it is time to be with yourselves and each other, with no audience. In that quiet you learn what cannot be heard in the noise: what you really want, where you are going, who you are without your roles.

Saturday again, guests due again, and suddenly one of you says: “Let's cancel. Let's just be.” You switch off your phones, make soup and talk all evening to old records — as you have not talked since your first year. Towards the end the other admits they have long been tired of the work everyone admires. **You need quiet so that your light comes from within, not just from the people around you.**

Being alone together in quiet is sometimes scarier than going to a noisy party: what if a hard conversation comes up? And you fill your evenings with guests again. And if one withdraws, the other may take it for cooling and feel hurt. Guard quiet hours like a celebration: the Sun too needs an evening in order to rise in the morning.

items.title: Grateful for every turn

captions.B: Gratitude and lightness at every turn

items.meaning: Each turn of the wheel is met with gratitude, and you don't cling to the top.
text: Success comes to you, and you share its warmth generously. The Sun shines brightly on you, but the Wheel of Fortune reminds you that the top is only one point on the circle. Your union is about gratitude for every turn: enjoying the climb without pride, accepting the descent without despair, and sharing luck while you have it.

In your best year, when things are going well, you start a tradition: every month you give a small part of what you earn to those who are down right now — an animal shelter, acquaintances, a lonely neighbour. When a couple of years later the wheel turns and your own difficulties begin, help comes unexpectedly — from those very acquaintances and that neighbour. **You share your sun generously, and the wheel brings it back to you at every new turn.**

The Sun does not like sunsets. When luck goes, successful people find the descent hard: they are ashamed, they hide it, they blame each other. Others get so used to the top that they stop valuing it and demand more and more from life. Give thanks on good days and hard ones alike: the wheel turns for everyone, but it shines on those who remember that it is round.

items.title: Energy for two

captions.A: Vivid, warm and full of life
captions.B: Shared strength and a zest for life

items.meaning: You charge each other up — for a six o'clock start, a marathon, a new project — and that lights up others.
text: You are bursting with energy, and people warm themselves beside you: a vivid, warm, life-loving couple. The Sun gives you light; Strength turns that light into action: stamina, persistence, zest. Together you can charge each other up — for a six o'clock start, a marathon, a new project, something neither could manage alone.

You start running in the mornings as a joke, and a month later two neighbours tag along in the park, and then a pensioner with walking poles. Now you have a run on Saturdays and a shared breakfast on Sundays with everyone who ran, and a fifty-year-old beginner runs five kilometres for the first time in his life. **Your strength shines on others: watching you, people remember that they have energy too.**

The Sun and Strength together can overheat. One is used to leading, and so is the other, and zest turns into rivalry: who is stronger, more successful, right. Or you can charge each other up so much that you stop noticing tiredness and drive each other beyond your limits. Rest as keenly as you work, and measure yourselves not against each other but against your former selves.

items.title: A sun that shines into shade

captions.A: Successful, warm and generous with joy
captions.B: Compassion for those in the dark

items.meaning: You direct your luck to where it is lacking, and help as an equal, not from above.
text: Much goes well for you, and people are drawn to your warmth: a successful, hospitable, joyful couple. The Sun is responsible for your light; the Hanged Man, for the ability to stop and see the world through the eyes of someone who has been unlucky. Together you learn not only to enjoy your success but to share it: time, money, your home, attention.

After a good year you decide not to change your car but to pay for a niece's studies, as her parents are struggling. She comes to stay at weekends, shy at first, then tells you everything. She passes her first exams with good marks and calls you before her mum — and you both pretend you are not crying. **Your luck shines beyond your own home: you share it with those for whom it is dark right now.**

The Sun can scorch even the person being helped. Generosity turns into patronage — “after all we've done for you” — and gratitude begins to be demanded. And success can blind you to another's misfortune: “they should have tried harder”. The Hanged Man's humility is useful here: help so that the person feels an equal, not a debtor.

items.title: A sun that rises anew

captions.B: Courage to renew even when all is well

items.meaning: Your life changes not out of trouble but out of fullness, and so your sun rises anew each time.
text: People envy you kindly: warm, successful, hospitable, everything works out for you. Your light comes from the Sun, and Death reminds you of its main property: even the sun sets every evening in order to rise anew in the morning. Your union is about the courage to change your life not out of trouble but out of fullness: to let go of what is successful once it stops bringing joy, and to begin a new day.

A good flat, a steady job, friends who invite you to their country cottage — you have it all. And suddenly you admit to each other that you are bored. Instead of putting up with it, you let the flat and go abroad for a year to learn a language and try a new craft. Friends tap their temples, but on the very first evening in the new place you sit over a textbook full of strange letters and roar with laughter, mixing up “thank you” and “sorry”. **You are meant to change your life from fullness, not from trouble, and so your sun rises anew each time.**

The light goes out when success is guarded from change. Everything is so good that it is frightening to touch, and you freeze: the same places, the same conversations, the same pride in what you have achieved. Or one wants something new and the other clings to what works, and the argument turns into reproaches: “nothing's ever enough for you”. Let the old radiance go with gratitude — the new will be no paler if you meet it together.

items.title: The sun in a soft light

captions.A: Vivid, successful and full of energy
captions.B: A warm measure: joy without excess

items.meaning: Your light warms rather than scorches: you enjoy life without excess or showy display.
text: Your shared task is a joy that needs no excess. The Sun makes you a vivid, successful, visible couple: you work a lot, celebrate a lot, give a lot. Temperance softens this light to a warm glow in which both you and those around you feel good: no race for status, no showy display, gratitude for what you already have.

For your tenth wedding anniversary friends expect a lavish party from you — you always loved a grand scale. Instead of a banquet you rent a cottage by the water and invite the eight people closest to you. No host, no programme, conversations until dawn and a barbecue everyone takes turns at. The guests later say it was the best party of their lives. **Your light warms all the more when there is nothing superfluous in it.**

The Sun overheats easily. Success demands ever new proof: more expensive, bigger, better than the neighbours' — and strength and money go on it. There is another risk too: one balances while the other shines, and the first tires of living in the shadow of someone else's brilliance. Measure is neither poverty nor modesty for show, but an honest answer to the question: how much do we really need to be happy?

items.title: Living life to the full

captions.A: A successful, vivid couple people envy
captions.B: Great prosperity and a taste for pleasure

items.meaning: Modesty isn't your style: you want big things, achieve them and enjoy what you have earned together.
text: Modesty is not your style, and you don't hide it. The Sun makes you vivid, successful, warm: people are drawn to you, people envy you. The Devil adds the courage to want big things — a house, travel, a business of your own, a passion that does not fade with the years. Your meeting is about living life to the full and not apologising for it.

You open your patisserie with the last of your money, and in the very first week the queue stretches round the corner. Instead of a modest “let's celebrate at home” you close for the evening and invite everyone who helped: from the cream supplier to the neighbour who guarded the renovation for a week. Until three in the morning you dance between the display cases and count not the takings but the guests. **Your prosperity shines not just for you: you celebrate success so that its warmth reaches everyone who was there.**

The Sun and the Devil together overheat easily. Success is never enough, work eats up weekends, and money begins to measure the worth of people, each other included. Comparisons, the race for status, a jealous count of who brought in more — and the joy drains out of prosperity. Stop now and then and ask yourselves which of all this you really wanted.

items.title: Sun after the storm

captions.A: Successful, vivid and in the public eye
captions.B: Support in each other when all falls apart

items.meaning: Anyone can shine in fine weather; you met to stay a light for each other in a storm.
text: Much goes well for you: happy and successful, you are used to things working out. But the Tower reminds you that success is not forever: a business, a position, a familiar life can all be shaken. That is exactly when your meeting is tested. Anyone can shine in fine weather; you are to become a light for each other in a storm.

Your restaurant is the most fashionable in town, and then within six months it all collapses: the area empties, guests leave, debts arrive. You close it without scenes or panic, move to a smaller flat and start again — first lunches to order for friends, then a small café. Acquaintances are amazed that you haven't lost your smile. **Your sun shines even after the storm, because you keep it alight for each other.**

Falling hurts successful people especially. Pride gets in the way of admitting failure, and you pretend everything is fine, spending your last strength on the picture. The other trap: one blames the other for the collapse and compares them with their former brilliance: “you used to be different”. Allow yourselves the loss: the light comes back faster when you don't have to pretend it never went out.

items.title: A light that kindles others

captions.A: Warm, vivid and loved by all
captions.B: Inspiration and dreams that are shared

items.meaning: Around you people dare to follow their own path: your warmth kindles others' dreams.
text: People are drawn to you: a warm, cheerful couple who are easy to be with. The Sun gives light, and the Star gives it direction — inspiration and hope. Your success matters not in itself: it is there so that others believe they too can succeed. That is your shared dream, even if you have never once said it aloud.

At your birthday party a niece sits at the table, afraid to apply to art school: “what if they don't take me”. Interrupting each other, you both tell her how you changed careers at thirty-five and how frightening it was. By dessert the niece is scrolling through a foundation course programme on her phone. **Your warmth kindles other people's dreams: beside you, people dare to follow their own.**

Light that people admire easily turns into a stage. You want to be an example, and failures start to be hidden: in public all is wonderful, at home there is tiredness and anxiety. Shine honestly, stumbles and all: what inspires people is not glitter but a living path.

items.title: The sun and its night side

captions.A: Vivid, cheerful, all out in the open
captions.B: Depth, intuition and acceptance of mystery

items.meaning: Your sunny union trusts intuition and accepts what cannot be seen by day.
text: By day everything is clear to you: vivid and cheerful, you live openly and confidently. The Sun lights every corner, but the Moon reminds you that everyone has a night: dreams, anxieties, intuition, what logic cannot explain. To accept this night side — your own and each other's — is to find in it not a threat but a depth your light sometimes lacks.

In the middle of a bright summer, when everything is going wonderfully, one of you suddenly sinks into a strange sadness. The other, out of habit, tries to shake them out of it: “Come and see friends, it'll take your mind off it.” But this time they stop and simply sit beside them in the dark on the balcony. An hour later the first tells of a dream that has haunted them for a week, and in talking about it you speak for the first time of fears you had both hidden behind smiles. **Your clarity grows wiser when it learns to listen to a quiet night voice.**

The Sun doesn't like shadows. You want to fix your partner's anxiety and sadness at once, cheer them up, drown it out with advice — and the person stops sharing. There is a second danger: one lives only by day, while the other hides their night so as not to spoil the shared light. Let each other be sad: the Sun does not go out because the Moon is near.

items.title: Two suns sharing one sky

captions.B: Joy, success and a happy, generous home

items.meaning: Two suns in one sky, you shine side by side without fighting over the sky or scorching each other.
text: The Sun is doubled in your couple: vivid, warm and successful, you shine both in how others see you and in what you create together. Your home is full of guests, laughter and plans, and your successes delight both you and those around you. The key skill for two suns is to shine side by side without fighting over the sky, and to warm each other rather than scorch.

You both get promoted in the same month, and it could have become a competition: who matters more, who earns more. Instead you throw a joint “two promotions” party and invite all your friends. Toasts, laughter, jokes about now having to hire help at home. **Your two suns don't fight over the sky but light it up together, and there is light enough for everyone.**

A double sun risks scorching. Who is brighter, who more successful, who gets more praise — quiet rivalry can eat away at even a happy union. Or you can get so carried away by success that you forget to rest, and the light burns out. Rejoice in each other's victories more loudly than in your own — that is how two suns become one sky.

items.title: A light that wakes the family

captions.B: Reconciliation and revived family ties

items.meaning: With your joy you reconcile relatives and bring family ties back to life.
text: Warmth radiates from you naturally: vivid and generous, you know how to rejoice. The Sun shines on everyone, and Judgement directs that light towards the family — to old grievances, broken ties, relatives who haven't called for years. With your warmth you wake what has fallen asleep and reconcile those who have long stopped speaking.

One partner's sisters haven't spoken for fifteen years over an old quarrel about an inheritance. For your milestone birthday you invite both without telling either about the other. The first half hour is icy, then shared laughter over an old story, and by the end of the evening the sisters are sitting side by side in tears. Now they call each other every week. **Your warmth wakes what has fallen asleep in the family, and relatives become family again.**

Not everything can be thawed. Sometimes relatives aren't ready to make peace, and your efforts meet coldness. Or else: you get so caught up in other people's reconciliations that you forget your own grievances with each other. Shine, but don't demand: Judgement wakes those who are ready to wake.

items.title: The fullness of a sunny life

captions.B: Wholeness and a sense of life's fullness

items.meaning: Separate victories add up, in your hands, to a full, harmonious life.
text: Success has come to you often: vivid and happy, you can do much and have achieved much. The Sun brings victories, and the World gathers them into a whole — not a string of achievements but a fullness of life with room for work, love, friends, travel, rest. You are meant to feel that everything is in its place and stop chasing the next victory.

After yet another big success you sit on the terrace and realise you don't know what more to want. Instead of setting a new goal you simply stay there until sunset, remembering everything you have been through together. The other says: “I think we have everything.” The first nods. It is the happiest evening in years. **Your victories add up to a whole life, and you are learning to enjoy it, not just to achieve it.**

Fullness can turn into stagnation. You have everything, you stop growing, and the sun starts shining out of habit. Sometimes the trouble is different: one feels fulfilled while the other still strains towards new summits, and you stop understanding each other. Wholeness is not the end of the road but a platform from which the next horizon can be seen.

items.title: The sun allowed to play

captions.B: Carefree joy and freedom from the race

items.meaning: Enjoying life with no aim and resting without guilt — that is what your success opens up.
text: Your success is on display: vivid and active, you are always busy. The Sun shines at full strength, and the Fool reminds you that you can shine just because — not for a result but for joy. Rest without guilt, play without a goal, laughter without a reason — that is what you often lack. You are meant to allow yourselves to be carefree.

Even on holiday you both check work email. This time the other takes the first's phone, locks it in the hotel safe and says: “A week. No work. We're going to fool around.” The first two days are hard going; on the third you build a sandcastle; on the fifth you learn to stand on a surfboard and fall off a hundred times in a row. You come home feeling ten years younger. **Your sun learns to play, and joy stops depending on success.**

Carefreeness may seem a weakness to successful people. One rests, the other worries about missed opportunities and pulls them back into the race. And lightness can turn into carelessness about a business you have built for years. Alternate: the sun shines on weekdays and weekends alike, only differently.

items.title: Your own call in a noisy family

captions.B: Your own quiet decision and mutual trust

items.meaning: Your relatives are always near, and you met to decide what matters together, behind a closed door.
text: Your relatives are always near: advice, opinions, questions about children, a wedding, a flat. Judgement keeps you within the family circle, and the High Priestess closes the door: important things are decided by the two of you. About family, children, your life — not by others' expectations but consciously. And you still have to work out which attitudes you inherited from your elders and whether you want to carry them on.

Every family gathering begins with the elders' same question: “So when?” You take a week and go away together to a cabin by a lake, without relatives or phones, to talk calmly for the first time about what you yourselves want. You come back with a decision that belongs to you alone, and gently but firmly tell the family: “This is our business, and we've decided.” **You learn to hear yourselves through the family chorus, and the decision becomes truly yours.**

Keeping things between the two of you can hurt relatives. They are used to taking part in everything, and your closed doors seem to them like estrangement. Or it goes otherwise: one still secretly consults the family, and trust between you cracks. Tell your relatives your decisions with care, but don't report to them: the Priestess guards your secret without disowning the family.

items.title: A family line that grows

captions.A: Holding to kin and family traditions
captions.B: Plenty, a home and a growing family

items.meaning: You grow family and prosperity so that the family line continues and grows stronger.
text: Family to you means the family line: traditions, elders, children, the bond of generations. Judgement keeps you within the family circle, and the Empress gives that circle fruit: a home, prosperity, a growing family, a generous table. You are meant not only to keep the roots but to grow new branches from them.

When you first invite the whole family to your place for New Year, everyone comes: grandmothers make aspic, grandfathers set up folding tables, aunts bring pickles. You realise your home has become the centre of the family, and you decide to enlarge it: you build on rooms and plant a big garden so that there is room for everyone. Now four generations gather at your celebrations. **Your family line grows, and you become the garden where it thrives.**

A family's abundance can become a burden. You take on caring for everyone, and your couple gets lost among the relatives. And a growing family can demand so much that neither strength nor time is left for the two of you. Grow the family, but guard your own branch: the Empress cares for the whole garden, but for herself as well.

items.title: A house to outlast generations

captions.A: Close to their kin, keepers of the family
captions.B: A firm foundation for the whole family

items.meaning: You build your family a reliable home that will outlast the generations.
text: Keepers of the family — that is one way to describe you: you are close to your relatives and stick by your own. Judgement ties you to the family line, and the Emperor gives that line a footing: a home, prosperity, an order children and grandchildren can lean on. You are meant to build something that will outlive you — a firm foundation for the whole family.

Grandfather's old house in the village was falling apart, and the relatives had long given up on it. You decide to restore it: for five years you put all your holidays and savings into it, relay the foundations, replace the roof, bring in water. Now every summer everyone gathers here, from great-grandmother to great-grandchildren, and each has a room of their own. **You build your family a house that will stand for another hundred years.**

A foundation for the family can become a burden. You take responsibility for everyone and overstrain yourselves, and the relatives get used to you sorting everything out. Or power over the shared home breeds disputes: whose word counts most. Build together with your relatives, not for them: the Emperor protects, but he doesn't carry everyone on his back.

items.title: Keepers of the family line

captions.B: Living traditions, knowledge for those to come

items.meaning: The family's memory is passed on alive — not as rules but as stories, songs and meaning.
text: Roots are not empty words to you: you hold on to family, remember the family's history, honour your elders. Judgement ties you to the past, and the Hierophant makes you its keepers: you will pass traditions, values and knowledge to your children. Your task is not to preserve the past in a jar but to pass it on alive, so that it warms rather than weighs down.

One winter you gather all your older relatives and record their stories on a voice recorder: how they lived, what they ate on holidays, what songs they sang. It comes to forty hours of memories. You transcribe them and make a book with photographs, which you give to each family at New Year. Nephews and nieces who used to be bored at family gatherings now quiz the grandmothers themselves. **You turn the family's memory into living knowledge that is passed on with joy.**

Keepers easily become wardens. Traditions turn into compulsory rules, and the young start avoiding them. Or each pulls towards their own family's customs, and holidays become an argument about the right way. Pass on the meaning, not the form: a custom lives as long as people want to keep it.

items.title: A choice of heart, not of kin

captions.A: Close to their family, living by tradition
captions.B: A choice of your own and love from the heart

items.meaning: Your love is the choice of two, not of a family council — and in time the family accepts it.
text: Your union is woven tightly into family life: relatives, traditions, the approval of elders. Judgement keeps you within the family circle, and the Lovers remind you that love is the choice of two, not the decision of a family council. To choose each other with your hearts, even if your relatives expect something else, and still not turn away from them — that is your path.

One partner's parents dreamed of “a match from a good family”, while the other grew up in a small village and works with their hands. The first years — coldness at the holiday table. You don't argue or justify yourselves; you simply live: you hold hands in front of the family, help when asked, don't hide your love. Five years later the first's mother herself asks the other to teach her to bake pies. **You choose each other with your hearts, and in time the family accepts that choice.**

A choice made against the family's will can become a war. One is torn between relatives and partner, the other demands that they pick a side. Or love turns into protest, and the relationship rests on opposition rather than feeling. Don't make each other choose between love and family: give the family time to get used to it.

items.title: Taking the family business on

captions.A: Family-minded, devoted to the family cause
captions.B: Progress and wins generations waited for

items.meaning: You met to take up what your elders began and carry it further — boldly and in your own way.
text: Family means a lot to you: family traditions, the elders' work, the memory of who started what. Judgement ties you to the past, and the Chariot keeps that past from freezing. You are meant to take what your parents and grandparents began and carry it further — boldly, in your own way, to victories they could only dream of.

For many years grandmother's sewing workshop barely made ends meet. When it passes to you, relatives advise selling. Instead you study, go to trade fairs, come up with your own clothing line and start selling it online. You sew the first twenty dresses in the evenings on that very same machine of grandmother's, and they sell out within a week. **You carry forward what your elders began, and the family is proud of you.**

The family chariot can run in someone else's ruts. You so want to live up to your elders' expectations that you forget your own wishes. Or, the opposite, you break everything old to prove yourselves right and hurt those who started it. Carry the business forward, respecting its past, but choose the road yourselves.

items.title: Fairness in family matters

captions.B: Honest agreements with the family

items.meaning: You met to settle family matters honestly and openly — sacrificing neither family nor couple.
text: A thousand threads tie you to your relatives: celebrations, help, shared property, old promises. Judgement keeps you within the family circle, and Justice demands that this circle be fair. Who cares for whom, how an inheritance is divided, how much you help each family — you are to settle such questions openly and by rules everyone understands.

When the question arises of who will look after one partner's elderly mother, the relatives look to you out of habit. You gather all the brothers and sisters round one table and propose a fair plan: who comes on which days, who pays how much, who handles the paperwork. The conversation is hard, but by the end everyone agrees to the schedule. A year later the mother says she has never seen her children so united. **You bring fairness into family matters, and the family grows stronger for it.**

Fairness in a family is often mistaken for bookkeeping. Calculations begin of who put in how much and who is entitled to what, and old grievances break out in every conversation. Or you take on more than your fair share and then silently resent it. Agree in advance and out loud: relatives find it easier to accept rules than to guess your expectations.

items.title: Your own corner in a big clan

captions.B: Boundaries and a wisdom of your own

items.meaning: In a big family you keep a corner of your own and think for yourselves.
text: Your relatives are always close by: shared celebrations, advice, help, phone calls in the evening. Judgement binds you tightly to the family, and the Hermit asks for a corner of your own — a place and time where the two of you think for yourselves, without a chorus of voices. You are to set boundaries that don't hurt your relatives but give your couple room to grow into its own wisdom.

Sunday is lunch at one partner's parents', Tuesday a call from the other's parents with advice. For the first time you spend a Sunday at home together: you sleep late, go for a walk, talk about your own things. In the evening Mum rings, hurt. You calmly explain that one Sunday a month is now yours, and six months later she herself checks: “Is this your Sunday or ours?” **You build your quiet corner in a big family, and your relatives learn in time to respect it.**

Separating from your family is not easy. Every refusal brings guilt, and you either retreat or defend yourselves too sharply. There is a second danger: your quiet as two becomes a wall, and the relatives feel rejected. Talk about boundaries calmly and in advance, not in a moment of hurt: that way they are easier to accept.

items.title: A second chance from fate

captions.A: Family-minded, loyal, holding to their roots
captions.B: The luck of a second chance, the nerve to change

items.meaning: Fate gives you a second chance, and you know how to take it, remembering past lessons.
text: Roots matter to you: you hold on to family, traditions, your own. Judgement ties you to the past, and the Wheel of Fortune shows that the past is not a sentence. Fate turns and gives second chances: to return to an abandoned dream, to make peace with those you fell out with, to begin what once failed. You are to recognise these chances and not let them slip.

The house where one of you grew up was sold to strangers long ago, and they often reminisce about it aloud: the veranda, the old pear tree, the creak of the gate. Then suddenly you see an ad — the house is for sale again, and at a price you can manage. The decision is made in an evening. Now your apple trees grow in that very garden, and the neighbours still remember grandfather. **The wheel turns towards you with a second chance, and you know how to take it.**

Second chances frighten those who fear repeating the past. One clings to an old grievance and refuses the turn; the other is angry that they are letting luck slip. Or it goes another way: the past comes back, and you meet it with the same old mistakes. The wheel offers a chance but promises no result: take it, remembering what you have learned.

items.title: A pillar for the whole family

captions.A: Family-minded, devoted, sticking by their own
captions.B: Strength to protect your own and stand firm

items.meaning: Those close to you come first, and you become a pillar for them that knows how to say “no”.
text: Those close to you come above all else, and it shows: you are a strong family couple. Judgement ties you to the family line, and Strength gives you the role you have been growing into: to become its pillar. Not one that obeys the elders or orders the young about, but one that can be leaned on on a hard day — calm, dependable, able to say “no” when the family needs it.

When one partner's father loses his job at fifty-eight, all the relatives advise him to keep his head down. You instead help him open a small joinery workshop: you put in your savings and spend the first months delivering orders yourselves. The workshop finds its feet, and for the first time in years he says “thank you” to you both in front of everyone at a family dinner. **You become the strength the whole family leans on — and you yourselves decide how to spend it.**

A pillar easily becomes a burden. Relatives get used to you sorting everything out and offload their problems onto you, and you can't say no. The other trap: strength turns into power — “we know better how you should live”. Hold your strength with a gentle hand: help, but don't take other people's lives entirely upon yourselves.

items.title: Forgive, then take care

captions.B: Forgiveness and a new view of your kin

items.meaning: Your loyalty to family is joined by forgiveness: you see your relatives anew and care for them without grudges.
text: Family matters most to you, and it shows: you are close to your relatives, keep traditions, support your own. The voice of the family line sounds loudly in you — that is Judgement. The Hanged Man suggests turning your view of that line upside down: seeing old grievances against parents and siblings, past injustices, through the eyes of those who back then did not know the right way either. From such a view forgiveness is born.

One partner's father was always stern and sparing with affection, and for years you kept your distance. When he is left alone in a big house, you take on his care: you visit at weekends, mend the roof, bring pies. Over tea he suddenly talks about his own father — and for the first time you understand where that sternness came from. **You help each other forgive: to see in your relatives people who once could not cope either.**

Care becomes sacrifice when it is carried out of guilt. One gives the family all their time and strength, the other puts up with it in silence, and your own home empties. Or forgiveness stays in words while old grievances break out in every family quarrel. The Hanged Man teaches you to look differently, but not to forget yourselves: care for your relatives in a way that doesn't lose you each other.

items.title: The end of a family script

captions.A: A couple who put family first
captions.B: A new chapter of the family story

items.meaning: Old family scripts end with you: a new chapter of the family line begins with the two of you.
text: Family comes first for you, and people see it: you are close to your relatives, hold on to your own and open up only to them. Judgement is the voice of the family line, the memory of generations you carry with pride. But not all of it is worth carrying further, and Death helps you separate inheritance from burden. Your task is to end the family stories that keep repeating — grievances, taboos, the habit of silence — and begin a new one with yourselves.

In both your families it was not done to talk about feelings: love was shown through food and reproaches. When you move in together, you agree it will be different for you. You learn to say “I love you” aloud, to hug for no reason, to apologise when you were wrong. The grandmothers are puzzled at first, and then start hugging goodbye themselves. **With you the old family story ends, and a new one begins — one you will want to pass on.**

Judgement and Death collide painfully when renewal is taken for betrayal of the family. Relatives take offence, you feel guilty and slip back. Or the reverse: the roots are cut away entirely, rejecting even what could have supported you. Say goodbye to the family's past with gratitude: you can leave the script behind without disowning the people.

items.title: Family and couple in balance

captions.A: Family-minded, loyal, with their own circle
captions.B: A balance between family and the two of you

items.meaning: You give the family its due but keep what matters most for the two of you — that measure is the point of your union.
text: Your greatest wealth is family, and people know it. Judgement keeps you within the family circle: parents, siblings, grandfather's traditions, compulsory Sunday lunches. Temperance looks for the proportion at which there is enough for the family and for the two of you — so that love for your relatives does not eat up your time together, and your time together does not tear you from your roots.

One partner's mother lives under the same roof as you. The first six months: constant arguments about who is in charge in the kitchen. Then you divide the house: Mum has her own room and her own evening, you have your bedroom and a rule of knocking before entering, and on Sundays there is a shared lunch with everyone at one table. **You join family and couple so that everyone has enough room and enough warmth.**

Measure is lost when relatives start deciding for the two of you. The elders' opinion outweighs your own, and one of you feels they are living by someone else's rules. In such a union Temperance means boundaries agreed in advance, not won in a quarrel.

items.title: Your own wealth, your own call

captions.A: A couple for whom family always comes first
captions.B: Means of your own, free of others' control

items.meaning: Staying close to your family, you earn and decide for yourselves — your own strength is no enemy of family.
text: Your family is not just the two of you but a whole clan, and relatives are always close by: with advice, money, opinions. Judgement keeps you within the family circle. The Devil nudges you towards something unexpected — your own strength: your own money, your own desires, your own right to decide. You are to step out from under the family's wing and build a prosperity you manage yourselves.

One partner's parents gave you a flat, and with it came their right to decide what curtains you have and when to have children. You decide to move to a rented place and save for your own. The room is cramped, side jobs eat up the weekends, but on the very first evening you hang curtains you chose yourselves — cheap, bright yellow, and you both think they are wonderful. Relations with the family only grow warmer for it. **You build your well-being yourselves, and so you can be generous to your relatives without debts or grudges.**

A pull towards your own can turn into a fight with the family. Money becomes a battlefield: who owes whom, who put in how much, who will inherit. There is a second danger too: one still depends on parental support, and the other is angry and demands a choice. Separate gently: independence is valuable when it doesn't turn your relatives into enemies.

items.title: Family after the collapse

captions.A: A family couple devoted to their kin
captions.B: New, honest relations with the family

items.meaning: When the family order cracks, you build new relations with your kin — more honest than before.
text: Family is sacred to you, and devotion to your own shows in everything you do. The Tower brings a trial into this picture: the family order may crack — an old grievance comes to light, an inheritance is divided, what generations kept quiet about surfaces. You are to come through this collapse and build new relations with your family — more honest and freer than before.

Dividing a grandmother's flat splits one partner's family: the brothers aren't speaking, the parents are in tears. You take no one's side, and when passions cool a little, you gather everyone on neutral ground — a rented house in the country. The conversation is hard, with tears and shouting, but by morning, for the first time in ten years, everyone sits at one table. **You come through the collapse of family grievances and build in its place something that rests not on silence but on truth.**

Family collapses wound more deeply than others. You want to put everything back as it was, to pretend nothing happened — and the crack remains. Or you can be so hurt by your relatives that you cut ties altogether. The Tower destroys in order to build: don't rush either to make peace at any cost or to leave for good.

items.title: Your own star in the family

captions.A: A couple for whom family and kin come first
captions.B: A dream of your own, and hope for your children

items.meaning: Honouring your family, you find a dream of your own and give hope to those who come after you.
text: Your lives are tightly woven into your family's: celebrations, duties, traditions handed down from generation to generation. Judgement keeps the bond with your kin, and the Star reminds you that everyone in that family line should have a dream of their own, not just an inherited script. Together you are meant to find yours and show your children that you can honour your family and still shine in your own way.

At a family council it is decided who will take on grandfather's car repair shop — and everything points to you. Then the other quietly says they have dreamed all their life of something else: teaching children to draw. Silence falls; grandmother purses her lips. The first takes their hand and answers for both: “Your brother will take the garage, and we'll open a studio.” **You choose your own star without disowning your family, and in doing so you give hope to everyone who comes after you.**

Family expectations can put a star out. The dream is put off because “our own need help”, and years go on other people's plans. Or you can defend your dream so sharply that you break with your relatives. The Star's light is gentle: talk about your dream calmly and often, until your family gets used to seeing you this way.

items.title: Family secrets by moonlight

captions.A: Family-minded, devoted to kin and tradition
captions.B: Understanding family secrets, trusting instinct

items.meaning: Every family has things kept quiet, and you look gently into that shadow to understand yourselves.
text: You know your family's history — at least the part told round the holiday table. Judgement ties you to the family line, and the Moon reminds you that every family has things it keeps quiet about. Unspoken grievances, forgotten names, recurring stories. You look carefully into this shadow to understand what from it still affects your life.

Going through grandmother's old trunk, you find letters no one in the family knew about: she had a first love, a parting, a secret friendship that lasted her whole life. In the evenings you read them aloud and suddenly recognise your own fears in grandmother's. Much in your couple becomes clearer. **You look into the shadows of your family and find in them keys to yourselves.**

Family secrets can be heavy. A dug-up past can wound the living, and you don't know whether to tell the relatives. Or the family shadow becomes an excuse: “it runs in our family”. Open secrets with care, decide together what to share, and remember: knowledge of the past is there to make you freer, not to find someone to blame.

items.title: A big table for the whole family

captions.B: Joy and warmth that bring the family together

items.meaning: You met so that your family gathers not for sad occasions but around joy and a big table.
text: You hold on tight to your own: family is your greatest wealth. Judgement ties you to the family line, and the Sun makes that tie warm and joyful: not duties and debts but celebrations, laughter, a big table with room for everyone. You become the sun around which the family gathers.

For years your relatives saw each other only on sad occasions. You decide to change that and invite everyone to the country cottage in summer — just because, with no occasion. Thirty people come, children meet their second cousins, the old folk remember their youth. The gathering becomes a yearly event, and now people look forward to it more than to New Year. **You gather the family around joy, and it feels like a family again.**

A sun in a family can overheat. You become the centre everyone comes to for help and celebrations, and you run out of breath yourselves. Or joy turns into an obligation: there must always be a celebration, and every hitch becomes a reason for grievance. Accept your relatives' help as generously as you give: everyone lays the table, not just the hosts.

items.title: Family as a calling

captions.A: Family-minded, devoted, sticking by their own
captions.B: A strong family, forgiveness, generations linked

items.meaning: Family is your calling, and you build it on forgiveness, not on duty.
text: Judgement is doubled in your chart: family is both how others see you and what you are together for. You are devoted to your family line, stick by your own, value marriage and tradition. You are meant to create a family that becomes a support for several generations: where mistakes are forgiven, elders respected, the young heard, and the doors always open to your own.

Four generations gather at your celebrations: great-grandmother, grandmothers, you, nephews and nieces. Every year you take a group photo on the same porch. The youngest nephew asks why some people are missing from the old pictures, and you tell him the family's story — with quarrels, reconciliations and forgiveness. **You are building a family line where forgiveness is stronger than grievances, and it will outlive you.**

Double Judgement can become a court in the literal sense. Relatives judge, discuss, control, and your private life dissolves into the family's. Or grievances are handed down from generation to generation, while forgiveness stays in words. Keep the doors open, but close them sometimes too: the family needs a couple that has something of its own, theirs alone.

items.title: A family open to the world

captions.B: Openness and the union of different worlds

items.meaning: Your family holds firm, and you met to open it to the world and bring different cultures to one table.
text: You hold on tight to your roots: traditional, family-minded, loyal to your family line. Judgement keeps the bond with the past, and the World widens it to the horizon. Your family can become a home for different people, cultures and views and grow only stronger for it. You are meant to join your family line with the wide world.

When one partner's younger sister marries a man from another continent, the relatives are bewildered. You, though, fly out to meet his family, learn a few words of their language, bring jam and grandmother's pie recipe. At the wedding the two families each sing their own songs, and by morning they sing together. Now your family holiday is celebrated on two continents. **Your family grows wider when you open it to the world, and the roots only grow stronger.**

Openness can unsettle relatives. The elders don't accept change, and you find yourselves between tradition and a new world. Or you get so carried away by the wide world that you break from your roots. Widen the family with care: Judgement guards the past, the World opens the future, and you stand between them.

items.title: Free of the family chorus

captions.B: Freedom to live your own way, and lightness

items.meaning: You live your own way and laugh at others' expectations without drifting from your family.
text: Your relatives mean a lot to you, and their voice sounds loudly in your life: advice, expectations, “the way we do things”. Judgement keeps you within the family circle, and the Fool flings the door open: you may live your own way. Freedom doesn't mean giving up family — it means the right to your own decisions, mistakes, adventures. You are meant to learn this lightness without hurting your own.

The whole family has decided that you will see in the New Year at grandmother's as always. This time, for the first time, you say: “We're going to the mountains, just the two of us.” Shock, hurt, phone calls. You see the New Year in in a tent on a slope, with a flask and sparklers, and it is the best celebration of your lives. And at Christmas you visit grandmother with presents and stories, and she listens open-mouthed. **You allow yourselves freedom and find that the family doesn't lose you for it.**

Freedom from family can turn into flight. You are so eager to break away that you sever ties, and then you miss them. Or one is free while the other is torn between you and their relatives. Separate lightly and with a smile: the Fool sets off on the road, but he can always come home.

items.title: Depth amid wide spaces

captions.B: Emotional depth and quiet closeness

items.meaning: You understand each other to the very bottom, not just see the world together.
text: Your world is wide: free and open, you have seen different countries and different people. The World gives breadth, and the High Priestess depth: understanding your partner not by words but by pauses; sharing what is most intimate; accepting the dark sides, not just the bright ones. Your freedom becomes closeness when it has room for quiet as two.

Travelling, you meet hundreds of people, but on a night train one of you admits: “I think I know more about our fellow passengers than about you.” It is painful and honest. That evening, for the first time, you tell each other what you have never told anyone: childhood fears, old shameful stories, secret dreams. After that night you look at each other differently. **Your wide spaces gain depth, and beside you is a person you know to the very bottom.**

Opening up is scarier than travelling: to open up is to become vulnerable, and you want to retreat again into the lightness of the road. Dive in turns and together: the Priestess guards the depths, but she doesn't lock them.

items.title: Travellers plant a garden

captions.A: Free, rootless, citizens of the world
captions.B: A garden, a home and plenty on your land

items.meaning: You find a place where you want to put down roots and grow something of your own.
text: Roots were never part of your story: free and open, you lived now here, now there. The World gives space, and the Empress suggests stopping to plant a garden. A home of your own, land of your own, a harvest of your own give freedom meaning. You are meant to find a place where you will want to stay, and grow your own abundance there.

On yet another trip you end up in a small mountain village that smells of woodsmoke and apples, and get stuck there for a month: helping your landlady with the harvest, learning to make jam in a copper pan. As you leave, you put down a deposit on an abandoned house at the edge of the village and argue all the way home about where the garden will go. Friends don't believe you have settled. **Your freedom finds its soil, and a journey turns into a garden that grows.**

Roots may seem shackles to free people. One falls in love with the house, the other starts to miss the roads. Or the household eats up all your time, and the world you loved so much is forgotten. Plant the garden, but keep a suitcase ready: the Empress grows, the World calls, and there is room for both.

items.title: A home for citizens of the world

captions.B: A home of your own and a reliable footing

items.meaning: You build a reliable base so that you have somewhere to come back to from any road.
text: Your addresses change often: free and open, you live now here, now there. The World gives space, and the Emperor reminds you of home — not a cage but a base: a corner of your own, a steady income, a reserve that doesn't depend on where you happen to be. Freedom grows calmer when there is somewhere to return to.

You change countries more often than others change holiday destinations, and you never stay in a rented flat longer than two years. Sitting on your suitcases in yet another of them, you decide to buy a small house — not to settle down, but to have somewhere to come back to. Now between trips you live in your own house by a lake, and a map with pins hangs in the hall. **Your freedom gets a home, and now you come back from every road instead of simply moving on.**

A home may seem an anchor to free people. One grows attached to it, the other misses the road and pulls towards travel. Sometimes looking after the house eats up time for travel, and you both feel trapped. Let your home be a harbour, not a permanent mooring: you can put out to sea from it.

items.title: A way of life from many worlds

captions.B: Shared values and a way of life born of experience

items.meaning: From the experience of many countries you assemble your own way of life — not much, but yours.
text: You have seen a lot: different countries, different people, different ways of living. The World has given you breadth, and the Hierophant asks you to make something of your own from it — a way of life, values, traditions that will be yours. Not other people's customs, but your own, gathered bit by bit from everything you have seen that touched you both.

From every trip you bring back not a souvenir but a custom: a Japanese tea ceremony on Sundays, a long Italian lunch with friends, a sauna before New Year like the northern neighbours. So many customs pile up that friends call your home “a country of its own” with its own calendar of holidays. **You assemble your way of life from the best you have seen in the world, and it becomes yours alone.**

A way of life gathered from everywhere can be left without roots. There are many customs, but none has really taken hold, and the family has nothing to lean on. A different trap: one holds to the traditions of their own country, the other to foreign ones, and you argue about whose faith is right. Choose a few things, but hold on to them: the Hierophant needs loyalty, not a collection.

items.title: The free choose each other

captions.A: Free, modern, with a broad outlook
captions.B: Closeness and a choice made out of love

items.meaning: You are free to be apart, and that is exactly why you choose every day to be together — that is why you met.
text: Freedom is your foundation: a broad outlook, a modern relationship, a world without borders. The World gives space, and the Lovers bring something worth more than space — closeness. You are not obliged to be together, and that is exactly why your choice of each other carries such weight. Free people who decide every day to stay side by side — that is your love.

For a long time your relationship was light: different cities, rare meetings, no promises. After three months apart one flies in without warning and says: “I don't want to be without you any more.” You don't give up your freedom — you simply decide to live it together. **Your freedom grows deeper when a choice appears in it: I'm with you.**

Closeness can frighten freedom. One wants more time together, the other feels restricted. There is a second danger: freedom becomes an excuse not to choose, and the relationship hangs in uncertainty. Agree that your union is the choice of free people — not a cage, and not a chance encounter.

items.title: A lifelong expedition

captions.B: Goals, routes and wins on distant roads

items.meaning: Freedom needs a goal, and your travels become expeditions in which the road has meaning.
text: Space is something you never lack: travel, moves, friends all over the world. The World gives breadth, and the Chariot fills it with purpose. Not just to drive wherever your eyes lead you, but to plot routes, take summits, see expeditions through. Your freedom becomes truly yours when it has a direction.

You decide to drive across a whole continent, from one coast to the other, in a single summer. Friends think it madness. You plan the route, fix up an old off-roader and assign roles: one at the wheel, the other navigator and cook. Three months later you stand on the ocean shore, tanned and tired, knowing everything about each other. **Your freedom gains a goal, and every road becomes a shared victory.**

Expeditions can replace life. You are so taken with long routes that unpaid bills and unanswered calls pile up at home. Alternate roads and stops: the chariot drives on better when it is put in the garage now and then.

items.title: Freedom by fair rules

captions.B: An equal partnership and clear agreements

items.meaning: Your freedom rests on fair rules: in an equal partnership there is room and clarity for you both.
text: A modern view of relationships is in your blood: free, open, without prejudice. The World gives you space, and Justice makes that space safe: clear agreements, an equal contribution, fair rules both of you know. Freedom without rules turns into uncertainty; with them it becomes a real partnership.

You work in different countries and live apart for six months of the year. So that it doesn't turn into endless rows, you write down rules: a call every evening, shared money in one account, who flies to whom and when, what counts as a breach of trust. Friends wonder how you manage without quarrels. **Your freedom rests on an honest agreement, and so there is no room in it for suspicion.**

Rules can feel tight for free people. One starts seeing control in the agreements, the other betrayal in any departure from them. Revisit the rules together and in good time: fairness in a free couple changes along with life.

items.title: A journey inwards

captions.B: Wisdom brought back from the road

items.meaning: You travel not only round the world but inwards, and from every road you bring back understanding.
text: Roads are in your blood: flights, new countries, people from all over the world. The World gives you space, and the Hermit offers the hardest journey of all — inwards. Together you are to bring back from your travels not only photos but understanding: about life, about yourselves, about what really matters. Then every road will make you wiser.

Instead of another noisy resort you walk an old pilgrimage route: three weeks, rucksacks, nights in monastery guest houses. You talk little and think a lot. At the last halt the other says that for the first time in years they know what they want: to leave their job and study. The first nods — they had been thinking the same. **Your roads lead not only across the map but deep within, and you come back from them wiser.**

Depth requires stopping, and you are used to moving. Travel turns into escape from your thoughts, and you change countries so as not to meet yourselves. Make at least one trip a year a quiet one: no plan, no hurry, just the two of you.

items.title: Luck at every point on the map

captions.B: Happy accidents in the wide world

items.meaning: Your luck lives on the road: in delayed flights and chance cafés you find what you lack at home.
text: Breadth runs through everything about you: a free couple who move easily and find your own people everywhere. The World opens the map before you, and the Wheel of Fortune scatters happy accidents across it. Trust the road — unexpected turns, unplanned stops, people you meet on trains. That is exactly where your luck hides.

Your flight is delayed for a day in an unfamiliar city, and instead of fuming you go for a walk. In a small café you get talking to the owners; by night you are invited to a family dinner, and in the morning they see you off with a jar of jam and an invitation for the whole of next summer. **Your luck lives on the road: every unplanned turn opens up a new piece of the world for you.**

Freedom and luck together easily turn into an endless wait for the next miracle. You wander from chance to chance and put down roots nowhere, while those close to you stay far away. Carry not only a suitcase but a reserve: luck loves those who are ready for its whims.

items.title: Strength for the wide world

captions.B: Stamina and courage for big things

items.meaning: You choose big challenges together and see them through — the world is within your reach.
text: A map of the world is always to hand, and you set off easily. Strength gives this open space a footing: stamina, courage, the ability to get through a hard stretch of road. Together you dare what most people don't: long routes, difficult projects, a life beyond the familiar.

The dream of crossing a mountain range has lived in you for five years. A year of preparation: weekend training, maps, gear. On the fourth day of the trek the other twists an ankle, and the first carries both rucksacks to the pass; there you decide not to give up but to walk more slowly. Two weeks later you stand on the summit — behind schedule, but together. **You are made for roads that need not only freedom but the strength to reach the end together.**

Strength in the wide world can turn into a chase for records. Every route must be harder than the last, and you remember your closeness only at rest stops. Choose goals within reach for you both: a shared summit is worth more than a personal record.

items.title: Seeing through others' eyes

captions.A: Free travellers with a broad outlook
captions.B: Empathy for people who live differently

items.meaning: To you the world is not just space but other lives: you see them through the eyes of those who live differently.
text: The world is your home: travel, moves, friends in different countries. The World gives you space, and the Hanged Man teaches you how to live in it: not as a tourist taking photos but as a guest who turns their view around and tries to understand how others live. Together you collect not countries on a list but an understanding of people.

Instead of another resort you spend your holiday volunteering on a farm in a mountain village: milking goats, teaching children English, sleeping on mattresses. In the evenings your hosts talk about their lives, and for the first time you realise how little you knew about what “hard” means. You come home changed, and your dinner-table conversations change for a long time. **You travel not for impressions but for the ability to see the world from the other side.**

A broad view turns into condescension when other lives are measured by your own yardstick. A change of view is needed between the two of you too: sometimes look at the world through each other's eyes.

items.title: A new world after the old
