captions.A: Free, modern and open to the world
captions.B: A new life in another land

items.meaning: You close a completed circle of life without regret and step into the next together — even in another country.
text: Your friends are scattered all over the world, and your views on life are broad and modern. The World brings a circle of life to fullness, and Death keeps you from getting stuck in that fullness. When a circle has closed, you close it without regret and step into the next together — sometimes into another city, sometimes another country, sometimes simply another life under the same roof.

With established careers and a flat in the centre, you sell almost everything and move to a country where you know no one. The first year: language classes, odd jobs, mistakes in every document. The second: first friends, the first job in your profession. In the third you catch yourselves dreaming in the new language. **You know how to close one world and enter another without losing each other at the border.**

A new circle does not begin if the old one is not finished. You can move a thousand kilometres away and take the same quarrels, grievances and habits with you. Before each crossing, sort out what you are taking and what you are leaving — aloud and together.

items.title: Two languages at one table

captions.A: Open to the world, free, without borders
captions.B: A harmony of two different worlds

items.meaning: Two different worlds share your table, and from them you blend a third world of your own.
text: Your home is a meeting place of two worlds: different languages, habits, cuisines, views on holidays and bringing up children. The World makes you open and free; Temperance teaches the chief art of such a union — blending. Not choosing whose world is right, but joining both in a proportion where neither loses its flavour.

One grew up by the sea and eats fish for breakfast, the other in the mountains and cannot imagine a morning without porridge. At home you speak a mix of two languages, and guests leave having learned a couple of words in each. You see in the New Year twice, by two calendars, and friends in both countries envy you. **You create a third world, where two different ways of life do not argue but complement each other.**

The blend clouds when one world starts dissolving the other. The one who moved to the partner's country gradually loses their language, their friends, their holidays, and one day feels like a guest in their own life. And differences that used to delight begin to irritate over time: “that's not how we do it”. Watch the proportion: each of you needs a corner where their world sounds at full strength.

items.title: Passion without borders

captions.A: Free, open, citizens of the world
captions.B: Big ambitions and passion across distance

items.meaning: Your world has no borders: you build big and hold on to each other at any distance.
text: The world is open to you: you move easily, work in different countries, and to many your couple is a model of the modern union. The Devil brings two strong feelings into this freedom — ambition and attachment. You build big — a business, capital, a life without borders — and learn not to lose each other when thousands of kilometres lie between you.

One of you works on another continent three months a year. You call every evening, and reunions after a separation are like a honeymoon. Your shared business is growing in two countries at once, two clocks showing different times hang in the kitchen, and before calling you still check both. **The wider your world, the stronger the thread that runs between you across every distance.**

Freedom and grip fall out when one begins to suspect the other. Separation breeds jealousy, calls become checks, and one partner's success gives the other a reason for envy. Agree on what holds you together besides passion and work: a shared place, a shared ritual, shared plans for old age.

items.title: A world put back together

captions.B: A new world on the wreckage of the old

items.meaning: Your familiar world may collapse, but you know how to rebuild it anywhere.
text: Breadth of outlook is your greatest wealth: free and open, you feel at home anywhere. But any world can collapse, and the Tower reminds you of it: borders close, plans are cut short, a familiar life becomes impossible in a day. Your strength lies not in avoiding this but in putting your world back together wherever you end up.

You live in another country, with a home, a business and a circle of friends there, and suddenly circumstances force you to drop everything within a month and come back. The first weeks: bewilderment, an empty flat, a feeling that your life has been stolen. Then you start small: you ring old friends, set out the cups you brought with you, and on the very first Friday invite guests for the same soup you used to make there. **You rebuild your world on any wreckage, because your real home is in each other.**

The collapse of a world strikes at what you hold dearest — the sense of freedom. One may freeze, pining for the old life, while the other strains towards the new, and you stop understanding each other. Or you both blame circumstances and wait for years for everything to come back. Your freedom is inside you, not in your passport: start with what you can still choose.

items.title: A star on the world map

captions.A: Free, modern, a model for many
captions.B: A big dream and inspiration without borders

items.meaning: Your dreams are the size of the world, and you inspire others with them.
text: To many your couple is a model: free, modern, open to everything new. The World gives you space, and the Star gives you a reason to use it: dreams not for the next holiday but for a lifetime. Together you are to set a goal worth crossing an ocean for, and pursue it so that others, watching you, start dreaming bigger too.

One evening you spread a huge map on the floor and mark with pins the places where you want to live for at least a month one day. There are forty-three pins. One jokes that a lifetime won't be enough; the other replies that this means you have to start now — and you book the first trip on the spot. Friends follow your notes from the road and admit that because of you they have bought their own first tickets. **Your dream is the size of the world, and its light is enough to kindle others'.**

Big dreams easily turn into a race for experiences. The pins on the map matter more than the trips themselves, and photos more than talking to each other. Or one partner's dream leads to one side of the world and the other's to the opposite. Compare your maps: the star must be shared, even if the roads to it differ.

items.title: Riddles of the wide world

captions.A: Free travellers, open to the new
captions.B: Intuition and a love of the world's mysteries

items.meaning: Beneath the surface of new places you look for mystery and find it together.
text: Countries, languages, people — your geography is rich. The World gives you space, and the Moon calls you to where the guidebooks end: ancient legends, night-time rites, dreams dreamed only in certain places. You travel in depth: seeking not sights but mysteries, and trusting the instinct that leads you to them.

In a small mountain village an old woman tells you the legend of a lake that can be seen only in fog. Next morning there is fog, and, laughing, you set off to look. You never find the lake, but you come back with a story you tell for years and a feeling that the world is far more mysterious than it seemed. **The world is not just a map to you but a mystery, and you both love to look into it.**

Mystery can become an escape from simple life. You are so drawn to the mysterious that everyday life seems bland and those close to you dull. And if one takes the mystical seriously while the other treats it with irony, misunderstanding grows between you. Respect each other's interests, but don't let moonlight block out the day.

items.title: A sun in every time zone

captions.A: Quick off the mark, open to the world
captions.B: Joy and success without borders

items.meaning: Your light travels with you, and every new place becomes warm.
text: It is as if there are no borders for you: quick off the mark and open, you feel at home in different countries. The World gives you space, and the Sun fills it with warmth. Wherever you find yourselves, you know how to throw a party, find friends, succeed. Your couple is like a sun that rises in every time zone.

In every new city the first thing you do is find the best market and the best bakery and throw a dinner for your new neighbours. A month later you have friends; six months later a favourite park bench and a butcher who keeps the best cuts for you. When you move on, half the neighbourhood comes to the farewell dinner. **Your light moves with you, and every new place becomes warm.**

A sun on the road can forget its roots. You are so taken with new places that old friends and family are left far away, and one day you feel lonely. It can also go like this: joy comes to depend on novelty, and ordinary days seem dull. Keep a few fixed points — people and habits — that you return to from any country.

items.title: Roots on the world map

captions.A: Free, on the move, open to the world
captions.B: Bonds with roots and kin scattered worldwide

items.meaning: You roam the world, and you find your family and history on the map of the whole world.
text: A home without walls — that is you: you live now here, now there, and let go of places easily. The World gives space, and Judgement calls you to your roots — to family scattered across the world, to the family's history, to the places where it all began. You are meant to gather what has scattered and feel that even without a fixed address you have a home.

Going through old family papers, you learn that one partner's great-grandfather left for overseas a hundred years ago and that you have relatives on another continent. You find them online, write to each other, and a year later fly out to meet them. Twenty people who have never seen you welcome you as their own. Now every summer you meet, at their place or yours. **You find roots on the other side of the world, and your family turns out bigger than you thought.**

Roots can pull you backwards. A rediscovered family history becomes an obsession, and real life takes a back seat. Sometimes one reaches out to the relatives with all their heart while the other, freedom-loving, feels a stranger at these gatherings. Take from the past what warms you, and don't let it run the present.

items.title: Two worlds that became one

captions.A: Free, whole, a model for many
captions.B: A whole shared world and a full life

items.meaning: Your two worlds come together into one, with room in it for both the road and home.
text: The World is doubled in your couple: free and open, to many you are a model of a harmonious union. You are meant to create what rarely succeeds: a whole shared world with room for travel and home, freedom and closeness, what is yours and what is shared. This is a union in which two people don't lose themselves but come together into something larger.

You live now in one country, now in another, speak four languages and have friends on every continent. Yet you have a ritual that doesn't change anywhere: Sunday breakfast, at which each tells what new things they have learned about the world and about themselves. Friends call your home “a little planet”. **Your two worlds merge into one, and it turns out bigger than either alone.**

Double World can become closed. You are so happy together that you stop letting others in, and harmony turns into a glass ball. And the routine of the “perfect couple” can smother live feelings, with problems hidden behind a pretty picture. Keep the doors open and let the world change: the whole stays alive as long as there is movement in it.

items.title: After the finish, a new start

captions.A: Free, and they have seen the world
captions.B: New beginnings and the lightness of adventure

items.meaning: Having finished one journey, you boldly begin the next.
text: You have seen the world: free and open, you have been through much and completed much. The World is the last arcanum of the circle, and the Fool the first of the next. Your couple is about how every finish line is followed by a new start. You are meant not to get stuck in what you have achieved but to become beginners again and again — with curiosity and lightness.

At last you buy a house on the coast and decide your travelling days are over. A few months later the other starts to mope by the window. One evening the first puts two pairs of new boots and a Spanish textbook on the table: “We haven't been to Patagonia yet.” You laugh and open the map at once, feeling like beginners. **You complete one circle and with a smile begin the next, as if for the first time.**

Endless beginning can become an escape from rest. You don't let yourselves enjoy what you have achieved and at once strain to move on. There is a second danger: one is ready for a new circle while the other wants to live in the completed one, and you stop understanding each other. Rest between circles: the Fool needs a breather in order to leap again.

items.title: A Fool who learned to listen

captions.A: Cheerful, unserious, living for the moment
captions.B: Depth of feeling and considered decisions

items.meaning: You talk about feelings seriously and decide important things consciously, without losing your laughter.
text: Seriousness is not your strong point: cheerful and light, you live for the moment and joke your way out of hard conversations. The Fool laughs, and the High Priestess asks you to listen. What does the other really feel behind their smile? What do you want from this union? Answers to such questions need quiet and honesty, and you are meant to learn how to find them.

As soon as the conversation turned to the future, you always made a joke of it. This time the other doesn't laugh at yet another joke but says quietly: “I need to know what we are to each other.” For the first time the first doesn't dodge the conversation. You sit up late, talk about a home, children, fears, and it turns out you want the same thing — you were just afraid to ask. **Your lightness learns to listen, and behind the jokes a depth appears.**

A serious talk can frighten the Fool. One tries to talk about feelings, the other jokes or disappears, and the subject is put off again. And if there is too much seriousness, depth turns into heaviness and the laughter goes out of the relationship. Talk about important things lightly, but talk: the Priestess and the Fool get on splendidly when silence and laughter take turns.

items.title: A Fool who grew a garden

captions.B: Home, family and plenty grown with love

items.meaning: You live playfully, and you met to grow something of your own — home, household, shared work — and still laugh.
text: There is a lot of the child in you: carefree and cheerful, you live playfully. The Fool skips about, and the Empress suggests stopping to grow something — a home, a garden, a family, a business. Growing up won't take away your lightness; it will give it soil. You are meant to become gardeners who plant flowers while laughing.

Your carefree life — rented flats, travel, no plans — went on for a long time. Then the other comes home with a kitten found in the rain, and the carefree life gets its first crack: the kitten needs a litter tray, regular meals and someone who won't go hitchhiking for a month. To your surprise you like it: after the kitten come seedlings, a big pot of your own and talk of a house with room for everyone. Friends can't believe it: “You two? Running a household?” **Your lightness puts down roots, and a happiness grown playfully thrives in your garden.**

Growing up may seem to the Fool a loss of freedom. One settles into the role of homemaker, the other pines for the old carefreeness. Or the care of the home falls on one while the other goes on playing. Grow the home together and playfully: the Empress doesn't mind laughter in her garden.

items.title: A Fool who built a home

captions.B: A reliable home, order and responsibility

items.meaning: Building a reliable home, you keep your lightness.
text: Constancy has never been your strong point: carefree and free, you live for today. The Fool wanders, and the Emperor suggests building a home — not a cage but a base you want to come back to: a steady income, a reserve for a rainy day, clear duties. Your freedom won't vanish because of it; it will become calmer.

Rented flats, work here and there, money spent to the last penny — that is how you lived for years. Yet again a landlady throws you out with a week's notice, and you sleep on a camp bed at friends'. In the morning, for the first time in your lives, you make a plan: a place of your own in three years. It takes four. On moving into your small flat, the first thing you do is hang a hammock — to remember who you are. **Your freedom has a home now, and at last it is at ease there.**

To the Fool walls first seem a cage. One acquires a taste for stability, the other starts to get bored and pulls towards escapades. And if the rules are drawn too tight, the joy goes out of the home. Build a home with the windows flung open: the Emperor needs walls, and the Fool a view of the horizon.

items.title: House rules for free spirits

captions.B: Values of your own and a few traditions

items.meaning: Rules are not your thing, but you invent your own — ones that hold you without stifling.
text: Rules are not your strong point: free and cheerful, you live off the beaten track and are proud of it. The Fool laughs at traditions, and the Hierophant suggests something unexpected — to create your own. Not other people's rules but your values, your customs, what you truly believe in. Even the freest people need something that doesn't change.

You have always laughed at family celebrations, with their obligatory salads and toasts. But it turns out you too miss something of your own — so you invent “Fools' Day”: once a year, on a random day, you drop everything and do something you have never done. A parachute jump, a night in a tent on the roof, a flamenco lesson. Friends are envious and beg to join in. **You create traditions with room for freedom, and they hold you tighter than any rules.**

The Hierophant may frighten the Fool with strictness. One starts demanding order, the other rebels, and an argument about rules turns into a clash of characters. Invent rules cheerfully and together — then you won't want to break them.

items.title: A game that became a choice

captions.B: A real choice and love taken seriously

items.meaning: It all began as a game, and you met to say in earnest “we're a couple” — without losing the fun.
text: It all began lightly for you — cheerfully, with no plans or promises, like a game. The Fool dislikes certainty, and the Lovers demand it: one day you will have to say what you are to each other. Not out of duty but by choice: yes, I want to be with you — seriously. Your lightness won't disappear if this word is added to it.

When friends ask “are you a couple?”, you have long answered with a joke, though you live together. At a friend's birthday, when everyone raises their glasses “to couples”, the other suddenly asks quietly: “And what are we?” The first laughs, then puts down the glass and says in front of everyone: “We're a couple. I love you.” The other laughs and cries at the same time. **Your game becomes a choice and loses not a drop of fun for it.**

Choice seems a cage to the Fool. One is ready to be serious, the other jokes and plays for time, and lightness starts to wound. Worse when the choice is made out of fear of loss rather than love. Talk about what you are to each other directly and with a smile: the Lovers and the Fool get on splendidly as long as choice doesn't cancel freedom.

items.title: Carefree, hands on the wheel

captions.A: Carefree, cheerful, living without a plan
captions.B: Direction, discipline and a shared goal

items.meaning: Adventures are your love, but yours have a steering wheel: a goal, roles and a road to the finish.
text: You usually have no plan: cheerful and carefree, you dash off on escapades and trust to chance. The Fool loves the road for the road's sake, and the Chariot takes the reins: sets a goal, assigns roles, holds the course. The lightness stays, but now it has a steering wheel, and an escapade becomes a journey that leads somewhere.

A cycling trip across the whole of Europe was a dream you kept putting off. At last you set a date: we start in a year. One is in charge of the bikes and gear, the other of the route and money, and for the first time in your lives you keep a spending spreadsheet. Exactly a year later you set off — with a reserve, a map, a plan — and spend the most carefree summer of your lives. **Your carefreeness gets a steering wheel and finally drives where you dreamed of going.**

Discipline may seem boring to the Fool. One starts giving orders, the other rebels and wrecks the plans, and the chariot stands still. Or the goals become too serious, and the joy goes out of the adventure. Set cheerful goals and take turns at the wheel: the Fool holds the course more willingly when he has chosen the route himself.

items.title: A Fool who keeps his word

captions.A: Carefree, cheerful, living for the day
captions.B: Responsibility and honest commitments

items.meaning: Your carefreeness grows up and answers for its words without losing its lightness.
text: Carefreeness is something you share: cheerful and light, you live for the day and dislike obligations. The Fool leaps without thinking of the consequences, and Justice reminds you that the consequences will come all the same. A responsibility that does not kill lightness — that is your shared lesson: keeping your word, paying your bills, thinking about tomorrow, and laughing all the while.

Credit card debts crept up on you unnoticed: a trip here, a present there, a party for friends. A letter comes from the bank, and you no longer feel like laughing. You write out all the debts and make a plan: a year without extra spending and a cheerful rule — celebrate every card paid off with a pizza. The first pizza, for the smallest card, turns out to be the tastiest of your lives. **Your lightness learns to answer for itself and grows freer for it.**

Responsibility may seem a dull cage to the Fool. One takes on everything serious while the other keeps fluttering about, and the first tires of being the adult for two. It's bad too when rules are brought in so strictly that the joy goes out of life. Share responsibility equally and turn it into a game: the Fool keeps his word better when he is having fun.

items.title: A Fool who became a sage

captions.B: Depth and wisdom grown from experience

items.meaning: From all your adventures you draw wisdom, and your Fool is slowly becoming a sage.
text: Living without looking back is your style: cheerful and carefree, you leap into the new without hesitation. The Fool gathers experience but doesn't always have time to make sense of it. The Hermit asks you to stop and think: what of all you have lived through has become wisdom, and what has stayed just an adventure. Depth can grow from your lightness, and the smile will stay.

Over dinner you tell friends the stories of your escapades yet again: jobs walked out on, moves made for a bet, a night on a station floor in a foreign country. A friend suddenly asks: “And what did that teach you?” Silence falls. That night you lie awake for a long time and for the first time seriously go through your stories — and find far more meaning in them than you thought. **Your lightness ripens into wisdom when you allow yourselves to stop and think.**

Depth frightens the Fool with the threat of boredom. One starts to reflect, the other calls them back to adventures and finds the reflection tedious. And thoughtfulness can turn into longing for the old carefreeness. Think cheerfully: wisdom need not be serious, and the Fool knows how to say important things with a smile.

items.title: Beginner's luck

captions.B: Luck that favours the bold

items.meaning: Your courage brings you luck: you go to meet chance together, but you don't push your luck too often.
text: You dive into life without a plan, and people have long noticed that you are lucky. The Fool steps into the void, and the Wheel of Fortune slips a step under his foot. Together you can do what the cautious fear: say “yes” to unexpected offers, start from scratch, believe it will all work out. Your shared luck loves courage, but it also demands respect.

With no experience or connections you decide to start a boat hire on a river where there has never been one. Friends predict failure, the bank turns down a loan. You borrow from family, paint the boats yourselves, make up routes as you go — and on the very first Sunday the boats are all taken by noon, and you sit on the jetty with an empty change tin, laughing. **The wheel loves your courage: where others weigh the risks, you take a step, and luck catches you in mid-air.**

The Fool's luck is not endless. Leap into the unknown time after time, and one day the step won't be there: debts, ruined plans, the hurt of those you let down. Or you can rely on luck so much that you stop preparing and answering for the consequences. Leap boldly, but keep a spare parachute: the wheel turns downwards too.

items.title: Lightness with character

captions.B: Character, discipline and serious intent

items.meaning: Your carefreeness gains character: what you start gets finished, and your word holds.
text: It's fun with you: you start easily, drop things easily and start again just as easily. The Fool gives you a carefreeness many envy. Strength adds what the Fool usually lacks — character: the ability to keep going once it gets boring, a discipline that does not kill joy, serious intent that does not cancel a sense of humour.

Ten times you started learning Spanish and ten times gave up. The eleventh time you agree: twenty minutes every evening, no skipping, and whoever skips does the washing-up for a week. In the first month you take turns at the washing-up. By spring you are watching Spanish series with Spanish subtitles and arguing about who will first get a joke without them. **You are teaching your lightness to hold on, and it no longer flies off at the first gust.**

Strength can scare the Fool if it turns into pressure. “You've given up again” sounds like a verdict, and a free spirit starts hiding from their own promises. It is bad too when one becomes the warden and the other the eternal offender. Keep discipline shared and cheerful: the Fool keeps his word better when he is not threatened but played along with.

items.title: A Fool who learned to wait

captions.B: Patience and readiness to stop for another

items.meaning: Your lightness knows how to stop: to wait, to give and to find meaning in a pause.
text: Cheerful and quick off the mark, you are always rushing about with a new scheme. The Fool lives on impulse and dislikes standing still, and the Hanged Man invites him to hang upside down for a while: to stop, to wait, to give something up for another's sake. For free spirits this is an unexpected lesson, and it is why you met: sometimes the boldest adventure is to stay.

You were about to set off round the world for six months and had already bought the tickets when one of you was asked to take in two nephews while their parents worked abroad. You return the tickets, grumble, laugh at yourselves — and spend a year as accidental parents. Later you call that year the most important journey of your lives. **You discover what eternal wanderers never learn: stopping for someone else can be the boldest step of all.**

A pause comes hard to the Fool, and it is easily mistaken for a cage. One stays out of duty but pines and fumes; the other feels guilty about a sacrifice they never asked for. And sacrifice can become a way of escaping your own decisions: “I gave it up for you.” A stop is valuable when you choose it yourselves; if you feel the pull to move on, agree when you will set off again.

items.title: Starting from zero, laughing

captions.B: Freedom to end the old and begin again

items.meaning: Like a balloon, you let the past go, and a blank page holds no fear for you.
text: Nobody would call you serious: you live as you please, take problems lightly and can laugh where others frown. But in your couple the Fool's lightness serves Death. Many are frozen with fear at closing a chapter, but for you it comes easier: you let the past go like a balloon and look at the blank page with curiosity.

Your café goes under after two years, and instead of a wake you hold a sale with music: you give the chairs away to friends, brew the last coffee on the old machine and laugh at your mistakes. A month later you are already learning to build wooden boats at a friend's boatyard — from scratch, with no experience, eyes shining. **Beside each other an ending holds no fear: you meet it with a joke and look at once to see what begins next.**

Lightness becomes escape when starting from scratch is easier than finishing. As soon as it gets hard, you drop the venture, the city, the agreement without working out what went wrong. Mistakes move house with you, and unpaid debts and unresolved grievances pile up behind. Before starting something new, ask yourselves honestly: are you letting go of the past or running away from it?

items.title: Freedom in the right proportion

captions.B: Measure in freedom and calm reliability

items.meaning: Your freedom goes with reliability: you stay light, but people can count on you.
text: Your freedom is not going anywhere — it is a matter of proportion. The Fool makes you a light, cheerful, slightly reckless couple who live by instinct. Temperance adds what keeps this lightness from shattering: evenness, patience, the ability to wait before deciding. Together you learn to blend spontaneity with reliability, so that life stays an adventure without turning into chaos.

You still dash off on trips with no plan, but now you have an “untouchable envelope” — money that is never spent on any escapade. On one trip the car breaks down in the middle of the steppe three hundred kilometres from home, and the envelope turns a disaster into an adventure with a happy ending: repairs, a night in a hotel, a funny story for friends. **You manage something rare: to stay free and still be people others can rely on.**

Measure frightens the Fool if it sounds like a cage. One starts keeping things in order, and the other takes it as a betrayal of your shared lightness: “you've got boring”. Or one partner's freedom rests on the other's reliability, and that one tires of being the only grown-up in the house. Take turns with the serious stuff: let each of you be reckless sometimes, but not always the same one.

items.title: Lightness that found an anchor

captions.B: Strong attachment and serious success

items.meaning: Your lightness finds an anchor: you grow attached in earnest and pursue big goals.
text: The Fool dislikes anchors, and from outside that is just what you are: carefree, cheerful, living for the day. The Devil brings what the Fool usually runs from — strong attachment and a pull towards big goals: money, a business, standing. In your couple lightness gains weight: you learn to hold on in earnest to each other and to what you have started.

You changed jobs, cities and hobbies so often that friends stopped keeping track of what you were up to. For a laugh you start baking sourdough bread for friends. A month later friends are bringing their friends, and you borrow money for a proper oven and pay it off with a zeal you never knew you had. **Your lightness has at last found something worth holding on to — and holds on in earnest.**

A grip frightens a free person, and they may start running from it. One gets carried away with the business and money, the other feels caged and pulls back towards carefreeness. And attachment can turn jealous: “you're mine, free as you are”. Agree where your freedom lies and where your obligations — then passion won't become a chain, nor lightness an escape.

items.title: Fall down, then laugh

captions.A: Carefree adventurers, quick off the mark
captions.B: The knack of getting up after a fall

items.meaning: Falls will come, and after each one you get up laughing and build something new.
text: You are quick off the mark and take risks easily — a couple of adventurers whom nothing fazes. The Fool leaps without looking, and the Tower shows that a leap does not always end softly. You will have falls. But your lightness is not a weakness but a gift: you can get up after a collapse, dust yourselves off, laugh and start building again.

You put everything into an open-air music festival, and on opening day a downpour washes out the field, the stage sags and the headliner never arrives. The guests scatter, the money is gone. In the evening you sit in a wet tent among the wreckage and laugh until you cry — at yourselves, at the sky, at having picked this of all days. Next morning, still damp, you are already sketching canopies for next time on a napkin. **Your lightness helps you live through any collapse and turn it into a story from which something new begins.**

Carefreeness after a fall can become escape. Instead of working out why it collapsed, you leap into the next adventure, and the collapse repeats. Laugh, but clear the rubble too: the Fool gets up faster when he knows what he tripped over.

items.title: Play that became art

captions.B: A talent that is carried through

items.meaning: Play becomes art in your hands, and what you dream up gets seen through to the end.
text: Your lightness is creative: you play, invent, fantasise, and many think you unserious. The Fool gives the courage to try without fear of looking silly; the Star, the talent and inspiration that grow from that courage. Together you are meant to turn play into art: not to drop what you have dreamed up halfway, but to carry it through until it shines for others too.

The little songs you make up for each other in the kitchen have long been a household tradition. A friend who is a sound engineer hears one and offers to record it “just for fun”. You record it, post it — and a week later it is being sung at children's parties in several cities. For the first time you wonder whether your play could be something more. **Your lightness becomes talent when you stop being shy of what you invent together.**

The Fool quickly loses interest, and the Star needs patience. What you start is dropped as soon as it gets hard, and unfinished schemes pile up around you. See at least one idea through each year: a star is lit not by a plan but by something done.

items.title: A leap into a moonlit night

captions.B: Instinct and imagination you can trust

items.meaning: Into the unknown you leap boldly, but listening to your inner voice.
text: Fear seems unknown to you: carefree and cheerful, you leap into the unknown with a smile. The Fool doesn't look where he steps, and the Moon reminds you that the night road is full of shadows. It calls not for caution but for instinct — an inner voice that tells you where to put your foot. Together you are meant to join lightness with intuition: to leap boldly, but where the heart calls, not just anywhere.

In the middle of a night drive on an unfamiliar road the satnav loses signal. One, laughing, suggests turning at random; the other suddenly says: “Left. I don't know why.” You turn left and half an hour later come out at a small hotel with a lit window, where the last free room is found for you. **Your lightness finds the way when it listens to instinct.**

The Fool may not notice that the Moon is showing him a mirage. Carefreeness leads you into murky situations, and you end up where you did not want to be. Or one partner's fantasies lead you both away from real tasks. Listen to anxiety even while you laugh: sometimes it tells the truth.

items.title: A carefree sun

captions.B: The joy of life and a warm, bright home

items.meaning: You met to turn play and laughter into a sunny home that is warm for everyone who visits.
text: There is a lot of the child in you: cheerful and light, you laugh where others frown. The Fool plays, and the Sun turns that play into real joy: a warm home, celebrations, a success that comes easily because you are not afraid to try. Your couple is like a sunny day: everyone wants to be in it.

Your home is like a playground: a swing on the balcony, fairy lights all year round, board games instead of television. Friends bring their children to you and then stay until late themselves, because “it's so easy at your place”. As they leave, one guest says that after your home they want to live again. **Your lightness becomes a sun that warms everyone who comes to visit.**

Carefreeness can turn into irresponsibility. The party goes on while the bills pile up; fun hides problems nobody wants to talk about. Or one tires of being the grown-up for two. The sun shines on weekdays too: find joy not only in celebrations but in paying the rent on time.

items.title: Free birds build a nest

captions.B: Family, roots and a serious step forward

items.meaning: You dare take serious steps without losing your freedom: free birds acquire a nest.
text: Anchors were never your thing: free and light, you live like birds. The Fool loves the road, and Judgement sounds a call — to family, to roots, to steps that can't be taken halfway. One day you will want a nest. Freedom won't disappear because of it — it will simply gain a place you want to come back to.

For ten years you lived out of suitcases, changing countries and rented flats. At a niece's christening, holding her in their arms, the other suddenly says: “I want a family too. A real one.” The first laughs, but that evening admits they had been thinking the same. You start looking for a house — not for a year but for good — and take your packed rucksacks to the very first viewing, just in case. **You answer the call of family and find that a nest doesn't cancel wings.**

A serious step can frighten the Fool. One is ready, the other plays for time, and the call goes unanswered for years. Or a family is built out of duty to relatives rather than desire, and freedom turns into longing. Answer the call when it is yours: Judgement wakes those who are ready, not those who are hurried.

items.title: From the first step to the goal

captions.B: Completion and a journey travelled in full

items.meaning: You walk the road to the end and build a whole world from it — from the first step to the goal.
text: Nobody begins better than you: light and free, eternal beginners who find everything interesting. The Fool stands at the start of the road, and the World at its end. Your couple travels the road in full: from the first carefree step to a wise fullness in which everything lived through comes together into a whole picture. You are meant not only to begin but to reach the end.

You started out with a rucksack and empty pockets, hitchhiking across half the country. On your anniversary you lay out on the table photos of the whole journey: tents, rented rooms, your first kitchen of your own, friends found along the way. The other says: “We never planned any of it.” The first laughs: “And it all worked out.” **Your road from a carefree start to a whole life is the main thing you have created together.**

The Fool doesn't like endings. What is started is dropped for something new, and the road turns into a string of first steps. Or fullness frightens: “what next, if we have everything?” See at least the main things through to the end: the World awaits those who have walked the whole road, not just started it.

items.title: Two fools in one boat

captions.B: Freedom, trust and joy together

items.meaning: Two free spirits, you stay together without chains: trust instead of checking up.
text: The Fool is doubled in your couple: free and cheerful, you live like two eternal adventurers. You are meant to create what many think impossible: a union with no cage but with loyalty; no checking up but with trust; no plans but with a shared road. Two free people who every morning choose to walk on together.

You plan holidays no more than a week ahead, work here and there, and live in a small flat crammed with guitars and rucksacks. Friends are now envious, now tap their temples. Someone asks whether you aren't afraid. You exchange glances and laugh: “What would scare us is being bored.” **You hold each other not by the hand but by a smile, and that bond is stronger than any chains.**

Two Fools risk not noticing the precipice. One's carefreeness is multiplied by the other's: debts, broken promises, an uncertainty that wounds. And freedom can become an excuse not to talk about the main thing — what you are to each other. Agree on at least two things: money for a rainy day and an honest “I'm with you”. For Fools that is enough.

items.title: A home where everything grows

captions.E: Cosiness, care and shared abundance

items.meaning: The warmth between you is homely and practical: you look after each other, and your shared well-being grows in your hands.
text: Everything grows under your hands: flowers on the windowsill, your means, shared plans, even the cat you once took in as a scrawny kitten. The Empress fills your home with care and warmth: a good dinner, order that doesn't feel like a barracks, chores done together and with pleasure. In a home like this you can be a little spoiled, and you allow each other that weakness.

Your Sunday mornings smell of pie: one kneads the dough, the other slices apples and argues about how much cinnamon to add. Then the two of you go round the market, choose seedlings for the balcony and come home with bags full of things you could easily have done without. **Your closeness shows in care: a laid table, a warm blanket, a shared venture growing day by day.**

Abundance spoils when people start measuring it. Who earns more, who puts more into the home, who has “fallen behind” — and care turns into rivalry, and cosiness into a field for reproaches. Give thanks for small things aloud: in a garden not watered with attention, nothing grows.

items.title: A fortress from the inside

captions.E: Reliability, protection and order at home

items.meaning: Dependable order and a sense of protection hold you: behind outward reserve lie respect, passion and faith in each other.
text: From outside your home looks like a fortress: reserved and sparing with words, you don't open up to outsiders. Inside, though, it is warm and safe. The Emperor gives you both a sense of protection: each knows the other will cover for them, back them up, not abandon them at a hard moment. Behind the strictness hide respect and passion; you simply don't put them on show.

On Friday one partner's important project collapses, and they come home in silence. The other asks no unnecessary questions: puts dinner on, then gets out a notebook: “Let's go point by point — what can be saved?” By midnight you have a plan; by Monday half the problem is solved. **Your closeness lies in the certainty that beside you is someone who won't lose their head and will watch your back.**

Order suffocates when it turns into a rulebook one person lives by. Rules multiply, decisions are made without discussion, nit-picking is heard more often than praise, and the other starts toeing the line. Keep the fortress open on the inside: speak about feelings as clearly as about plans, and revisit the rules together.

items.title: A charter of your own

captions.E: Trust, shared views and loyalty to your own ways

items.meaning: You trust each other as people who believe in the same things: friends, allies and keepers of shared rules.
text: You do not only love each other — you are also kindred spirits. The Hierophant gives you a shared footing: similar views on what is honest and what matters, loyalty, a habit of helping without being asked. You always have something to talk about, and you argue more like two students over a book than like opponents. Authority in the house is not seized but recognised: whoever knows a subject better is listened to willingly.

You have small rituals of your own: a Sunday pancake breakfast, a walk in the first snow, a letter to each other on your anniversary. Nobody invented them on purpose; they grew by themselves and now hold the week together the way a frame holds up a house. **Your closeness stands on a shared charter that the two of you wrote and keep not out of duty but because it is yours.**

The charter weighs on you when one starts reading it to the other like a sermon. “That's not how it's done”, “I know better what's right” — the lecture comes from the best intentions but sounds like a verdict. The other's opinion stops being taken seriously at home, and the argument is no longer about the matter but about who here guards the truth. The one being lectured falls silent — not from agreement but from weariness.

items.title: Speaking from the heart aloud

captions.E: Openness, tenderness and choosing each other daily

items.meaning: There are no secrets and plenty of tenderness between you — so words need care when feelings take over.
text: There are almost no closed doors between you. The Lovers fill your relationship with sincerity: you tell each other everything, touch each other in passing for no reason, and accept in the other the imperfections they hide from everyone else. Decisions, even small ones, you make together — which bread to buy, where to go at the weekend — because the other's opinion truly interests you.

Monday morning: one is still half asleep, the other brings coffee and sits on the edge of the bed to tell a dream. Five minutes late for work, but you both smile all day. In the evening you share the day in the same detail and really listen. **Your closeness is built from hundreds of small confidences, and each one is a way of choosing each other.**

Openness wounds when in the heat of a quarrel words fly not wide but straight to the mark. You know everything about each other, and that knowledge easily becomes a weapon: one phrase thrown out in anger cancels a week of tenderness. Decisions made on emotion have to be reversed later. Peace gives way to war, war to peace, and you both tire of these swings, though the love does not go anywhere.

items.title: A course set by two

captions.E: Movement, passion and a shared course

items.meaning: You live at the pace of a journey: always moving, deciding quickly and together, though each needs a path of their own too.
text: Sitting still is hard for you, and you don't try. The Chariot sets your pace: something is always starting — a move, a project, a hike, a new passion. For all the speed, your roles are clear and your joint decisions quick, and if someone close to you is wronged, you leap to their defence before you have had time to discuss it. Each has their own path outside the home, and it does not drive you apart but gives you something to tell each other in the evening.

The decision to buy an old van and convert it for road trips is made over one dinner. A month later it stands in the yard; one is in charge of the engine, the other of the route and budget, and at weekends you are already touring the region. **Your closeness is born in motion: you are most together when you are travelling the same way, each in their own seat.**

Speed becomes pressure when one starts steering for both. They decide where to go, hurry, don't ask, and the other either submits or yanks the reins — and conflict flares up over nothing. The other's successes stir not joy but envy, tiredness stirs irritation. The Chariot races on, only you draw the strength for it from each other and never have time to replenish it.

items.title: Scales that never lie

captions.E: Honesty, reliability and an equal share from both

items.meaning: An honest order reigns in your home: promises are kept, duties split equally, and arguments stay calm and to the point.
text: You know what to expect from each other, and that knowledge calms you. Justice sets up an honest order in your home: what is said gets done, duties are divided so that nobody feels hard done by, and complaints stick to the matter, without drama. Your heads are cool, your hearts hot: the passion has not gone anywhere, it simply does not give orders when you decide.

On the fridge hangs a list: who pays the rent this month, who collects the parcels, who rings grandma on Wednesdays. Friends chuckle at your bookkeeping, but you have not quarrelled over chores for years. When one cannot cope, the other takes over their line without reproach, and the debt is repaid just as calmly. **You are at ease together because each is sure their contribution is seen and weighed fairly.**

The scales tip when honesty is replaced by counting. Each remembers who did how much, and any request sounds like a debt. Promises are put off “until later”, and the other waits without reminding — and stores it up. Feelings fit poorly into such a system: they can't be split down the middle. The order at home is perfect, but there is less and less warmth, and nobody can say on whose side of the scales the fault lies.

items.title: Two windows in one house

captions.E: Quiet, trust and each one's right to solitude

items.meaning: A quiet understanding lives between you: love shows in deeds, and each has a right to their own corner and thoughts.
text: There are few loud declarations between you, but plenty of attention to small things. The Hermit keeps things quiet between you: each has a right to their own corner and their own hours alone, and it does not hurt the other. Love here is shown in deeds — a cup of tea brought in, a lamp mended — and important matters are discussed unhurriedly and not before both have thought them through.

Evening, and the flat is quiet: one reads in an armchair, the other is building a model sailing ship in the next room. For an hour nobody says a word, and both are content. Then one comes in with two mugs and asks how the mast is coming along — and the conversation stretches until midnight. **You don't need to be side by side all the time to be close: your silence is shared even when you are in different rooms.**

Silence becomes a wall when you retreat to your room to avoid a conversation. Hurt goes unspoken, a problem goes unnamed, each solves it alone, silently, and announces the conclusion ready-made. The other is the last to learn of anything important. Together it grows chilly, apart it is frightening, and you live like two hermits under one roof: each with their own lantern and not a single shared fire.

items.title: A meeting that was meant to be

captions.E: A sense of fate, a shared rhythm, meeting change well

items.meaning: You share a sense of a destined meeting: a common rhythm, gratitude and a habit of facing fate's turns together.
text: From the very start you felt this meeting was no accident. The Wheel of Fortune gives you a shared rhythm: you see life in a similar way, get carried away by the same things and accept each other in any state — on a lucky day and on a disastrous one. There is a lot of gratitude between you: for having met, for the luck, for the other being there.

You are both made redundant in the same month. Another couple would start working out who is to blame, but you spend the first evening joking about “a sign from above” and the second over a map of the country. A week later the fridge holds a map with three circles and lists of vacancies in each of the three cities, and neither of you mentions blame. **You meet each turn of the wheel together, and for you change is not a misfortune but the next chapter.**

The wheel rocks you when you start blaming each other or fate for the changes. Luck turns away — and instead of a conversation comes “you're the one who dragged us here”. The mood jumps from quiet to quarrel, each waits for things to sort themselves out, and problems pile up, left to drift. Something still holds you together, but it grows harder to remember what.

items.title: Sparks from two flints

captions.E: Passion, jealousy and a clash of characters

items.meaning: Two strong characters spark between you: you argue in earnest, give way by choice, and the heat turns into passion.
text: You are two strong characters, and neither intends to become a shadow. Strength runs a hot current between you: you charge each other, flare up at the slightest word and sense keenly when the other needs support and when a challenge. Tension doesn't build up but turns into passion, and that keeps you alive even after many years.

An argument about where to see in the New Year starts at breakfast and by lunch is a matter of principle: both have dug in, both are right. Then one laughs first — “fine, you win, but next year I choose” — and the heat goes not into resentment but into a kiss. **Your closeness runs hot because it brings together two people who don't bend but choose to give way.**

The fire burns when an argument turns into a fight for the throne. What matters is no longer resolving it but winning: who is louder, who is in charge, whose truth weighs more. Jealousy becomes a way to test your power, mockery a weapon. The loser of a round saves strength for the next, and home becomes a ring where both are tired but neither can be the first to drop their guard.

items.title: A love that knows how to wait

captions.E: Self-sacrifice, waiting and a testing of feelings

items.meaning: Yours is a love that can wait: you put the other's need first, and feelings grow stronger for being tested by time.
text: Your closeness builds slowly, and there is no point rushing it. The Hanged Man teaches you to see things from the other's side: you give way, listen, put the other's need ahead of your own and sense each other even at a distance. Much here is tested by waiting — a declaration, a decision, a shared step — and you know how to wait without losing warmth.

Your partner is offered six months' work in another city, and you decide not to go together. Every evening a call, at weekends long letters with more tenderness in them than in many face-to-face talks. When they come back, it turns out you have lost nothing, only learned to understand each other by your pauses. **For you, feelings that have survived waiting are stronger than those that were never tested.**

The test turns into sacrifice when it is always the same one who gives. They forget about themselves for the other's sake, then wait for gratitude that doesn't come and keep a silent tally: “I've done so much for you…” The other feels guilty but doesn't understand what for. The waiting stretches on with no end date, decisions are put off, and both freeze in a place where no one leaves and no one truly lives.

items.title: Several lives of one union

captions.E: Constant change, crises and renewed feelings

items.meaning: Your union keeps being reborn: you let the old couple run its course and build the next one together.
text: You don't owe it to each other to stay who you were when you met: if one outgrows their former self, the other does not demand them back but gets to know them anew. Death transforms not only each of you but the union itself. Habits, roles, even the way you make up one day stop fitting, and then the couple you used to be has to die away — otherwise the new one has nowhere to be born.

One of you has gone back to study: notes in the evenings, classes on Saturdays, and the old couple who went everywhere together no longer fits into the week. You could cling to it, resenting the empty chair opposite. Instead you admit that couple is gone and build a new one: each has an evening of their own, but Sunday morning is shared and sacred. **You don't repair change like a breakdown: you let the old union live out its time and give birth to the next one together.**

It is harder when you are ready to be reborn at different speeds. One already lives the new way and hurries the next change, while the other is still saying goodbye to the last one, and the goodbye hurts. The harder one tries to remake the other for the new life, the tighter the other clings to the old. The new has no time to take root, the old is not fully let go, and a draught runs through the house: the door to the past is not yet shut, and the next one is already flung open.

items.title: Water blended drop by drop

captions.E: Calm, patience and gently growing closer

items.meaning: The warmth between you is steady: you grow closer drop by drop, settle things before they become rows and treasure peace.
text: You grow closer not in a rush but gradually, the way two waters of different temperatures are mixed: little by little, until it is even. Temperance sets a calm tone for you both — patience, the ability to wait out a flare-up, the habit of reaching agreement before it comes to an argument. Peace of mind is dearer to you than any purchase, and the warmth between you neither burns nor cools, but holds.

One of you wants a seaside holiday, the other the mountains, and instead of a quarrel a third option appears: a week by a lake with both water and trails. Nobody gave in completely, and nobody lost. In the evening you sit on the jetty in silence, and the silence is light. **Your harmony was not given at once: you blend it yourselves, drop by drop, and that is why it lasts for years.**

Evenness deceives when it is always the same one doing the blending. They smooth things over, give way, adjust — and one day discover that none of their own taste is left in the shared water. The other sincerely doesn't notice the imbalance: after all, everything is calm. Then silence stops being peace and becomes cold: difficult things go unsaid so as not to upset the balance, and it grows harder to understand what keeps you together.

items.title: A magnet that won't let go

captions.E: Wild passion, temptation and dependence

items.meaning: The pull between you outweighs reason: no desire is hidden, and “you're mine” must never mean “you belong to me”.
text: You are drawn to each other more strongly than reason suggests, and this pull does not ask permission. The Devil holds you tighter than any argument: the attraction does not weaken side by side, in a quarrel, or when it would be wiser to retreat to separate rooms. On the plus side this is courage: you are not ashamed of your desires, you name them out loud and accept in the other the darkness they show no one else.

One of you confesses what they have kept quiet for years: they have long wanted to quit a safe job for a risky venture. The other does not wince or moralise but asks, “How much do you need to give it a try?” — and that same evening you work out what to cut back on. **Your closeness rests on the fact that here you can want things in earnest and hide not a single desire.**

The pull turns dark when “you're mine” starts to mean “you belong to me”. A call from an unknown number demands an explanation, an evening with friends a report. Quarrels die out in an embrace, but none of them gets resolved: making up with passion is easier than agreeing in words. You stay together because tearing yourselves apart is impossible, and you ask yourselves less and less often whether you are good together.

items.title: A storm that clears the air

captions.E: Rows, shattered illusions and sudden change

items.meaning: Between you is the honesty of a storm: what is false collapses in a row, and what survives keeps you side by side.
text: Nothing false lives long between you. The Tower brings down whatever is built on assumptions: a convenient silence, a prettified image of your partner, an agreement neither of you has kept for ages. It brings it down loudly — with a row, a slammed door, a decision made in a single evening. But whatever survives the blow you no longer test for strength: it is real, and in trouble you stand shoulder to shoulder faster than most.

For six months you pretended that moving for one partner's job suited you both. Over dinner the other suddenly puts down the fork and says what has been building up: “I can't breathe here.” Voices crack, the balcony door slams, by midnight you are both hoarse — and in the morning, for the first time, you sit down honestly to work out how to move back. **In your home an illusion does not live long: the first storm sweeps it away, and on the cleared ground you build something that will hold.**

It is dangerous when the storm becomes a habit. A row starts working as a lever: “then I'm leaving” is said not in earnest but to make the other give in, and each time it comes easier. A barb hits the most vulnerable spot, because you know exactly where it is. After a quarrel the wreckage is not cleared, you simply go on living among it, until you start bracing for the next blow before it lands.

items.title: A sky you both reach for

captions.E: Romance, big dreams and idealising your partner

items.meaning: Between you is romance and faith in each other: each sees a light in the other they have not yet noticed in themselves.
text: Beside each other you want to be better than you are. The Star fills you both with hope: each sees in the other who they could become, and says so out loud. Dreams are never mocked here — they are written down, discussed in the kitchen past midnight and tried on as if they had already come true. Tenderness is no cause for embarrassment, at home or in public.

One of you mentions in passing that they used to paint as a teenager. A week later there are brushes on the windowsill, and the other hangs the first clumsy study in the hallway, in the most visible spot, and shows it to guests with as much pride as if it were a museum piece. **You look at each other as at the stars: you notice a light the other has not yet seen in themselves.**

The light blinds when an image replaces the living person. The partner in your dreams is always inspired, tender and understands without words, while the real one gets tired, forgets, wants quiet — and disappointment sounds like a reproach: “You've changed.” One starts playing a role to measure up, the other tries to fit their partner to the picture. The beautiful story goes on, but there is less and less of the two of you in it.

items.title: Sensing through the dark

captions.E: Secrets, fears and emotional swings

items.meaning: You sense each other without words: you read each other's moods, and fears melt once a secret is brought into the open.
text: Much happens between you without words. The Moon makes you sensitive to each other: you guess the other's mood from the way they put down a cup, and you know when to ask and when to leave them be. But the same Moon brings fog — anxiety with no visible cause, a mood that turns into its opposite by evening. Each of you keeps a dark room of your own, and that is not necessarily a threat: it is how each of you keeps a little mystery.

Your partner came home late and is silent. You could imagine anything — you both have rich imaginations — and by midnight a whole novel has grown out of that silence. Or you can sit down beside them and ask. It turns out they were dressed down at work in front of everyone and felt too ashamed to talk about it. **Your fears melt when a secret is brought into the shared light rather than left for the imagination to finish.**

The swings go higher when what you imagined is taken for the truth. One is hurt by something that never happened, the other doesn't understand why they are being punished with coldness — and now each expects a catch. A confession made in a moment of closeness resurfaces in a quarrel as a reproach, and nobody wants to confide any more. You still sense each other without words, only now what you sense is wariness.

items.title: Joy for no reason

captions.E: Happiness, vivid feelings and family joy

items.meaning: There is a lot of joy between you: you laugh, praise and celebrate each other's wins more loudly than your own.
text: You are warm beside each other, and the warmth shows even on an ordinary Tuesday. The Sun fills your home with joy: you laugh a lot, praise easily and celebrate each other's small victories louder than your own. One feels protected by the other, each succeeds in their own field, and so home becomes a place you want to get back to early.

On Friday one of you gets a bonus, and the evening turns into a party: a cake from the nearest bakery on the table, favourite music playing, someone already phoning the parents to boast. A month later the other has a reason — and the celebration repeats on the same scale. **With you, one partner's joy is not halved but doubled: every success becomes a shared light in the house.**

The Sun burns when brightness is no longer enough without comparison. Joy at a partner's success gives way to jealous counting: who brought in more, who gets more praise. Care becomes control — “I know better whom you should be friends with” — and the warm home grows cramped. From outside your couple still shines, but inside one of you more and more often feels too hot to breathe.

items.title: A past that asks to be heard

captions.E: The return of the past and fateful changes

items.meaning: Your union has a long memory: the past returns to be sorted out and forgiven, and calls you to finish what you began.
text: Your union has a long memory. Judgement raises what seemed closed: old grievances, family stories, long-postponed decisions. It returns not to torment you but so that it can finally be sorted out and forgiven. After such conversations you wake up a little different — and it is often then that you decide on something that changes your life: to marry, to move, to invite your parents to live with you.

In a box of documents one of you finds the notes you wrote each other in your first year. In the evening you read them aloud, laugh at the grand phrases and suddenly fall silent at the line “I want a house by the river”. A month later you are already driving out to view plots. **The past doesn't pull you back: it reminds you who you meant to become together and calls you to finish what you started.**

It is hard when the past returns without forgiveness. An old mistake surfaces in every quarrel — “remember how you…” — and an argument about unwashed dishes turns into a trial of your whole history. Each waits for the other to admit guilt first. Decisions that are due drown in going over old ones, and the house grows cold, though nobody is going anywhere.

items.title: A map with room for two

captions.E: Harmony, growing together and a strong union

items.meaning: There is room for both of you: you see things alike, share duties equally and look for solutions that fit two.
text: Your union has room for both of you — for how you are alike and for how you differ. The World gives you the sense of a life that has come together: you see things similarly, talk a lot, share duties equally and don't push each other. A quarrel for you is not a reason to establish who is right but a task: to find a solution with room for you both.

One has dreamed all their life of living by the sea, the other can't imagine life without a big city. For years this looked like a dead end, until you sat down with a map and found a seaside city with a university, a theatre and work for both. You prepare the move like an expedition: a spreadsheet, deadlines, who brings what. **Your union grows because you widen every new step until it fits two.**

The whole grows dim when one starts building the world to their own blueprint. The other's views are quietly corrected — “you'll thank me later” — their hobbies called pointless, their friends unnecessary. It can go the other way: everything is arranged so well that the days become identical, and in the finished world nothing is left to grow. From outside the union is strong, but inside there is less and less air.

items.title: Two with the door left open

captions.E: Freedom, adventure and an unpredictable relationship

items.meaning: Between you is freedom and friendship: nobody demands an account, and you choose each other every morning, not out of duty.
text: What holds you is not obligation but the wish to be close, and you both know it. The Fool lets air into your relationship: each is free in their own pursuits, neither demands a report, and you are friends in the same way as you are lovers. Here you can dash off on a trip on a Friday evening, change careers at forty and own up to the silliest thing you have ever done — the other will laugh and not judge.

On Saturday morning one of you says: “Shall we go somewhere?” — and an hour later you are on a local train with no plan, a flask and a packet of biscuits. You will be back late, with wet feet and a story you will retell to friends for years. **Your closeness lives in freedom: you choose each other anew every morning, and there is not a drop of duty in that choice.**

Freedom turns into emptiness when neither dares to name what is between you. Are you together — or just side by side? Building something shared — or living like flatmates with a good sense of humour? The serious talk is put off because it will “spoil everything”, and at the first hard turn it is easier for each to go their own way than to stay. The adventure goes on, but you are no longer sure you are in the same boat.

captions.dual: Caring and making things grow

items.meaning: Both of you are keepers of plenty: caring, generous, fond of growing things and making a home cosy.
text: At heart you are both gardeners. The Empress has given you both care, generosity, a love of beauty and comfort, the knack of growing things: children, a home, a business, a garden on the windowsill. You both understand why the table should be full and the home warm, and you are equally glad when something you planted begins to bloom. Care turns into rivalry when both want to be in charge of it: who cooks better, who puts in more, who brings up the children better — and what was meant to bring joy becomes a field for jealousy.

captions.dual: Building, keeping your word, answering

items.meaning: Each of you is a natural head of the household: responsible, solid, used to building and defending your own.
text: Your characters are cut from the same stone. The Emperor gives you both responsibility, order, the ability to build and defend: a home, a business, your people. For both of you a plan matters more than a mood, and you keep your word even when it's inconvenient. Both of you can be relied on, and you know it. Only two masters can find one house cramped: each is used to giving orders, and an argument about where to put the wardrobe turns into an argument about who is in charge.

captions.dual: Honouring the same sacred things

items.meaning: Your characters ring with the same note: what is honest, what is sacred, and which words are never taken back.
text: You don't need to agree on fundamentals: you share one tuning fork. With the Hierophant in your make-up, you live by a shared faith and test actions by it: what is acceptable, what is never allowed whatever happens, what is worth giving up comfort for. When a serious choice comes, you know in advance what the other will choose. The harmony goes off key when each speaks as if they held the whole truth: “I know what's right for you”. Then two sermons sound, and neither hears the other.

captions.dual: Living by the heart and choosing love

items.meaning: At heart you are both romantics: you decide with the heart, value beauty and choose people over gain.
text: Deep down you are made alike: you both decide with the heart. The Lovers at the core of a character make a person open, warm, sensitive to beauty and to how they are treated. You both know that tone matters more than words and that you choose people, not profit. You are equally able to admire — and equally quick to hurt each other with a careless word. The danger is that both expect love to be proved and take offence in silence: two sensitive hearts notice a chill sooner than others — and close up sooner.

captions.dual: Racing in one harness

items.meaning: By nature you are both fighters: decisive, active and unable to stand still.
text: You recognise the same spring in each other. Built like the Chariot, you live in motion, set a goal and take it, decide fast and stand up for your own. The other understands without being told why something begun can't be put off, and why defeat stings more than victory delights. Together you don't brake; you accelerate. Trouble begins when two strong characters are cramped in one rut: each wants to steer, and the team starts pulling in different directions.

captions.dual: Measuring the world by honesty

items.meaning: You are cut from the same cloth: you both put honesty above convenience and keep your word even when it's awkward.
text: Your characters rest on one support — honesty. Justice at the core gives you both directness, a sense of measure and respect for agreements: said it — do it; borrowed — return it; got it wrong — admit it. You trust each other without needless checks because you know the worth of your own word, and you argue briefly and to the point. Honesty becomes harshness when each is sure their yardstick is the only right one: then an argument turns into a trial in which both are prosecutors and judges, and neither is ready to admit that scales can differ.

captions.dual: Thinking in quiet and getting to the heart

items.meaning: Your characters are alike in depth: you both think slowly, say little and value the right to be alone.
text: You are both people of depth. The Hermit teaches you both to think first and speak after, to look for the heart of things rather than the glitter, to guard your time and your quiet. Beside each other you rest: nobody demands endless conversation or takes offence if an evening passes in silence. Each respects the other's “I need to think”. Silence estranges when you both withdraw at the same time: hard things are settled alone, feelings go unspoken, and a home so good for thinking becomes too quiet for two.

captions.dual: Meeting change with a light step

items.meaning: Change comes easily to you both: you seize chances, decide quickly and believe in luck.
text: You are both people unafraid of change. The Wheel of Fortune at the core of a character makes a person flexible and quick off the mark: changing job, city or passion is not a tragedy but a new chapter. You don't have to talk each other into a risky turn: the other is already packing a bag. You both believe luck comes to those who are ready, and you both get back up quickly after a fall. Lightness lets you down when you both drift with the current: decisions are put off “until a sign”, problems are left to drift, and in a bad patch each blames fate — and a little the other.

captions.dual: Holding firm and never giving in

items.meaning: You are both strong natures: persistent, passionate, able to take a blow and not give in.
text: You recognise each other by strength of character. Strength at the core gives you both persistence, passion and endurance: not giving in, seeing things through, keeping hold of yourself when others break down. Beside someone equally strong you don't have to pretend to be weaker than you are — a rare relief. You admire each other and charge each other up for big things. Hardest of all is when two stubborn wills butt heads: each is sure that giving way means losing, and an argument over a trifle becomes a duel of characters.

captions.dual: Seeing life differently

items.meaning: A special outlook unites you: you both know how to wait, to feel for others and to see what others miss.
text: You both look at life a little differently from everyone else. The Hanged Man gives you patience, compassion, readiness to help and the ability to see a situation from an unexpected side. You don't need to explain to each other why it is sometimes better to wait than to act, or why helping a friend matters more than your own gain. Even at a distance you sense how the other is. Patience grows heavy when you both get used to sacrificing: each gives way and waits for the other to notice, and in a couple where nobody asks anything for themselves a quiet resentment builds.

captions.dual: Letting go of the old and changing

items.meaning: You are both unafraid of change: you can close chapters, let go of the past and start with a clean slate.
text: You can both do what frightens many: close chapters. Death at the heart of your characters gives the courage to change, a readiness to let go of the outworn and start again without looking back. The other doesn't judge leaving a secure job or breaking with the past: they would have done the same. You accept each other with all your baggage and aren't afraid that the other will change. Change rocks you when it becomes a habit: you both strain to renew everything in sight, and nothing constant is left in your union to lean on when times are hard.

captions.dual: Seeking the middle and smoothing things

items.meaning: Your characters share a sense of measure: both calm, patient, good at agreeing and averse to extremes.
text: You are both built on the law of measure. Temperance is the core of both characters: calm, patience, the ability to agree and find the middle where others break lances. It is easy for the two of you: nobody makes scenes, arguments are settled by talking, and life runs evenly, without jolts. You both value peace of mind above outward glitter. Peace becomes stagnation when you both cherish it so much that you stop talking about unpleasant things: discontent is smoothed over, strong feelings hidden, and the even surface conceals what should have been discussed long ago.

captions.dual: Wanting hard and getting it

items.meaning: You share a strength of desire: both passionate, ambitious and unafraid of your dark sides.
text: At the core you share one passion. The Devil in both your characters means strong desires, grip, ambition and honesty about your own dark side. You aren't ashamed to want a lot and don't judge each other for bold dreams and expensive pleasures. Beside someone equally strong you can be wholly yourself — with your zeal, your jealousy, your thirst for success. It is dangerous when two strong desires start pulling each other to extremes: competition, control, a struggle for power — and neither wants to be the first to loosen their grip.

captions.dual: Breaking the old and building anew

items.meaning: You were both made for stormy weather: blunt, honest, able to bring down the outworn and build again.
text: Your characters were tempered in the same fire. The Tower at the core makes a person direct, decisive and steadfast in trouble: unafraid to tear down what has outlived itself and build something new in its place. You are both calm when everything around is falling apart, and both intolerant of falseness — better a bitter truth than a pretty lie. An explosion comes when two storms meet in one quarrel: both speak harshly, strike where it hurts most, and what is said at such moments stays in the memory for a long time.

captions.dual: Dreaming and inspiring

items.meaning: You are both dreamers: creative, sincere and inspiring to those around you.
text: You are both people who glow from within. The Star at the core means dreaminess, a creative streak, sincerity and a hope that doesn't go out after failures.
