You inspire each other and both understand why it's worth staying up all night for an idea and why a dream matters more than “being sensible”. In such a couple each becomes a little better. The dream deceives when you both live more by it than by deeds: beautiful plans multiply but rarely come true, and each waits for the other to get down to earth.

captions.dual: Feeling more than is said

items.meaning: You are alike in sensitivity: you both feel finely, fantasise a lot and live by intuition.
text: You both have thin skin. The Moon at the core of a character gives sensitivity, a rich imagination and an intuition that often runs ahead of words. You understand each other by a tone, a pause, the way the other put down a cup. A mood spoilt by a single look, or a dream before dawn, is no trifle to either of you. Sensitivity frightens when two anxieties start feeding each other: each fills in the other's thoughts, fears grow in silence, and one thing left unsaid turns into a story that never happened.

captions.dual: Shining and warming others

items.meaning: There is a lot of warmth in you both: open, generous and life-loving, you like it bright around you.
text: You are both sunny people. The Sun in a character means openness, generosity, a love of life and a wish for brightness all around: guests, celebrations, success you want to share. You don't dim each other; you blaze up: one partner's joy is caught by the other. It is easy for you to praise, thank and be proud of each other aloud. Only two suns can find one sky cramped: each wants to be at the centre, successes start being compared, and warmth imperceptibly gives way to rivalry for attention.

captions.dual: Holding on to your own and your kin

items.meaning: Your characters share roots: you both hold on to family, remember where you come from and know how to forgive.
text: Your characters have similar roots. Judgement at the core makes a person family-minded in a deep sense: loyal to their own, mindful of the family line and its traditions, able to forgive and start again. You both understand why you can't miss grandmother's birthday and why peace with a brother matters more than any job. You back each other even when the other is wrong. Roots start to hold too tightly when you both live with an eye on your relatives: decisions about your life together are made with the elders' opinion in mind, and your own voice drowns in the family chorus.

captions.dual: Seeing the world wide, without borders

items.meaning: You are on the same scale: you both think broadly, are open to the new and want to live in a whole, not in fragments.
text: Your characters are on the same scale. From the World you both have a broad outlook, an interest in other cultures and people, a pull towards wholeness: for life to be gathered together and things seen through. You understand each other in talk about big things — the future, meaning, how the world works — and you are equally relaxed about other people's oddities. Breadth turns into stubbornness when each has a finished picture of the world of their own and neither is ready to budge: two world views argue instead of combining into a shared one.

captions.dual: Living lightly and starting from zero

items.meaning: You are two free birds: light, quick to laugh, ready to start from zero and unable to bear cages.
text: Lightness is what you share. The Fool at the root of your characters means freedom, humour, readiness to start from scratch and leap into the unknown without calculating every step. You don't keep each other on a short leash or make tragedies out of mistakes: a cup is broken — that's lucky; a plan fails — we'll think of another. It's fun with the two of you, for you and for everyone around. Carefreeness takes its toll when neither takes on the dull and serious: bills, commitments, hard conversations are put off until they all come down at once.

captions.semidual: Wanting to grow something of your own

items.meaning: Above all, you both want to make things grow — a home, a family, prosperity, life.
text: You both want things to grow around you. The Empress gives you both one dream: a warm home, a full table, a garden, a family, a prosperity you can see and touch. When one suggests getting a dog or a plot of land, the other is already working out where the vegetable beds will go. A shared dream weighs on you when you want to grow everything at once: the garden, the renovation, the dog, another room — and amid all the shared bustle nobody notices that the two of you have long needed a rest.

items.meaning: Your desires sound in unison: you both want love, beauty and for everything to be decided together.
text: You both want the same thing — a love in which everything is beautiful. The Lovers give you both similar dreams: dates, attention, tenderness, a beautiful home and decisions made together, even small ones. You are equally delighted by flowers for no reason and equally expect your anniversary to be remembered. Identical desires become a trap when you share one picture of ideal love: an evening that doesn't match the dream disappoints you both at once, and there is no one to say that it's fine as it is.

items.meaning: In what matters most you want the same: quiet, depth and the right to find your own answers.
text: You want the same things — and they aren't noisy parties. The Hermit shapes both your desires: quiet, space of your own, a long talk about what matters, knowledge found for yourselves. You don't have to explain to the other why an evening alone is rest, not a slight, or why a book sometimes matters more than guests. A shared hunger for meaning lets you down when the search for answers postpones life itself: both want to understand first and decide later, and important things — a home, work, shared plans — wait for years for someone to finish thinking.

captions.semidual: Wanting to give and to live differently

items.meaning: Your desires are in tune: you both want to help, to give and to see life differently from most.
text: Your desires coincide — and rarely with what most people want. You are both drawn where the Hanged Man is drawn: to help without counting, to live by rules of your own that others don't always understand, to stop now and then and look at everything from another angle. Neither of you will ask why a holiday was cancelled for a friend or a lucrative offer turned down. Shared generosity grows heavy when others start counting on your “help without counting”: relatives and friends get used to taking, you are both equally bad at saying no, and there is less and less strength left for your own life.

items.meaning: Your desires match in strength and daring: you both want passion, success and freedom to own your appetites.
text: What one wants, the other wants too — and just as strongly. The Devil's desires are shared between you: passion, excitement, the good life, a success you aren't ashamed to name aloud. You don't have to talk each other into a bold plan or apologise for an expensive pleasure: the other wants the same and doesn't judge. The match becomes dangerous when two strong desires start spurring each other on with no brakes: more, faster, riskier — and nobody to say “stop”.

items.meaning: You have similar dreams: you are both drawn to mystery, depth and an understanding that needs no words.
text: Your desires meet where others don't look. The Moon gives you both the same dreams: mystery, deep closeness, intuitive understanding, a world of fantasy where only your own are let in. You guess each other's wishes from a single glance and often want the same thing at the same moment — to go away, to fall silent, to start something strange. Instinct lets you down when you stop checking guesses with words: you think the other wants the same, but they want something else, and you both silently take offence at what never happened.

items.meaning: You want life on the same scale: one city is too small for you both, and everything beyond the horizon calls.
text: Your desires are the same size — big. The World rings through both your desires: travel, new countries and people, a sense of life as whole and wide, without needless borders. The other meets a suggestion to move away for a year or learn a third language not with “why?” but with “when?”. A shared horizon lets you down when it hides what is close by: you both dream of the faraway, while home, money and everyday life are left without anyone in charge — and each expects the other to see to them.

items.title: Frank only with each other

captions.A: A reserved couple who keep much to themselves

items.meaning: In public you are reserved and sparing with words, at home frank: people guess about you, but only you know the truth.
text: In public you are one way, at home another. The High Priestess makes you reserved and a little mysterious: you take neither quarrels nor tenderness out in public, you keep much to yourselves, and guesses spring up around you. Yet between yourselves you are honest and talk about everything heart to heart. Often you are opposites who complement each other so precisely that from outside it looks like a secret pact.

For years one partner's colleagues don't know you are together: at office parties you stay polite and apart. When the truth comes out, the office buzzes for a week, while you calmly go on talking late into the night in the kitchen, as you always have. **People see a closed door and never guess how warm and frank it is behind it.**

Reserve in public can turn into coldness at home too. The unspoken piles up, feelings are suppressed, and everyone sees the “together — apart” swings, but no one knows why. Sometimes you discuss each other with outsiders while staying silent with each other. The Priestess wants your life to stay a mystery to the world — not your feelings a mystery to each other.

items.title: Hosts of the big table

captions.A: A house-proud, generous couple of ample means

items.meaning: To outsiders you look prosperous: a generous table, a cosy home, a smooth-running household and warmth enough for guests.
text: Your well-being shows from the doorstep. The Empress shows people a smooth-running household, a cosy home and a generous table you would not be ashamed to invite anyone to. It is clear that you respect each other — not for show but in small things: the way one passes the other a plate, the way you consult each other in front of guests. Everything around you grows — a garden, children, a business — and people enjoy warming themselves near you.

Some twenty people come to your family celebration: neighbours, colleagues, someone's children with dogs. One carries dishes in from the kitchen, the other makes sure everyone gets a seat and some attention. Next morning a neighbour admits: “I rest at your place the way I did at my mum's in the country.” **At your table people are well fed and warm, as if they had come home.**

Prosperity on display attracts envy and advice. Some whisper about where your money comes from, others pry about children and “when are you going to”. Sometimes you yourselves let too much out in public: jealousy breaks through in front of guests, an argument about money is heard at the table. A cup set out for show draws other people's hands, and you have to guard it from everyone.

items.title: Two behind a stone wall

captions.A: A solid couple, as safe as a stone wall

items.meaning: You come across as solid: reliable, well-off, reserved with strangers and immovable when it comes to your own.
text: You give the impression of a fortress. The Emperor shows people solid masters of their house: the home in order, business going well, decisions weighed, your own defended without hesitation. With outsiders you are reserved and rarely go visiting, but your “yes” is worth a great deal, and people come to you when they need someone to rely on.

Friends have a deal about to fall through and need someone to vouch for them. They call neither the richest nor the closest people they know, but you: “You won't let us down.” You come together, read every line of the contract, ask three awkward questions — and sign. **To your friends your couple is a stone wall you can shelter behind in any weather.**

The wall shuts people out when reserve turns into coldness. In company one speaks for both, the other is silent, and guests cannot tell whether they have an opinion of their own. You hold yourselves so stiffly that people are a little wary of inviting you, and friends gradually fade away. Outside there is order and plenty, but nobody knows whether it is warm behind those walls.

items.title: A couple others look up to

captions.A: A reliable, proper couple with its own ways

items.meaning: To others you look like a textbook couple: faithful, sensible, with your own ways — people come to you for advice.
text: From the outside you look like the kind of couple people hold up as an example. The Hierophant gives your image solidity: faithful to each other, with shared views, your own ways and rules you don't break. You are friends as well — it shows in how you talk — and people often come to you for advice as they would to elders, even if you are younger.

In the middle of her divorce, a friend of one of you calls not her parents but you: “Can I come over? You're the only ones who do things properly.” You sit her down in the kitchen, put the kettle on and take turns telling her what you once worked out yourselves. A year later it is you she brings her new partner to meet. **You show that a union can have a charter that holds better than any vows.**

The model turns to stone when it starts to preach. Unrequested advice, “that's not done in our family”, a slight condescension to those who live differently — and people begin to steer clear of you, as of strict teachers. And at home you have to live up to the sign on the door: quarrel in whispers, never show weakness. A couple everyone looks up to risks forgetting that it, too, has the right to make mistakes.

items.title: Lovers in full view

captions.A: A beautiful couple in love who don't hide it

items.meaning: Your love is visible from afar: you flirt with each other in front of everyone and tell stories as a duet.
text: People smile when they look at you. The Lovers make you two stand out: stylish, sociable, unembarrassed by tenderness in public, you tell stories as a duet, picking up each other's sentences. Even years on, a spark is visible between you, and friends every so often ask: “How do you do it?”

At someone else's wedding you dance so that for a minute people stop filming the newlyweds. Later at the table one starts telling how you mixed up the trains a week ago, the other corrects the details, and the whole company is in stitches. **You show people what many only dream of: you can be together for years and still admire each other.**

Being such a bright couple attracts more than admiration. People gossip about you readily, and you yourselves start to depend on how you look from outside: a quarrel can't be shown, tiredness can't be admitted. It can go the other way too: showdowns spill out in front of guests, jealousy is played for an audience. The more performance, the less that is real, and sooner or later the audience notices.

items.title: A couple always on the road

captions.A: A busy team that is always on the move

items.meaning: Onlookers see a team rather than lovers: always busy, on the road and standing up for each other.
text: You are rarely caught at home. The Chariot shows people a couple in motion: together you start a business, head for the mountains, move to another city and fit in a dozen other things besides. Others see you more as a team than a romantic couple — two strong people holding a shared course who never let anyone hurt the other.

Friends call to invite you to a barbecue and learn that this week you are rafting down a river and next week opening a second shop. In your joint photo you are both in helmets, holding paddles. When someone takes a dig at one of you, the other answers before the first has opened their mouth. **You are seen as a well-drilled team where each knows their place and is ready to cover the other.**

The image of a team cracks when movement turns into flight. A new venture is dropped halfway for the next one, decisions are made in a hurry, and from outside it seems you are always rushing somewhere without knowing where. It can go the other way too: two strong people begin to compete in public, interrupting and correcting each other. Friends no longer see a team but two rivals who cannot share one cart.

items.title: Strict front, warm home

captions.A: A reserved, honest and reliable couple

items.meaning: At first glance you seem a strict, even dull couple, but people know your word is firmer than any contract.
text: On the outside you look restrained. Justice shows people a couple that is organised and direct: you don't kiss in public, you don't take hasty steps, you say what you think and do what you promised. Some will call you boring, but you are the ones people leave their flat keys with while on holiday and invite as witnesses when signing something important.

At a friend's birthday you keep slightly apart, polite and calm, and one of the guests whispers: “Do they even love each other?” But at the end of the evening you are the first to leave, holding hands, and in the taxi you argue about a book so heatedly that the driver turns round. **You look stricter than you live: your fire is not for spectators.**

Restraint becomes coldness when directness hits your own. In front of friends one honestly lists the other's faults — “but it's the truth” — and the guests awkwardly look away. Or you are so used to keeping a straight face that from outside you seem like neighbours: each about their own business, nothing shared in sight. Love hidden so well is hard for people to make out, and they stop believing in it.

items.title: News only after the fact

captions.A: A quiet, modest couple who live out of the spotlight

items.meaning: People are the last to hear about your decisions: you live quietly and share news once it is already done.
text: You don't like fuss. The Hermit makes you seem quiet and a little mysterious to others: you rarely have guests, you say little about yourselves, and big events — a wedding, a move, a new job — you announce when they are already behind you. But anyone who comes to you for advice leaves with an answer they remember for years.

Friends learn about your move to another city from a photo on social media: boxes, new windows, the caption “We're here”. Some are hurt that they weren't asked to help, some are impressed. You simply didn't want to discuss the decision before it was ripe. **You do things first and talk about them afterwards — and that earns respect mixed with curiosity.**

Quiet in public can look like coldness. From outside it is unclear whether you are together or each on your own: you skip celebrations, don't speak of feelings, address each other with restraint, like colleagues. This hurts those close to you, and around a couple who tells nothing, guesses spring up. The less you let people in, the more they fill in for themselves — and usually get it wrong.

items.title: A couple that gets lucky

captions.A: Lucky, easy with change and sociable

items.meaning: To others it looks as if luck simply follows you, but your luck is knowing when to turn together.
text: Your luck is a topic of conversation. To others the Wheel of Fortune paints you as a couple for whom everything works out: you change jobs, homes and hobbies easily and come out ahead every time. You are sociable, decisive, you repay debts on time, and people enjoy being around you — as if luck were catching.

From a holiday in an unfamiliar city you come back with a job offer for one of you and a lease on a flat by the sea for next summer. Friends shake their heads: “How do you do it?” You simply got talking to the café owner and weren't afraid to say “yes”. **People think you are lucky, though the secret is simpler: when the wheel turns, you turn with it.**

The flip side of the image is a rollercoaster everyone can see. Today you celebrate a stroke of luck, tomorrow you call friends to borrow until payday, the day after you are riding high again. Quarrels come in waves too, and people get used to “something's happened again” with you. When a bad stretch drags on, others think you are always in trouble, and then you start to believe it yourselves.

items.title: Heard across the room

captions.A: A strong couple with a voice and weight

items.meaning: People see you as a strong couple with weight and a voice: you start things, organise them and see them through.
text: Wherever you turn up, you are noticed. Strength gives you both a voice and weight: you are energetic, punctual, able to take on the organising and see a plan through to the end. People are drawn to your confidence and gladly follow you — into a shared venture, on a hike, to a community clean-up you dreamed up in one evening.

For a year the residents of your block can't agree on a playground. You gather the neighbours: one writes a letter to the council, the other finds a contractor and haggles a discount. Three months later the playground is up, and ever since you are invited to every meeting. **To others you are a couple that doesn't complain but simply gets things done — and carries others along.**

Strength on display easily becomes pressure. You argue in public louder than you should, one corrects and pulls up the other in front of everyone, or teases them so that only the teaser laughs. Others feel awkward: they see not a couple but a struggle where one clearly has the upper hand. Confidence attracts as long as it has softness in it; without that, people start to be a little afraid of you.

items.title: Two who will always help

captions.A: A caring, warm couple always ready to help

items.meaning: You are known as a couple who always helps: you'll take people in, listen, give your last and ask nothing back.
text: To others you are people one can turn to. The Hanged Man gives your image softness and warmth: you are hospitable, peaceable, openly caring towards each other and just as ready to help others — selflessly, without keeping count. A little otherworldly too: you love unusual pursuits and quiet places away from the crowd.

A neighbour's flat is flooded, and an hour later she is drinking tea in your kitchen with her cat and a suitcase. You make up the sofa for her, one of you drives her to work, the other sorts out a plumber. A week later she leaves, and the whole building knows whose door to knock on in trouble. **Everyone knows that you two always have room for one more — and time to listen.**

Kindness everyone can see starts to be expected as a matter of course. You can no longer say no — what would people say? — and you give time, money and energy to those used to taking. From outside the picture is flawless, but at home you are both worn out and irritable, and the irritation lands on each other. Others see saints, while you increasingly feel like servants of your own reputation.

items.title: Quick to begin again

captions.A: A couple who make starting over feel less scary

items.meaning: You are living proof that life goes on after hard times and can turn out better than before.
text: To many you are proof that anything can be started afresh. Death makes you, in others' eyes, a couple who close chapters easily: you change cities, jobs and habits — and don't drag the past along. You are active, quick off the mark and love trying new things, and around you people want to stop fearing change.

A friend whose whole life collapsed at once — job, flat, plans — comes to you of all people: “You two know how to start over.” You don't console her; you get out a sheet of paper: what can be let go today, and what to take along. By midnight she has a list of three points and is laughing for the first time in a month. **To others you show that the end of the old can become the start of something better.**

The shadow of this image is a couple with no brakes. You go through so many changes that others can't keep up: a new city, a new job, a new passion, all within a year. Risky decisions look reckless from outside, and sharp turns frighten even those close to you. It is hard to lean on a couple who keep renewing themselves: it seems that tomorrow you will no longer be where you were.

items.title: A seam you cannot see

captions.A: Calm, patience and a striving for harmony

items.meaning: Everything seems to go smoothly for you of its own accord, and few see how much work that smoothness takes.
text: In public your couple looks seamless. A sharp word never reaches the guests, a decision is shown only once it is made, and nobody can tell whose it was to begin with. This is how Temperance looks from outside: its evenness is handmade, and there is a seam — you just cannot see it.

At your housewarming friends tour the fresh renovation and marvel: “What, not a single row?” You exchange a glance. Only you know about the two-week argument over the tiles; the guests see only neat rows. **Others see a smooth wall, while you know how much mortar went into it — and that is why it holds.**

An imbalance appears when it is always the same one doing the smoothing. Changing the subject, softening the other's bluntness, filling an awkward pause — one of you does it so deftly that people stop noticing them. Invitations go to the brighter one, and the other is asked along “for company”. In the shared portrait one face stays in focus; the other becomes a pleasant blurred background.

items.title: A pull everyone can see

captions.A: A vivid, passionate couple with strong character

items.meaning: You two draw every eye: people see passion, daring and a strength they are slightly wary of.
text: The sparks between you are visible to everyone. The Devil makes you passionate, vivid and a little daring: you are unlike others, try new things boldly, get what you want and make no secret of loving the good life. People feel slightly uneasy around you and very curious — the way anything with real power draws you in.

You turn up together at an exhibition opening in unexpected outfits, and within ten minutes a little crowd has gathered round you. You argue about a painting so heatedly that one of the artists asks to carry on over dinner, and by morning you have a joint project with someone you have known for eight hours. **Strength and desire have become your shared engine, and people want to be near it.**

A pull on display is easily mistaken for possessiveness. A jealous look across the room, a hand that holds too tight, a barb aimed at whoever came over to talk — and people see not passion but a chain. Sometimes you indulge each other in everything, and from outside it is unclear who is leading whom. The strength people admired begins to frighten them.

items.title: A couple made of stories

captions.A: A vivid couple, always stirring and building

items.meaning: People love telling stories about you: you build with your hands, don't fear sharp turns and don't break in a storm.
text: People love telling stories about you. The Tower makes you vivid and unpredictable: sharp turns, decisions made overnight, events friends retell wide-eyed. You are forever building something: renovating an old house, assembling furniture, re-roofing the cottage, and from outside it is clear how well you work together with your hands.

Your friends tell it at your birthdays better than you do: how you knocked down a wall in a rented flat in one weekend, having squared it with the landlord by phone straight from the DIY store. And at the housewarming guests touch that very wall, rebuilt from scratch, and can't believe the two of you did it. **To your friends you are living proof that after a storm you can rebuild stronger than before.**

A vivid story attracts gossip too. When something goes wrong for you, people readily wait for the next collapse: “something's always falling apart with them”. Sometimes you add fuel yourselves — having it out in public, cutting people off abruptly, flaring up over trifles. Then instead of a couple who weather storms, people see a couple who attract them, and start keeping their distance.

items.title: A picture that doesn't lie

captions.A: A vivid, inspiring couple people admire

items.meaning: People admire you: you are bright, open and inspire others to believe beautiful love exists not only in films.
text: People like looking at you. The Star makes you bright and open: you are stylish, sincere, unembarrassed by feelings in public, and you inspire others just by being yourselves. Often you share a calling too — both in the same profession, both passionate about your work — and people see not only love but a shared light.

The two of you speak at a conference, and after the talk people come up not with questions on the subject but with another one: “May I ask how you met?” A joint photo from an exhibition gets more responses than any work post. **You are seen as the rare case where a beautiful picture is the truth, not the wrapping.**

Light in public demands constant confirmation. It becomes important how you look together, how many likes a photo gets, what colleagues will think. A quarrel is hidden, tiredness touched up, and the union starts living for an audience. When the wrapping matters more than the contents, others are the first to sense the falseness, and yesterday's role model becomes a subject of gossip.

items.title: A puzzle to your friends

captions.A: A mysterious couple people spin rumours about

items.meaning: To others you are a mystery: you say little about yourselves, but much is said about you — and almost always wrong.
text: The Moon wraps you both in haze. You say little about yourselves, you have unusual professions or hobbies that seem eccentric to others, and people fill in the gaps themselves. Yet you are interesting company: you can keep up any conversation — from dreams to ancient civilisations — and after an evening with you guests leave thoughtful.

At an office party a colleague of one of you cautiously quizzes the other: is it true you met on an archaeological dig? And that you have a house out of town with no electricity? You smile and don't deny it: the truth is more interesting, but it is yours. **Legends grow up around you, because you guard what is yours and are in no hurry to show it.**

Haze becomes fog when secrecy turns into half-truths. One tells friends one thing, the other something else, complaints about the partner are voiced behind their back, and small exaggerations add up to a story that never happened. Then rumours feed not on mystery but on contradictions, and people no longer know where the truth lies. A couple's secret is worth keeping, but not to be confused with a lie.

items.title: A house where the lights are on

captions.A: A warm, successful couple who light up a room

items.meaning: People feel warm around you: you are successful, hospitable and generous, and your home is full of guests and laughter.
text: It is bright around you. The Sun makes you warm, successful and generous: each has their own field in which they excel, and together you keep an open house where guests are welcome at any hour. You travel a lot, laugh loudly, rejoice in others' success, and people are drawn to you as to a bonfire on a cold evening.

Your summer party in the garden is the event of the year for the whole street: a long table, fairy lights, music late into the night, the neighbours' children racing between the grown-ups. Someone comes with a pie, someone with a guitar, and someone just because it feels good at your place. **You have warmth enough for everyone, and around you people become more generous themselves.**

Bright light casts shadows. Your wealth and success are discussed behind your back; some envy you, some wait for you to slip. Worse when the sun between you starts to burn: one outshines the other in front of guests, claims shared victories, jealously watches who got more attention. Outside it is still a party, but at the table there are no longer two hosts — just a star and their entourage.

items.title: We stand by our own

captions.A: A family couple who hold on to their own

items.meaning: Everyone knows family is everything to you: your own people always come first, and outsiders need time to become family.
text: Your own come first. Judgement makes yours a family couple in the deepest sense: you hold on to your relatives, remember the family dates, gather the generations at one table and open up to people only once they become your own. Much may divide you — age, background, faith — yet from outside it is plain that this does not get in the way but rather binds you closer.

Three generations gather for the milestone birthday of one partner's grandmother, and the other, once met by the family with suspicion, now gives the main toast. Everyone knows it was they who found the great-grandfather's old photographs in an archive and made an album of them. **In your hands the family line carries on, and even someone it once refused to accept becomes one of its own.**

Family life on display can look like a closed door. Friends are hurt that you can never be got hold of — always relatives, always your own. Newcomers find it hard to enter the circle, and you keep promises to outsiders less often than promises to your own. From outside you look like a fortress with the drawbridge up: you are happy inside, but nobody outside knows how you really live.

items.title: No borders on your map

captions.A: An open couple for whom one city is too small

items.meaning: People take you for citizens of the world: you travel a lot, make friends easily and strike many as the ideal couple.
text: From outside you look like a couple for whom one city is not enough. The World gives your image breadth: you travel a lot, get on easily with people from different cultures and take a modern, relaxed view of relationships. In arguments you look for a compromise, you split duties equally, and to many of your acquaintances you are an example of what a couple can be.

Your friends live in five countries, and your wedding guests came from three continents. You see in the New Year now in the mountains, now with one partner's relatives thousands of kilometres away, and your kitchen smells of dishes brought back from your travels. **Your shared world is bigger than any spot on the map, and everyone who knows you can see it.**

The image of an ideal couple is heavy to wear. Acquaintances expect endless harmony from you, and you begin to act it out: you hide conflicts, let displeasure slip out as barbs in front of guests and open the door less and less. A wide world in the photographs, a cramped one at home. People notice the difference before you are ready to admit it.

items.title: Students forever on holiday

captions.A: A light, vivid couple of adventurers

items.meaning: You are seen as eternal adventurers — light, funny, free — and people envy your carefree ways a little.
text: You look like perpetual students on holiday. The Fool makes you light and vivid: flexible hours, sudden trips, creative schemes, laughter you can hear through the wall. You look at problems without panic and can start from zero as if it were an adventure — and many people envy you a little.

Friends are still debating in the group chat where to go for the May bank holiday, and you are already sending a photo from a station in an unfamiliar town: “We're here, come and join us.” Last year you gave up a safe job for a small workshop of your own, and the relatives phoned with condolences for a week. **Your courage to live your own way delights some and worries others, but leaves no one indifferent.**

Lightness is easily mistaken for frivolity. People don't take your plans seriously, you are invited to important events “if you can make it”, and the relatives wait for you to “finally grow up”. Worse if behind the light facade there really is a certain emptiness: each lives their own life, you are together only in photos, and you look more like two cheerful flatmates than a couple.

items.title: Gifts, walks and pies

captions.F: Gifts, care and beauty all around

items.meaning: Care you can touch is what restores you: a gift, a walk, a beautiful dinner, a shared success.
text: You blossom from care. The Empress fills your life with beauty and generosity: gifts for no reason, walks in the park, trips, making things together, good food and a cosy home. It matters to you that what you share keeps growing — a garden, a venture, your means — and that every success is celebrated like a harvest.

A hard day, and you don't feel like going home. But the hallway smells of apple pie, there are flowers on the table, and on the side table lies the very scarf one of you had been eyeing in a shop window. An hour later you are walking together through the autumn park, and the bad day dissolves. **What restores you is care you can see, taste and touch.**

Generosity runs dry when care flows only one way. One bakes, gives presents, throws parties, and the other takes it for granted and gives nothing back. Gifts become a way to apologise without words, purchases a consolation, and the house fills with things but not with warmth. Receiving is not enough for the Empress: her garden blooms only when both of you water it.

items.title: The power of a shared plan

captions.F: Shared goals, order and a safe home base

items.meaning: A shared plan gives you strength: a goal for the year ahead, order at home and a celebration planned to the last detail.
text: The best rest for you is a shared plan on the table. The Emperor fills your life with order and shared goals: you like setting tasks a year ahead, crossing off what's done, watching your household grow. You are charged by the sense of a secure home base — and, to outsiders' surprise, by a passion that has not gone anywhere behind the solid exterior.

In January you sit down over a big sheet of paper: what do we want by next winter — a country cottage, a holiday by the ocean, a promotion for one of you. By summer half the items are ticked off, and you celebrate with a dinner one of you has planned down to the last detail, including who sits where. **What charges you is not chance but a goal you move towards together and watch come closer.**

The plan runs out of breath when it turns into a rulebook with no room for wishes. Everything is set out point by point, and nothing ever happens “just because”: no sudden trip, no evening with nothing to do. Passion, which needs surprise, falls asleep under a pile of tasks. The Emperor would do well now and then to write in an item with no purpose — say, a surprise only one of you knows about.

items.title: Rituals that keep you warm

captions.F: Keep your own traditions and family rituals

items.meaning: Your own rituals keep you going: Sunday lunch, a shared holiday, a heart-to-heart — repeats that never grow stale.
text: You gather strength through repetition. The Hierophant fills your life with traditions: holidays of your own, Sunday lunches with family, walks along the same route, long talks about how life works. You are nourished by the sense of being part of something larger — a family, a circle, a story — while each of you grows in their own work, knowing the other has their back.

On the first Saturday of December, as every year, you get out the box of decorations and argue over where to hang the glass owl inherited from a grandmother. Then you invite friends round for mulled wine to the family recipe everyone already knows by heart. After a hard autumn this evening puts everything back in place. **What restores you is not novelty but what repeats year after year and means more each time.**

A ritual goes flat when it is kept out of duty. Lunch with the relatives becomes a chore, a holiday a script where not a single line can move, and the suggestion “let's do it differently this year” sounds like a revolt against home. One of you drags the tradition along, the other puts up with it for the sake of peace. The form is still there, but the warmth it was once invented for is gone. One new custom, invented by the two of you, is enough to make the old ones breathe again.

items.title: A midweek date

captions.F: Attention, compliments and dates for two

items.meaning: Attention to each other recharges you: a midweek date, a compliment for no reason, a decision made together.
text: Your union feeds on attention. The Lovers restore you whenever you truly notice each other again: in a compliment paid not out of habit, in a date in the middle of the working week, in a conversation about everything under the sun until midnight. Even small decisions — which tiles, where to go on holiday, what's for dinner — you like to make together, and it is not a burden but one more reason to be close.

After a month of crunch, one of you texts at lunchtime: “Seven tonight by the fountain, dress up.” In the evening you stroll like tourists around the city you have lived in for ten years and laugh that for the first time in a month you are talking about something other than work. **What brings you back to each other is not a holiday once a year but a small date one of you found time for.**

The supply of attention runs out when it is waited for rather than given. Each silently waits for the other to make the first move and remembers who last said something nice. A date turns into an exam: wrong restaurant, wrong look. You still choose the tiles together, but as neighbours in a renovation, not as a couple. What usually brings it back is something very small — a note on the mirror, a call for no reason — if you do it first, without waiting your turn.

items.title: Wind in both your faces

captions.F: Movement, the road and each other's wins

items.meaning: Movement is what recharges you: the road, a shared route and each other's wins, celebrated as your own.
text: Standing still wears you out, and the road recharges you. The Chariot fills your life with movement: hikes, packing in one evening, a move to a place you chose together, the thrill of a shared goal. And victories that are not someone else's: when one of you reaches a new height, the other draws no less energy from it than the winner.

After a hard month you don't lie on the sofa; on Friday evening you get into the car and by nightfall pitch a tent by a lake with no signal and nothing to do. On Saturday, twenty kilometres on foot; by evening your legs are buzzing — and all the tiredness somehow drains away. On Monday you come back as if from a month's holiday. **You rest not from movement but in it — especially when you are heading the same way.**

The spark goes out when each races down their own road and stops looking back. One has disappeared into a project, the other into their sport; you see each other in the kitchen on the way from one thing to the next. Victories are no longer celebrated together but compared: who has more, who overtook whom. The Chariot rolls on, but now there are two teams of horses, and with every kilometre there is more empty space between them. One shared weekend on the road is enough to ride side by side again.

items.title: The calm of a kept word

captions.F: Honesty, predictability and keeping your word

items.meaning: Trusting each other's word steadies you: what is said gets done, and nobody needs to keep watch.
text: You rest where everything is honest. Justice fills the union with predictability in the best sense: if one says “I'll pick you up at six”, at six they are at the door; if they promise to deal with the tax office, they will. You don't have to guess what the other meant or stay on guard: you can breathe out and simply be together.

Friday evening, both of you worn out. One says plainly: “I need an hour of quiet, then I'm all yours.” The other doesn't take offence or read into it, but goes off with a book to another room. An hour later you are cooking dinner together and chatting as if you had rested for a week. **Clarity is how you rest: nobody hides anything, and so it is calm to be close.**

Calm turns into boredom when honesty becomes the only thing you give each other. Everything is agreed, everything goes to plan, there are no surprises — and that is exactly what you begin to miss. One catches themselves looking for an excuse to quarrel, just so that something happens. Justice holds but does not warm: sometimes it is worth breaking your own schedule for a walk that was not in the plan.

items.title: A silence worth listening to

captions.F: Deep conversations and the right to be alone

items.meaning: A silence that needs no filling feeds you, and so do talks after which the world makes more sense.
text: Your strength comes back in quiet. The Hermit brings depth into your life together: long conversations about what really matters, respect for the other's right to be alone, admiration for how your partner sees further and thinks deeper. You may have pastimes others find strange — old maps, rare mushrooms, the history of one back street — and in them you meet as in a secret club for two.

Sunday. Each in their own corner: one sorts through old photographs, the other finishes a thick book. For about three hours you don't speak, and you are both content. Then one comes into the kitchen with a question they have been turning over all day, and until evening you talk about things you discuss with no one else. **What fills you is not noise but being able to stay silent side by side and then say what matters most.**

Silence goes empty if you hide from problems in it. One withdraws into their corner not to recover but to avoid discussing what is difficult, and the other takes it for coldness. Conversations grow rare, mystery turns into impenetrability. Each thinks about their own things, and nobody thinks about the two of you. The Hermit needs not only a corner of one's own, but also an evening when both come out of their rooms to the same table.

items.title: A lucky streak for two

captions.F: Luck, lightness and shared memories

items.meaning: Lightness recharges you: a lucky turn, a spontaneous trip and memories you go over together.
text: You come alive when life takes a turn. The Wheel of Fortune brings you lightness and a taste for change: a spontaneous trip, an unexpected offer, a stroke of luck you celebrate as shared. And in quiet spells memories hold you: you know how to go over the good moments so that they warm you again.

On a winter evening when everything is grey, one of you gets out the old album — the one with the hitchhiking trip when you got stuck in a small town and by chance ended up at a stranger's wedding. An hour later you are roaring with laughter and choosing where to go in spring, though there is no money yet. **Strength comes from the belief that the next turn of the wheel will be for the better — and from remembering how it has been before.**

Lightness wears off when the wheel stays at the bottom for long. Luck doesn't come, trips are postponed, and you start waiting instead of looking. Conversations become complaints, memories a reproach to the present: “we used to…”. But the wheel does not turn by itself: sometimes it is enough to change your weekend route or invite new people to feel that you are moving again.

items.title: A hot temper shared by two

captions.F: Taming fire with tenderness

items.meaning: Your fuel is a hot temper that you don't smother but guide gently: even anger ends in shared laughter for you.
text: You get your charge where things run hot: in excitement, stubbornness, desire, even anger. Strength doesn't put out this fire or drive it back with fear — it guides it gently, from within: when one flares up, the other catches the flame and keeps it from spreading.

One of you comes home after an unfair dressing-down and paces the flat, jaw clenched. The other doesn't coax them to calm down — they get angry together, out loud, until both start laughing at their own fury. The anger burns out, and you come out of it closer than you went in. **What fills you is a strong feeling you never had to hide or fear.**

The fire runs low when it is always the same one of you who has to guide it. When the other flares up, this one catches it, shares the anger, brings it round to laughter; but when they catch fire themselves, there is no one to catch them: the other has grown used to having the flame handled for them. The tamer runs out of breath, and their own fire is the first to go out. Yet your embers are alive: one shared blaze is enough to burn together again.

items.title: The world from a new angle

captions.F: Slow down and see the world differently together

items.meaning: A pause and a fresh view restore you: quiet time together, new places and being understood without words.
text: For you a pause is not lost time but fuel. The Hanged Man fills your life with stillness: an evening with nowhere to be, a film under one blanket, an aimless walk, a game made up on the spot. You like unusual pastimes — night fishing, the planetarium, an abandoned station out of town — and you sense each other even at a distance.

After a hard week you switch off your phones and go to a small town where nothing happens. All day you wander the streets, sit on the embankment and watch the river. You say little, but by evening one of you says aloud what had been going round in the other's head. **What fills you is the chance to stop together and see the familiar differently.**

The pause turns into stagnation when you never come out of it. You love quiet together so much that you stop letting the rest of the world in, and one of you always gives way over how to spend free time and is quietly bored. Care turns into “you rest, I'll do it”, and one burns out while the other rests. The Hanged Man needs the pause to fill both of you, not to be one partner's sacrifice for the other.

items.title: Renewal instead of a holiday

captions.F: Newness in everything: moves, frankness, growth

items.meaning: Change renews you: a move, a new habit, a frank talk — anything that helps you shed an old skin.
text: Renewal brings you to life. Death fills your life with change: a move to a new city, a change of job, a new habit you take up together, a heart-to-heart after which it is easier to breathe. You are bored when everything stays the same and glad when together you manage to shed what has outlived itself and start with a clean slate.

On New Year's Eve you don't make wishes; you hold a “farewell to the old”: each writes on a slip of paper what they want to part with — a habit of being late, a grudge against a brother, a job they are sick of — and together you burn the slips in the stove at the country cottage. By spring half of what was written really has gone. **What fills you is the right to leave the past behind and begin again together.**

Change wears you out when there is more of it than you have strength for. You renew everything in sight — flats, jobs, plans — and one of you already longs for a little constancy. Frankness turns into bluntness, and the new into an escape from an old that was never lived through. Death fills you when every ending is followed by a breathing space, and only then by a beginning.

items.title: A quiet evening, as planned

captions.F: Calm, shared taste and an even rhythm

items.meaning: A calm rhythm restores you: a quiet evening together, making things side by side and the sense that life runs its course.
text: An even rhythm is your best rest. Temperance fills your life with calm: a quiet evening for two, an unhurried weekend breakfast, making something together, where the hands are busy and the head rests. You enjoy admiring each other's taste — the way one chooses the crockery, the way the other arranges the books — and feeling that life is taking its course, without jolts.

On Sundays you have a “kitchen workshop”: one makes dumplings, the other boils jam or reupholsters an old stool. The radio, tea, nowhere to be. After such a day the week goes more easily than after any trip. **What rests you is not an event but a rhythm in which you are both at peace.**

The even rhythm grows dull when calm becomes compulsory. Any change throws you off course, strong feelings are hidden so as not to disturb the harmony, and boredom passes itself off as peace. One wants something unexpected but keeps quiet so as not to upset the other. Temperance would do well to add a new ingredient to the mix now and then, or the flavour goes flat.

items.title: Bold desires said aloud

captions.F: Passion, bold desires and the freedom of trust

items.meaning: Passion and daring energise you: admitting a desire, trying something new and knowing you won't be judged.
text: The courage to want — that is what charges you. The Devil brings passion and honesty into your life: you can admit a desire others would find strange, try something new, take a risk — and know you won't be judged. You are also fed by discipline: a shared routine, sport, an order with room for both excitement and freedom.

It comes out by chance that one of you has wanted to learn the tango all their life but was too shy. The other doesn't laugh; a week later they bring home a pass for two. The first lessons are a disaster, trodden toes and fits of laughter, but by summer you dance at someone's wedding so that the guests step aside. **Strength comes from the right to want boldly and to find in the other an accomplice, not a judge.**

The spark turns into a grip when nothing but passion is left. Only closeness holds you, conversations come down to making up, and freedom is quietly replaced by control. Desires stop being shared: each pulls towards their own pleasure and demands that the other back it. The Devil fills you as long as passion remains the free choice of two, not a chain both are afraid to break.

items.title: Building that brings you closer

captions.F: Building together and cherishing small joys

items.meaning: What you build with your hands restores you, and so do the small moments of happiness you notice even in a storm.
text: Working with your hands brings you closer. The Tower gives you building after demolition: you knocked down a partition and put up a new one, overhauled an old house, survived a storm and came out of it closer. You treasure small happy moments — the smell of fresh paint, tea right on the building site, laughter when something finally works — and a passion that hardships do not put out.

Together you take apart the old veranda at the country cottage: rotten boards, rusty nails, scraped hands. By evening, instead of a veranda there is an empty platform and a mountain of rubbish, and you are both so tired you sit right on the ground. One hands the other a sandwich, and somehow it is the best dinner of the month. **What comes ready-made pleases you less than what you have taken apart together and are building again together.**

Strength drains away when demolition is no longer followed by building. Storms outnumber breathing spaces, and small joys drown in waiting for the next blow. One gets used to expecting the worst, the other stops noticing the good. The Tower needs a rule of its own: after every storm, something built together, even if only a birdhouse.

items.title: Stars over the lake

captions.F: Romance, nature and faith in each other's dream

items.meaning: Romance is what fills you: a walk by the water, admiring each other and believing that each of your dreams will come true.
text: Being in love brings you back to life — years on, too. The Star fills your life with romance and hope: walks by the water, the night sky outside the city, admiration for the way the other burns with their work. You inspire each other, and one partner's big success becomes a source of light for you both.

A hard week, and on Friday evening one of you drives the other out of town to a lake without a word of explanation. A blanket, a flask, shooting stars over the water. You hardly talk — you just lie there and look up. On Monday one of you sends off a competition entry they had been putting off for six months: “There by the lake it became clear what I want.” **Beauty restores your strength because it reminds you what you dream of.**

The light dims when romance is put off “until later”. Walks give way to chores, dreams to reports, admiration to a habit of not noticing. Or the reverse: you live on a single dream without taking any steps towards it, and disappointment arrives before success. The Star needs both beauty and a road: sometimes one evening by the water is enough to believe in each other again.

items.title: A secret world for two

captions.F: Fantasies, games and a secret world of your own

items.meaning: A world only the two of you know feeds you: shared fantasies, games, private words and an unusual pastime.
text: You are nourished by what happens between you and nowhere else. The Moon brings fantasy and mystery into your life: words only the two of you understand, night-time talks about dreams, games nobody else plays, an unusual shared pastime. It matters to you to feel desired and a little mysterious to each other — even after many years.

You have a game called “strangers' night”: you meet in a bar as if for the first time, invent life stories for yourselves and flirt, and then ride home together, laughing. The people at the next table suspect nothing. **What fills you is the mystery you keep for each other and the chance to discover something new in the other every time.**

The secret world grows thin when anxiety takes the place of fantasy. Instead of play — suspicion; instead of mystery — things left unsaid; and the shared world becomes a place where each hides something. Sometimes one withdraws into themselves, and the other reads it as distance, though the first simply needs to get their strength back. The Moon needs trust as well as mystery: play is possible only when both know there is no false bottom beneath it.

items.title: Basking in each other's light

captions.F: Vivid experiences and pride in your partner

items.meaning: Vivid experiences and each other's successes energise you: one partner's win wakes the other's wish to grow.
text: Light is what charges you. The Sun gives you a love of life: vivid experiences, new people, dreams come true, loud laughter round a big table. But most of all you are fed by pride in each other: when your partner grows, it stirs no jealousy but pushes you, too, to reach higher.

One of you wins an award for a project they spent a year on. The other throws a party: invites friends, prints a photo from the ceremony, gives a toast that brings a shine to both your eyes. A week later they sign up for the course they have long dreamed of: “You've got me going.” **The other's light does not blind you but wakes your own — that is your fuel.**

The Sun dims when only one of you shines. One is always on stage, the other in the audience, and the one in the seats grows tired of clapping. Celebrations become rarer, routine replaces new experiences, and you stop sharing your joys because there is nothing to boast about. A love of life cannot rest on one person: each needs a reason for pride of their own, and the other should be the first to hear of it.

items.title: Bound by a shared story

captions.F: A shared cause, growing together and shared memory

items.meaning: Your shared story sustains you: everything you have lived through binds you, and a shared cause carries it on.
text: What holds you is everything you have lived through together. Judgement gives you a shared history: every trial, every celebration, every decision made by the two of you goes into the foundation, and the more years behind you, the firmer it gets. You are charged by a shared cause and by the sense that you grow not apart but together, answering the same call.

On a winter evening you go through a box of papers: your first tenancy agreement, tickets to the concert where you quarrelled and made up, a sketch of your future house on a napkin. An hour later your whole life is spread across the table, and you are both surprised how much ground you have already covered. **You need novelty less than the feeling that everything you have lived through is shared.**

A shared history stops nourishing you when you only ever look back. Memories become reproaches — “remember how you…” — and old grievances rise from the archive in every quarrel. The shared cause turns into a duty, growth into running on the spot. Judgement needs the past to call you forward: a couple's story should have a sequel, not just an archive.

items.title: Places worth going back to

captions.F: Frank talks and favourite places for two

items.meaning: You draw strength from a sense of wholeness: a place where you were happy, a long talk and a new horizon ahead.
text: You are restored by the feeling that the world is big and you are in it together. The World gives you room to breathe: travel, moves, a morning run together, a frank conversation that leaves nothing unsaid. And places where you were once happy: you long to go back there, and each time you return more whole.

Once a year you go back to the same shore where you spent your first holiday together. The café on the corner has a new sign, but the bench by the water is the same. You sit on it until sunset, talk about how the year has been and make plans for the next. **What brings you back together is a place where you were already whole — and a conversation in which nothing needs hiding.**

Space shrinks when life closes into a work–home loop. Trips are postponed, talk comes down to chores, sport to a gym card forgotten in a drawer. You don't quarrel, it just gets cramped. The World needs more than your cosiness: it needs a horizon. Sometimes a single trip to where you were happy is enough to feel whole again.

items.title: Laughter as a spare battery

captions.F: Humour, adventures and unconditional support

items.meaning: Laughter and adventure fill you: a spontaneous trip, a shared joke and the sense that together you can start from scratch.
text: Lightness charges you. The Fool brings laughter, adventure and unconditional support into your life: you can set off on a trip at an hour's notice, turn a failure into an anecdote and start again without chewing over the mistake for weeks. Next to each other you stop being serious adults — and that is exactly what restores your strength.

You have missed the train you saved for all year. For the first five minutes you both stand silent on the platform, then one says: “Well, shall we go wherever the next one goes?” The next one goes to an unfamiliar little town, where you spend the best three days of the year and bring back a story you tell at every party. **What fills you is not a plan but the ability to laugh together when the plan has fallen apart.**

Lightness stops nourishing you when it becomes a way of not noticing. Any serious subject is turned into a joke, talk about the future into “we'll sort it out later”, and one of you feels their worry isn't heard. Amusements follow one another, while beneath them builds up what nobody laughs at. The Fool needs not only freedom but also a minute when both fall silent and speak seriously.

items.title: A full cup that doesn't tip

captions.C: Grow prosperity and invest in the future

items.meaning: You know how to grow prosperity: a joint budget, sensible spending, investing ahead and a home that lacks nothing.
text: Your home strives to be a cup filled to the brim. The Empress runs the household with generosity and calculation at once: a joint budget, sensible spending, investment in the future — education, a home, a business of your own. Prosperity grows when you have a shared goal and each has their own calling, rather than one breadwinner and one keeper of the hearth.

You decide to buy a house outside the city and work towards it for three years: every month part of both salaries goes into a separate account, and you argue about the colour of the kitchen long before there is a kitchen. Along the way one of you finishes a course and finds a better job. When the house is bought, you celebrate not the purchase but what the two of you managed together. **Your money grows like a garden: from shared care and from each of you growing in your own right.**

The cup tips when only one of you grows. Their income rises, while the other depends on them for every purchase and feels like a dependant. Or spending outruns income, and parents bail you out until you can no longer do without them. An imbalance in money quickly becomes an imbalance at home: whoever earns decides, whoever doesn't keeps quiet.

items.title: A well-stocked fortress

captions.C: Build a secure home base and save for years ahead

items.meaning: Your home is a fortress with stores: decisions come slowly, there are no debts, and you save for years ahead.
text: Your household is built like a fortress. The Emperor gives you thoroughness: measure twice, cut once; the important first and the pleasant later; we neither borrow nor lend. You make money decisions slowly but solidly, and you always have a reserve for a rainy day, or even a fund meant for the next generation.

You buy not the first flat you like but the fifteenth, after a spreadsheet of price per square metre and a talk with a lawyer. You renovate to a plan, stage by stage, without loans. The neighbours have long been living among boxes and paying off loans, while you move in six months later, but into a place that is yours and debt-free. **Your prosperity rests on order rather than luck, and so the first gust of wind doesn't blow it away.**

The fortress grows oppressive when it has one commandant. One runs the budget, the other reports on every purchase, and any “let's take a chance” smashes against an iron “no”. Thoroughness turns into rigidity: the money sits there, while life is put off till later. The Emperor does well to keep several pots for different goals — including one from which each spends without accounting for it.

items.title: A budget by the family charter

captions.C: Live by rules that have stood the test of time

items.meaning: Your household is held together by rules, inherited or made up by the two of you, and by things that serve for generations.
text: Money in your home lives by a charter. The Hierophant runs the household by tradition: a shared budget, purchases for the family first, old things mended rather than thrown out, and savings that grow slowly but surely. Many of your rules came from your parents' homes, the rest you wrote yourselves — and you keep both codes with equal respect.

You have an envelope marked “for winter”, a grandmother's tea set that comes out twice a year, and a stool reupholstered for the third time. Big purchases are discussed at the table, as at a family council: why, for whom, what will we say about it in five years. A new fridge is chosen as if it will be handed down. **Your household is solid because every rule in it has been tested by more than one generation.**

The charter grows heavy when the rules start guarding themselves. “That's not how we do things” greets any new expense, one partner manages the other's money “out of care” without asking, and parents' advice walks into the budget without knocking. Over time the other stops wanting anything of their own: it is easier not to ask than to sit through a lecture on extravagance. A home where everything goes by the rules grows as quiet as a reading room.

items.title: Money is for enjoying

captions.C: Spend on beauty and joy for the two of you

items.meaning: You earn to live beautifully and generously: your money turns into shared experiences, gifts and a cosy home.
text: For you money is a way to enjoy life, not a goal. The Lovers run the household with the heart: you earn in order to spend on what makes life more beautiful — dinner somewhere good, flowers for no reason, a trip you talk about for years. Comfort and taste at home matter more than perfect order, and every big purchase you choose together, arguing about the colour until you are hoarse.

For the third Saturday running you trawl the furniture shops, because the sofa has to be “the one”: one of you wants green velvet, the other wants room for two with your feet up. You buy the green one and the big one, overpaying, but in the evenings you lie on it together with a film and don't regret a penny. **Your home is furnished not from a list but by feeling, and that is why it is a place to live in, not just to sleep.**

Generosity goes off course when money starts speaking instead of words. An expensive gift after a quarrel, a purchase “to cheer myself up”, hurt if the other spent on themselves without asking. Spending jumps after feelings: one moment a celebration, the next a regime of strict economy with reproaches. One of you is unhappy with how much the other brings in and says nothing aloud — only sighs over the receipts. The more feeling goes into the wallet, the less is left for conversation.

items.title: A household on wheels

captions.C: Earn on the move and don't pile up things

items.meaning: Your household is on the move: money goes on the road, growth and new projects, and things never hold you in place.
text: Your home is more headquarters than fortress. The Chariot runs the household on the go: two or three projects at once, a plan for the year ahead, a car that matters more than a new wardrobe, and you part with things easily if they get in the way of moving on. You earn money by hard work and spend it on motion — moves, trips, studies, a business of your own.

Before yet another move you give away half your things in a weekend: books to the library, an armchair to the neighbours, a box of crockery to the local group chat. One of you keeps a spreadsheet of costs at the new place down to the last penny, the other is already looking for work there. A month later you have settled in, and nobody remembers the armchair. **You acquire not things but opportunities, and so you are always ready to pull up stakes.**

The team pulls apart when both of you tug at the reins. One plans, the other buys, neither gives up the wheel, and the budget becomes a tug-of-war: who is in charge, whose spending matters more. Sometimes it goes the other way — the speed carries you both away: a new loan for a new venture before the old one has paid off, a loan “against the future”. The Chariot flies fast, and all the more reason for it to have one driver and a shared route.

items.title: An honest account for two

captions.C: Keep accounts, split fairly, have a plan B

items.meaning: Everything is fair between you: income is written down, spending discussed, and there is a backup plan for any eventuality.
text: Clarity about money matters more to you than an extra penny. Justice runs the household by contract: income and expenses are recorded, taxes paid, big purchases decided together and without haste. Each knows their share, a reserve is always set aside for the unexpected and a plan B thought through. You don't care for surprises — but then the late-night sums of “how do we make it to payday” rarely happen either.

Before buying a car you sit down one evening with a laptop: a spreadsheet, three options, what ownership will cost over five years, what happens if one of you loses their job. The argument is short and calm, the decision shared. The seller is surprised that you haggle politely, with figures in hand. **Money doesn't make you quarrel, because the rules of the game are written down, not guessed.**

The account turns petty when honesty becomes bookkeeping of feelings. Who put in how much, whose turn it is to pay for dinner, why you bought something for yourself and not for me — every trifle goes on the scales. Sometimes they tip further: one refuses to work “on principle” or saves in secret, the other carries everything and silently keeps a ledger of grievances. The figures are in order, but there is less and less warmth at home.

items.title: Things that last for years

captions.C: Keep supplies at the mountain pass

items.meaning: Your home is like a hut on a mountain pass: few things, each long considered, and something in the larder for bad weather.
text: For you a purchase is a decision you have to grow into. The Hermit runs daily life unhurriedly: before buying, you check prices, compare, put it off and come back to the question with an answer already in hand. As a result you own few things, but each serves a long time, and something is always put by for a hard day.

Choosing a kettle takes you a week: tabs full of reviews, a trip to the shop “just to look”, one more night to think — and then it serves for a decade. One of you keeps an inventory of the larder, the other teases, and then adds to it themselves: rice, batteries, light bulbs. **Your home is made of decisions, not purchases, and so it ages slowly.**

Caution turns into stinginess when the reserve is hoarded no longer for peace of mind but for a day that never comes. Touching it feels frightening, and every purchase demands a justification. One partner's rules become the only right ones, and the other starts buying quietly, hiding the receipts. The house is full, yet it feels chilly: the new duvet still lies in its packaging, “for later”.

items.title: Tides in a shared purse

captions.C: Catch the right moment and wait out the ebb

items.meaning: Your money comes in waves: the tides arrive unexpectedly, and the key is not to spend them before the ebb begins.
text: Your shared purse is sometimes full, sometimes empty, and that is perfectly normal for you. The Wheel of Fortune turns it without stopping: a sudden commission, a bonus or a lucky sale, then a lull when every expense has to be counted. You know how to spot opportunities, move for better conditions and be generous with each other, and you keep the budget honestly, if without excessive fuss.

In spring a big commission lands on one of you, and in three months you earn as much as you usually do in a year. You don't buy a new car: you pay off the loan and put money aside for the “quiet season”. In autumn the orders dry up, and you calmly wait it out while friends marvel at your composure. **You know the wheel will turn, and you save at high tide so the ebb never catches you off guard.**

The wheel is dangerous for those who believe luck has come to stay. A good month — and you are already borrowing against future earnings; a bad one — and the budget is left to drift: “there's never enough anyway”. Envy of those with a “steady” life eats away at you both, and each looks for someone to blame for the ebb. A change in money is neither punishment nor reward, but a turn you can prepare for in advance.

items.title: A firm grip for two

captions.C: Save hard and spend freely on what lights you up

items.meaning: You can raise money for a goal fast and never begrudge spending it on what lights you up: hobbies, sport, pleasures.
text: When it comes to money, you have real drive. Strength gives you both persistence and stamina: once you set a goal, you save hard, cutting the extras without moaning, and you solve problems not head-on but with ingenuity. Yet you are no ascetics: on what fires you up — gear, a favourite pursuit, a trip to the mountains — you don't spare money, because you know how much energy it gives back.

You set your hearts on a boat — and within a year you have saved for it, giving up takeaways and taxis. One of you found weekend work, the other thought of renting out the garage everyone had forgotten about. On your first summer evening on the water you decide it is the best purchase of your lives. **You spend your energy and your money on the same thing — on what makes you feel alive.**

The grip gets too tight when one hand holds the purse. One partner controls all the money and doles it out to the other “by the rules”, calling it order. Or work devours you both: you save stubbornly, but there is no energy or time left for the home or each other, the dishes pile up, the bins go unemptied. The strength that was enough for a goal goes into arguing about who is in charge of the money.

items.title: Patience in a shared purse

captions.C: Put everything into family and bide your time

items.meaning: Your wealth grows slowly: you put everything into the family, avoid debt and know how to bide your time.
text: You don't expect quick money. The Hanged Man runs the household without fuss: everything you earn goes into the family and each other, you dislike debt, pay bills on time and can politely refuse those who are forever asking for a loan. You respect any kind of work and don't chase easy money — prosperity comes slowly, but it comes.

For five years you rent and save a little at a time, giving up what others consider essential. Friends change cars; you change habits. One of you spends years in a modest job they love, and the other has never once reproached them over the salary. When the time comes to buy a place of your own, you buy it without a mortgage. **Your own corner grew out of patience and respect for each other's work.**

Patience turns into stagnation when waiting becomes scarier than acting. Nobody asks for a promotion, no business gets started, savings lie as dead weight: what if something happens. One depends entirely on the other's money and feels indebted. And others' wealth is viewed with quiet resentment: why them and not us? The Hanged Man should sometimes turn the view around: savings are not only to be guarded but also to be put to work.

items.title: Clear the ground for growth

captions.C: Shed the superfluous and adapt quickly

items.meaning: You know how to rebuild your household: cut needless spending, find your feet quickly in change and keep a reserve.
text: You shed what has outlived itself easily, like a snake its skin. Death teaches you to get rid of what you don't need in time: subscriptions you don't use, things that only take up space, spending out of old habit. You adapt quickly when circumstances change, always keep a reserve and trust each other in money decisions.

When one of you decides to change profession, you rework the budget in an evening: you give up the second car, move to a smaller flat, sell off half your wardrobe. For a year you live modestly and without complaint, and when the new work starts bringing in more than the old, the other is the first to say: “See, it was worth it.” **Your prosperity grows from the courage to let go of what no longer serves.**

Changes in money are frightening when one fears them more than the other. It is frightening to change jobs, frightening that the other will grow and become someone else — and a partner's growth is met with jealousy. Debts are shifted onto each other, and neither can be bothered to get to grips with the finances. Death demands honesty: you let go of the old together, and you begin the new together too, not each at their own expense.

items.title: Exactly as much as you need

captions.C: Live within your means and without clutter

items.meaning: You live within your means and without fuss: you spend in moderation, don't chase others' standards and hoard nothing.
text: Money in your home is neither cramped nor roomy — just right. Temperance runs the household within your means: spending in balance with income, no keeping up with the neighbours, a home without superfluous things. You are content with what you have, you help those close to you and always return what you borrow, and you think over purchases exactly as long as they are worth.
