Both are sure they judge fairly, only each measures by their own yardstick — and neither notices that what hurts the other is the tone itself, not the substance of the complaint.

A parcel that one of you promised to collect is still at the post office. The other doesn't shout but calmly lists: last Tuesday you forgot too, in March you didn't call the repairman, while they, by the way, have not let anyone down once all month. The accused produces a counter-list. By midnight each has a folder of evidence, and the parcel is still sitting there. **Your conflict is not about the deed but about the score each keeps alone and believes is the only correct one.**

The most dangerous thing is that admitting fault means losing the case. Nobody says “sorry, that was me”, because a verdict will follow. You stop making promises so as not to answer for them later. The cold builds up, while on the surface everything is smooth — like flatmates who neatly divide the fridge shelves and have long stopped talking.

items.title: A silence that piles up

captions.G: Retreating into yourself instead of talking

items.meaning: What spoils things for you is not shouting but silence: each withdraws into their shell and handles the hard stuff alone.
text: Your troubles grow in quiet. In conflict the Hermit teaches each of you to cope alone: hurt is lived through in silence, problems are solved single-handedly, help is never asked for — “I'll sort it out myself.” On the surface all is calm, there are almost no quarrels, but beneath that smooth water builds up everything that has never once been said aloud.

For a week one of you walks around gloomy: something is going wrong at work. The other asks, hears “everything's fine” and stops asking. A month later it turns out the first has long been looking for a new job and has already been to three interviews, and the other learns about it from mutual friends. The hurt is not about changing jobs. **What wounds is something else: in what mattered most, each of you turned out to be alone, though you were side by side.**

Silence easily slides into nit-picking. Unspoken irritation comes out sideways — remarks about an unwashed cup, criticism of how the other spends their time. Each proves they are right without explaining why, and sinks deeper into work or their own affairs. There are fewer friends, and fewer shared topics too. You don't quarrel, you drift apart, and that is quieter than any row but costs more.

items.title: Swings: lull, then storm

captions.G: Blaming fate and each other for a losing streak

items.meaning: Your rows go in circles — lull, storm, lull again — and in a bad patch it is easy to cast your partner as the culprit.
text: Your fallings-out go round in circles. In your conflicts the Wheel of Fortune rocks you back and forth: a quiet week, then a storm out of nowhere, then quiet again, as if nothing had happened. In a good stretch you get on wonderfully, but in a bad one each looks for someone to blame: fate, circumstances, the boss — and, since they happen to be right there, the partner.

A big contract has fallen through for one of you, the other's bonus has been cut, and nobody has cancelled the loan repayment. In the evening neither feels like discussing the budget, and you keep quiet. Three days later, an explosion: “If you hadn't talked me into that trip…” — “If you hadn't dragged your feet looking for work…”. Peace returns only together with the money. **Bad luck comes from outside, but the quarrel you bring in yourselves — when you look for its author in each other.**

The swings go higher when problems are left to drift. You didn't discuss the debt — it grew; you didn't talk about the hurt — it flared up a month later over something else. Each turn of the wheel leaves a residue, and in time you stop trusting even a good stretch: you wait for it to end. There is one way out — to meet a bad stretch shoulder to shoulder, against it rather than against each other.

items.title: Who out-stubborns whom

captions.G: Measuring strength and demanding the other measure up

items.meaning: Each quarrel is a duel of characters: both strong, both stubborn, and neither wants to give way first.
text: You quarrel like two strong people — in earnest and to the last. Here Strength turns an argument into a duel: each has their own truth, their own pride and their own expectations of the other — what they should be like, how they should look, how much they should achieve. For you giving way is almost the same as losing, and neither of you knows how to lose.

The conversation starts innocently: “Maybe you should change jobs, since you're not growing there?” The other hears a reproach and answers with a jab about someone else's unrealised plans. Half an hour later you are speaking different languages: one about care, the other about being measured yet again by someone else's ruler. Nobody raises their voice, but nobody backs down either. **Any phrase between you can sound like a challenge, and each of you feels bound to answer a challenge.**

A duel is dangerous because it has a winner. The one who gave way remembers the defeat and gets even later — with mockery in front of friends, with coldness, with a pointed “whatever you say”. Demands on each other grow, while tenderness dwindles: what tenderness can there be with a rival? You need strength not to out-stubborn each other but to be the first to unclench your fist and say: “Let's not do it this way.”

items.title: A sacrifice that sends a bill

captions.G: Playing on pity and piling up silent sacrifices

items.meaning: Your conflicts grow from silent sacrifices: one gives way, stores it up and one day presents the bill.
text: With you, shouting comes last; it all begins with giving way. In difficult moments the Hanged Man teaches you to give up what is yours for the other's sake — plans, wishes, weekends — and to do it silently. Each sacrifice seems small, but they are all written into an invisible ledger, and one day the bill arrives.

For the fifth summer running one of you holidays where the other wants — with their relatives, at their family's country house — without a single objection. On the sixth, when the other suggests the same place again, they explode: “I've spent my whole life fitting in with you!” The other is stunned: they never knew it was a sacrifice. **The explosion had been building for years — out of every “yes” that was really a “no”.**

Self-sacrifice can also become a way to control. Pity is played on, the other is reminded how much has been given, hurt is put on show. One holds the union together with all their might and hears only reproaches in return; the other feels forever in debt. The Hanged Man asks you to turn the view around: help needs no repayment, and a “no” said in time protects a relationship better than a dozen silent concessions.

items.title: Fighting a shadow from the past

captions.G: Comparing with the past and rushing change

items.meaning: Conflict comes from the past and from haste: one carries old fears, the other hurries change along.
text: Your quarrels often involve people who have long been gone. In difficult times Death brings an unfinished past into your life together: old grievances, habits learned earlier — in a parental home or a previous life — and the fear that it will all happen again. One pins other people's sins on their partner, the other rushes change to start with a clean slate sooner — and neither keeps pace with the other.

One of you is late at work and doesn't call. Nothing special — but the other suddenly goes cold: a father once came home late in exactly the same way, and afterwards the house stood silent for months. In the evening, instead of “how was your day”, there is an interrogation, and the latecomer cannot understand what they are on trial for. **The quarrel is not with the one beside you but with the shadow of someone who once caused pain.**

Something else knocks the ground from under you too: more change than can be borne. One changes job, city and plans every six months and demands that the other change along with them. The other clings to stability and picks at every trifle, just so that something stays the same. Death needs an order: first say goodbye to the old — past grievances and other people's scripts — and only then build the new.

items.title: Scales that each of you rocks

captions.G: Losing all measure and pulling to opposite extremes

items.meaning: Discord comes when measure is lost: one rushes, the other drags; one saves, the other spends, and there is no middle.
text: Trouble begins where the middle is lost. When things get hard, Temperance rocks the scales: one saves, the other spends; one hurries, the other dawdles; one boils over, the other is cold as ice. Each pulls to their own extreme, sure they are balancing the other — and your common language gets lost somewhere in between.

Over one weekend one of you manages to buy a new coffee machine, sign up for a course and suggest moving house. The other answers everything with “let's wait” and hides the bank statement. By Sunday evening you both sit in silence, staring at different screens: arguing is pointless, each speaks their own language. **You balance each other — right up until the scales break.**

It is coldest when one stops arguing and simply shuts down. Problems are not discussed, decisions are postponed, and what could have become a compromise becomes a truce without peace. You live side by side, politely and evenly, and more and more often cannot see why. Measure returns not through silence but through blending: each of you will have to step out of your extreme towards the other.

items.title: A grip instead of trust

captions.G: Jealousy, pressure and making up through passion

items.meaning: Your discord grows from the wish to possess: jealousy, pressure and reconciliations after which nothing is settled.
text: Your troubles grow out of a grip. In your fights the Devil makes attachment heavy: you want the other to be yours alone, to know their place and not look around. Jealousy flares over a trifle, pressure passes itself off as care, and every argument soon becomes a question of power: who gives way to whom, who holds on to whom.

One of you is getting ready for a school reunion. The other forbids nothing — they just say nothing all evening, and next morning it turns out the joint holiday is off: “Why would you want to go with me when it's so much fun there.” Three days later, a stormy reconciliation, gifts, vows. A month later it all repeats over something else. **Your quarrels do not settle the argument; they test who holds whom more tightly.**

Drama becomes a habit when calm starts to feel like boredom. Speaking in words is hard; it is easier to press — with money, silence, a threat to leave. Desires are not discussed but guessed, and a wrong guess is punished. The Devil reminds you of something simple and hard: force can hold on to time and promises, but not the wish to be close.

items.title: Words that are never forgotten

captions.G: Hitting with words and threatening to leave

items.meaning: Your quarrels are like a landslide: sudden and loud, and what is said in the heat stays in memory a long time.
text: Your disagreements don't smoulder — they explode. Here the Tower turns a small argument into a landslide: irritation builds for weeks and then collapses all at once, and everything is thrown in — old grievances, the other's weak spots, the harshest words. The storm passes quickly, but what was said settles in memory like dust after a demolition.

A squabble about the plumber somebody was supposed to call goes, in five minutes, to “you never do anything” and “maybe we should just split up”. By morning you have both cooled down, apologised and fixed the tap together. And a month later, in another quarrel, one of you quotes that night-time phrase word for word. **Your quarrels end quickly, but their words stay on to live in the house.**

The collapses come more often when everyday matters have no order: nobody knows whose turn it is, and the other's needs are noticed only once they are already shouting. Each explosion leaves a crack, and in time you start moving round each other carefully, as over an old floor. The Tower does not demand a life without storms, but it asks for one rule: in a quarrel, leave the foundation alone — don't threaten to leave and don't say words you can never take back.

items.title: When the ideal lets you down

captions.G: Measuring against an ideal and dousing the other's dream

items.meaning: Rifts open when a real person is measured against a dream of them — and keeps losing.
text: Your fault line runs where reality falls short of the dream. Where things get hard, the Star lights up an ideal picture in each of you — what a partner should be like, what your union and your life should be — and the living person beside you keeps failing to fit it. Discontent is rarely voiced directly: it hides in comparisons, sighs and polite silence.

In the evening an acquaintance posts photos of an anniversary surprise: balloons, dinner on a rooftop. Nothing is said, but the other feels a comparison hanging in the room. Soon they raise it themselves: “Of course, I'm not the rooftop type…” **What comes between you is not a deed but a picture one of you holds the other up against.**

The light goes out when the ideal starts to smother the other's dream. One tailors the other to their image, criticises their pursuits — “that's not serious” — and issues ultimatums. The other is ashamed to be themselves and says less and less about what they want. The infatuation remains, but nobody takes responsibility for what is shared: as soon as something serious has to be decided, the dreaming stops. The Star needs not an ideal couple but a real one, where each may shine in their own way.

items.title: Arguing with an imagined person

captions.G: Second-guessing the other and believing your fears

items.meaning: Discord is born of guesswork: each quarrels not with a living person but with the one their anxiety has drawn.
text: Your hardest quarrels are with someone who does not exist. In hard times the Moon sets the imagination running: silence seems like coldness, staying late at work like a secret, a chance remark like a hint. Each composes the other's thoughts for them and ends up quarrelling not with them but with the figure their anxiety has filled in.

One evening a promised call never comes. Within two hours the one waiting has imagined everything: hurt feelings, love gone cold, someone else in the messages. When the other comes home with a bag of tangerines, they are met with a chill and a “so where were you?” in a tone that suggests the answer is already known. **The quarrel begins long before you meet — in a story one of you wrote while the other was away.**

It hurts even more when secrets become weapons. In a quarrel, things told in confidence are dragged up, and the fear of losing the other turns into bans: don't see those people, don't stay late there. Nobody gives way, because each is sure they are defending themselves. The Moon asks for something simple and hard: ask before you believe your guess.

items.title: Two suns in one sky

captions.G: Outshining each other and competing in success

items.meaning: Discord flares when each wants to shine brighter: successes are compared, wins claimed and weakness never forgiven.
text: One sky can feel crowded for the two of you. When things get difficult, the Sun makes each of you a bit of a star who needs the spotlight: successes are compared, praise is counted, and the other's win stings more than your own failure. Your expectations of each other are high, and whoever falls short of them feels left in the shade.

At a friends' party one of you talks about their promotion, and the other adds: “Well, without my advice you'd still be stuck in your old job.” Everyone laughs, and on the way home a storm breaks: who owes whom, who sacrificed what, who outshines whom. **You share success more jealously than failure.**

Things get truly hot when brightness turns into control. One decides whom the other may see and in which direction to grow, looks after them so closely that there is no air left, and calls it care. Weakness is not forgiven, complaints are not heard, rest is called laziness. Nobody basks under such a sun — they hide from it. Your light is shared only when each has a place of their own beneath it.

items.title: A third voice at the table

captions.G: Deciding with an eye on family and never admitting fault

items.meaning: The past stirs up discord: old grievances, the voice of relatives and a habit of blaming the other, never yourself.
text: Many of your quarrels do not start with you. In hard moments Judgement brings the past into your relationship: your parents' scripts, old grievances, the family's opinion, which sounds in your head even when no relatives are around. You accuse each other but hear yourselves less well, and admitting “I'm no better” turns out to be harder than sitting out a week of cold.

Before buying a sofa, one of you asks their mother's advice; she is against it, and the other is the last to hear: “You know, Mum thinks it's too early for us.” The argument quickly slides into the past: and when we bought the car, did your mother decide that too, and remember what happened at the wedding… **It is not the sofa that sets you quarrelling but a third voice that one of you trusts more than the other.**

It is dangerous when a sharp chill takes the place of a conversation. Neither says what they feel, both wait for the other to admit fault first, and time works against you: grievances build an archive, and the family's complaints are added to it. Judgement needs an honest review: own your share, separate your parents' voice from your own and finally reach a verdict together.

items.title: Groundhog Day for two

captions.G: Reshaping the other's world to fit your own

items.meaning: Things go wrong when each fits the other into their own picture of the world, and the shared one shrinks to one script.
text: Your discord starts with the wish to assemble the world to your own blueprint. Where difficulties arise, the World convinces each of you that you know how life should be arranged — and you want to fit the other into that picture too: their friends, hobbies, views, weekend plans. While the pictures match, all goes smoothly. When they don't, a quiet re-education begins.

For three years one of you has been going to pottery classes, and the other calls it “your pots” — jokingly, it seems, in front of guests, with a smile. Each joke is small, but after the tenth the first stops telling how the class went. **What hurts is not the joke but that your shared world found no room for this passion.**

The world shrinks to Groundhog Day: the same routes, quarrels to the old script, reproaches learned by heart long ago. There are no agreements, each insists on their own way, and disagreement comes out not in words but in a barb or a silence. Sometimes you split up and get back together without ever talking it through. A shared world is possible only if it has room for two different people.

items.title: A joke that stopped being funny

captions.G: Running from the serious and breaking your word

items.meaning: What spoils things is not taking life seriously: promises of “later”, dodging hard talks and freedom with no shores.
text: Your quarrels are born of a lightness that has gone too far. In conflict the Fool teaches you to run: from a hard conversation, from a decision, from answering for what was said. Today you agree, tomorrow one of you changes their mind, the day after it has all been turned into a joke — and the other cannot work out what here can be relied on at all.

The car insurance was due, and one of you promised to renew it — then went fishing with friends instead: “Relax, there's time.” The deadline passed, a fine arrived, and the reproach was answered with a funny sticker in the chat. The other is not laughing, and the joke becomes the last straw of the month. **Patience runs out not over a single slip but because anything serious keeps being put off until later.**

Most hurtful of all is that each has their own rules of freedom. One wants complete liberty for themselves and is jealous if the other is late without calling. The status of the relationship hangs in the air, agreements shift with the mood, and any talk about the future ends with “don't be so heavy”. The Fool need not turn into a bore, but a word given to another is not a game.

items.title: A garden that grows from care

captions.spiritual: Grow living things: a home, a venture, a family

items.meaning: You value what grows from care — a home, a venture, a family — and your path is to plant and wait for the harvest together.
text: You measure life by what has grown. The Empress puts fertility in the broadest sense among your values: a home that is warm, a business raised from nothing, young ones you have brought up, a garden where every tree remembers who planted it. Spending good time together is not enough for you — you want something to bloom after you.

You buy an old house with an overgrown plot, and the first spring goes on clearing the rubbish. One of you lays out the vegetable beds, the other battles a leaking roof, and in the evenings you sit on the porch, dirty and content. A couple of years later you have apples to hand out to the neighbours and a habit of inviting friends “for the harvest”. **Your measure of happiness is what has sprung up from your care and now feeds more than just you.**

A garden demands all your attention, and it is easy to give it everything. You raise a home, a business or children and forget to water each other: talk is only about the household, rest is “once everything is done”. It is worse when only one of you grows: one partner's business has taken off, while the other is stuck in daily chores and feels more and more like an appendage to someone else's harvest. Abundance piles up, and the one who created it quietly wilts in the shade of their own apple trees.

items.title: Love as a daily choice

captions.spiritual: Choose each other again, and for real

items.meaning: Your core value is love as a choice: not once and for all, but again and again, as adults and with open eyes.
text: For you love is not a state you once fell into but a decision you keep making. The Lovers put choice at the centre of your relationship: made with the heart, but with open eyes, knowing both the best and the awkward sides of the other. Your shared path is to keep that “yes” alive once the novelty has worn off and the person beside you turns out to be an ordinary human with habits of their own.

Year ten, a Tuesday, exhaustion. One of you grumbles about an unwashed frying pan, the other snaps back — and suddenly you both fall silent and laugh: you have remembered how you once argued over whose turn it was to call first. The quarrel is never finished; it has simply stopped mattering. In the evening you walk the same route as on your first date, though there is a mountain of things to do. **Your union holds because you choose each other not from memory but anew — on weekdays too.**

The choice fades when you start choosing an improved version instead of the person. “I love you, but if only you…” — and then a list: work less, dress better, talk about feelings more often. Each correction is small, but together they say: you were accepted on conditions. The one being corrected learns to measure up and stops being themselves, and the one doing the correcting misses more and more the person they once fell in love with.

items.title: Two lanterns on one path

captions.spiritual: Seek meaning and go deep rather than wide

items.meaning: You would rather understand than keep up: your shared path leads deep, to a meaning you reach slowly and together.
text: Getting through the day is not enough for you — you want to know what it was for. The Hermit puts meaning at the heart of your values: not how much you managed, but what you worked out, what you understood about yourselves and each other. Your path goes deep rather than wide, and you walk it unhurried: each of you carries a lantern of your own, but both shine on the same path.

Friends invite you to a loud milestone birthday, and once again you choose an evening in the kitchen: one of you has read a book that turned their week upside down, the other asks questions until two in the morning. From the outside nothing has changed by the next day, but you both know you have moved on. A year of such evenings grows into a decision no one around you understands: to change careers, to study again, to move to a small town. **Your wealth as a couple is the understanding you reached yourselves and checked against each other.**

Depth becomes a well when you go down into it alone. Each of you thinks things through in silence and comes out to the other with a finished conclusion that is not up for discussion. Friends stop calling — you would say no anyway; new people seem shallow, the world outside too loud. The lanterns still burn, only each in its own cell, and the path between them grows over.

items.title: Seeing the world upside down

captions.spiritual: Give without counting and see differently

items.meaning: You value what others call a loss — a pause, a missed gain, help with no calculation — and find meaning in it.
text: From the outside your values often look odd. The Hanged Man turns the familiar picture over: where others see a missed gain, you see meaning; where everyone hurries, you stop and look differently. Your shared path is to give without keeping score and not to fear pauses: in them you both understand better where you are going.

You give up a seaside holiday because a friend needs help moving, and for another month you spend your weekends ferrying his boxes. The relatives tap their temples. Yet you remember that August as one of your best: working shoulder to shoulder, talking about everything, seeing each other in action. **What you value is not what you received but what you were able to give — and looking at life together from a new angle.**

Giving turns into sacrifice once it starts being counted. One of you always gives way — time, plans, money — and silently waits for it to be noticed. The other doesn't notice, because it has always been so. One day what has built up bursts out as a reproach: “I gave up everything for you…” — and the generosity you were proud of turns out to be a ledger of debts. The Hanged Man teaches you to give freely and to ask for yourself in good time.

items.title: Together of your own free will

captions.spiritual: Desire openly and never own each other

items.meaning: Above all you value a union where strong desire never turns into a right of ownership.
text: Your union tests one idea for strength: nobody belongs to anybody. The Devil brings the force of desire into your relationship — pull, passion, a thirst to live vividly — and honesty about the dark things others hide even from themselves. The value you are moving towards is to stay together by free will, held not by a chain but by choice, and to say your desires out loud, even the awkward ones.

One of you admits a wish to go and work in the far north for six months: good money, rare experience. The other goes cold at first — and still asks not “what about me?” but “what do you need to make up your mind?”. Six months of evening calls, and a homecoming after which you hold hands like in the first month. **You know that what holds strongest is not a lock but a door nobody ever locked.**

The pull turns dark when the wish to be close becomes the wish to own. Checking a phone “just because”, choosing the other's friends, holding them by money, a shared flat or guilt — each move feels like care, and together they add up to a leash. The one being held starts to break free or gives up, and either way desire leaves. What remains is a habit of each other that looks like love the way a cage looks like a home.

items.title: Understood without translation

captions.spiritual: Trust intuition and guard your inner world

items.meaning: You treasure a world only the two of you can see: intuition, fantasies and secrets that need no explaining.
text: The most precious thing about you is not on show. The Moon leads you both along a night road: instinct instead of a map, dreams and fantasies instead of five-year plans, understanding at a glance. Your shared path is not to hide this inner world from each other or fear getting lost in it, but over the years to grow into each other so that the line between “my hunch” and “ours” disappears.

You are viewing a flat, and everything fits — the area, the price, south-facing windows. In the lift you exchange a glance and say “no” at the same moment. You cannot explain it to the estate agent, and to each other you do not need to. A week later you find another one, awkward and odd, with a bay window and creaking parquet, and you both know: this is it. **Your shared compass is intuition you trust more than arguments, because the two of you share a single one.**

The night road frightens when the lantern goes out. Intuition gives way to anxiety, and each fills in the other's thoughts: home late — must be hiding something; said nothing — must be hurt. Instead of a conversation, guesses; instead of a question, a scene played out in your head. The secret that joined you becomes a wall, and you walk along it, afraid to knock. The Moon asks one thing: test fear with words before it grows into a whole story.

items.title: Complete, but never frozen

captions.spiritual: Freedom, trust and the union of two worlds

items.meaning: You want life gathered into a whole that never sets: out of fullness, your next step is always born.
text: What matters to you is the sense that life is gathered into a whole, with no missing pieces. This is the fullness of the World, and in your relationship it is alive: what has come together is not the end of the road, you carry it onward. Everything is in its place — and yet nothing has frozen: each year your whole looks a little different and stays whole.

There are days when everything has come together: work is done, there is nothing to argue about, nothing urgent ahead. Other people want to freeze on such a day and touch nothing. For you that is exactly when someone says, “Listen, what if we…” — and soon there is a second-hand piano in the room that neither of you can play. **Your union exists so that fullness never becomes a final sum: out of “we have it all” you grow the next step.**

The whole sets hard when you start guarding it from change. You already have everything, and every “let's try” meets a polite “what for?”: the same weekend routes, the same conversations, the same jokes. Your world turns into a museum where everything is beautiful and nothing may be touched. But you put it together on the move, and it feels cramped under glass: a single “let's” is enough to set the whole spinning again.

items.meaning: The partnership is fertile as long as growth doesn't turn into rivalry.
text: Your partnership stands on the urge to make things grow. The Empress makes it fertile: you both enjoy watching the business flourish, look after clients and team, and create around you the comfort and order people want to work in. Practicality goes hand in hand with generosity here, and joint work brings visible results — new products, people, income. The foundation cracks when rivalry for influence begins — who brought in how much, whose opinion matters more — along with disdain for whoever is growing more slowly for now.

items.meaning: On order and roles the business stands firm — until rules start to matter more than people.
text: The foundation of your partnership is order. The Emperor builds it like a solid household: roles are assigned, rules are clear, decisions are made rather than left hanging, and each has an area they answer for entirely. Trust here grows from simple knowledge: the other will do what they promised. Such a business withstands crises and grows slowly but surely. The foundation turns into a barracks when order matters more than people: rules for the sake of rules, control over every step, and two masters start dividing not tasks but power.

captions.base: Shared convictions and rules of the trade

items.meaning: The venture rests on shared values and rules; don't slide from sharing experience into lecturing.
text: You are partners by conviction. The Hierophant holds the shared venture on common views: what counts as honest work, how to treat clients, which rules are never broken whatever the deadline. You talk a lot, learn from each other and share experience gladly, and each one's authority is accepted freely — where they really know the subject. Such a partnership often grows into a school, a method, a recognisable approach. Firmness turns into rigidity when one decides they know what is right for both: then come the lectures, the corrections and attempts to remake the other in their own image.

captions.base: Liking, shared taste and choosing each other

items.meaning: You chose each other not just for practical reasons; raise work issues even when you'd rather not spoil the mood.
text: This partnership is held together by mutual liking. The Lovers stand for a partnership by choice: you came together not just for practical reasons, you enjoy working together, you reach agreement easily, and you share a taste — for the product, for clients, for how the shop window should look. Duties are split equally, decisions are made by the two of you, and clients sense a well-matched team. The weak point is that mood here replaces procedure: a hurtful remark at a planning meeting can stall a project for a week, and important things stay unsaid so as not to spoil the relationship.

captions.base: A shared goal and a high pace

items.meaning: Goal and pace hold you together; so you don't pull in different directions, each line of work needs one owner.
text: Movement lies at the heart of your partnership. The Chariot turns it into a team on the march: there is a goal, a deadline, roles, and neither of you can stand it when the work stalls. Together you easily take on several lines of work at once, and in front of a client or a competitor you stand shoulder to shoulder. The partnership starts to skid when two drivers pull the team in different directions: each wants to decide alone, new things begin before old ones are finished, and speed takes the place of direction. Then a simple rule helps: every line of work has one owner.

items.meaning: Your venture stands on honesty and clear rules; the key is not to turn every trifle into a trial.
text: This partnership rests on honest accounts. Justice makes the relationship transparent: shares are written down, duties divided, expenses recorded, promises kept on time. You trust each other because everything can be checked, and you argue briefly, figures in hand. Such a partnership withstands both a tax audit and a shift in the market. Honesty turns into a ledger of grievances when each of you starts keeping an invisible tally — who put in more, who stays late more often, who owes whom — and every small inaccuracy is treated as a breach of contract.

captions.base: Knowing the trade and considered decisions

items.meaning: Expertise and unhurried decisions are the bedrock; the danger is each of you silently shutting yourself away.
text: The foundation of your venture is depth. The Hermit unites people who are better at substance than at self-promotion: you spend a long time refining the product, study the market before entering it and talk to clients to the point. You give each other space — nobody pesters the other ten times a day, and decisions are made with thought. The same quiet is dangerous: each closes off in their own area, difficulties pile up unspoken, and sales are postponed because it is “not ready yet”. Bring the shared work into the light more often than seems necessary.

captions.base: A knack for catching the chance in time

items.meaning: Flexibility and a sense of timing are your support; in a downturn look for a solution, not someone to blame.
text: A sense of timing is what your partnership stands on. The Wheel of Fortune brings together people who turn up in the right place at the right moment: together you quickly spot an opening niche, switch to a new product, change suppliers without long hesitation. A bad month does not shake your trust — you both know the wheel will turn again. The weak spot lies in the streaks: on the rise everything falls into place, but in a slump decisions are put off “until better times”, money goes on patching holes, and each secretly blames the other for the bad luck. Your support is an agreement to look for a fix, not a culprit.

captions.base: Trust, composure and one line of thought

items.meaning: The partnership stands on trust and calm strength; argue about the task, not about who is stronger.
text: Your partnership holds on composure and trust. Strength gives the partners one direction of thought: you discuss hard things calmly, respect each other's strong points and can give way where the other knows better. Pressure from a client or a failed quarter you bear without panic — you both have the character not to snap. The same strength becomes a problem when it is aimed not at the task but at each other: an argument over a trifle turns into a duel, each believes that giving way means losing, and decisions stall on principle.

captions.base: Patience and a view from an unexpected angle

items.meaning: Your partnership knows how to wait and find a way round; make sure waiting doesn't become stagnation.
text: Patience is the main cement of your partnership. The Hanged Man at the centre unites people ready to wait for results longer than others would: you invest in a project that will not pay off at once, help each other without keeping score and look at tasks from an unexpected angle — where competitors see a dead end, you find a way round. Often the venture means more to you than profit. The danger comes when patience turns into stagnation: for years the project is “about to take off”, one partner carries everything in silence, and decisions are put off because it is “too early”.

captions.base: Readiness to change and start afresh

items.meaning: The partnership rests on a readiness to let go of the old; keep something that does not change.
text: Your partnership was born of change and lives by it. Death at the centre brings together people who don't cling to the old: you easily close what has stopped working, rebuild processes, change the model when the market demands it, and don't waste years on regret. Often such a partnership arises after a crisis — one or both of you start over, and the shared venture becomes a new chapter. The foundation grows shaky when renewal becomes a habit: everything changes so often that nothing constant is left to lean on, and one partner tires of the endless rebuilding before the other.

captions.base: Balance, measure and the art of agreement

items.meaning: Balance and the art of agreement hold you together, as long as the unsaid doesn't pile up for years.
text: Everything here rests on balance. Temperance unites people who complement each other and can agree without shouting: disputes are settled by talking, decisions are made when both agree, and work goes at an even pace without crunches. You feel calm around each other, and clients and the team sense that calm. The foundation weakens when peace becomes more important than the business: unpleasant things go unsaid, one keeps giving way, and a year later it turns out too much has been left unspoken.

items.meaning: Shared ambition holds you together; make sure the wish for success doesn't become a wish to possess.
text: The partnership holds on shared ambition. The Devil draws together people who want a lot and are not ashamed of it: big money, influence, high-profile projects. You understand each other's ambitions, forgive slips, talk openly about desires and back the other powerfully when they go all in. Such a foundation gives the business an energy cautious competitors lack. It turns dangerous where the wish for success becomes a wish to possess: control over the partner, manipulation, obligations that bind ever tighter, and a feeling that there is no longer any way out of this partnership.

captions.base: Solidarity in a crisis and directness

items.meaning: Trials and directness bring you together; don't let the partnership live only in emergency mode.
text: Trials bring you closer than successes do. The Tower at the centre gathers people who don't lose their heads when everything collapses: you make serious decisions quickly, support each other at a hard moment and can rebuild the business if the old one fell apart. There is little pretence between you — the truth is told directly, even when unpleasant. Such a foundation withstands what breaks other partnerships. The danger comes when the partnership starts to live only in emergency mode: the tension never drops, irritation breaks out in harsh words, and calm periods seem suspiciously dull.

captions.base: Understanding without words and a shared atmosphere

items.meaning: Instinct and a shared atmosphere bind you; still, move agreements out of thin air and onto paper.
text: More than any contract, you are held together by a shared sixth sense. The Moon creates a partnership where much is understood without words: you both sense where the market is heading, guess clients' moods and are drawn to unusual, creative tasks. You trust each other with secrets and guard your shared space from prying eyes. Such a partnership can create a business with a special atmosphere. The weak spot lies in the same unspokenness: agreements hang in the air, each fills in the gaps for the other, and one misunderstood word can sow a suspicion that is hard to dispel later.

captions.base: Loyalty, a shared history and forgiveness

items.meaning: Loyalty and a shared history are your capital; old grievances are worth forgiving for real.
text: Loyalty is the foundation of this partnership. Judgement binds people who hold on to each other for a long time: you may be united by a shared history, family, an old acquaintance or simply a readiness to forgive slips and offer a shoulder to lean on at a hard moment. You take each other into account in decisions and guard the shared venture's reputation like a family name. The foundation grows heavy when the past starts running the present: old grievances are not truly forgiven, words part ways with deeds, and nobody dares to say what doesn't suit them.

items.meaning: Freedom and trust are your glue; write down at least the main agreements before money comes into it.
text: Lightness is what holds you together. The Fool gives the partnership freedom and liveliness: you don't keep each other on a short leash, you back crazy ideas and can start from scratch without drama. Working together is fun, and failures become stories you laugh about later. Such a partnership easily survives crises that would break more serious people. The weak spot is the absence of a frame: the status of the partnership is undefined, duties are not written down, and when it comes to money or a hard decision, it turns out each understood the agreements in their own way.

captions.finIn: A generous start and quick first clients

items.meaning: The start will be generous; for six months spend only on what grows income, not on what decorates it.
text: Money in this deal appears easily — like the first shoots in good soil. With the Empress the start is generous: the first clients come quickly, people like the product, and investment in quality and customer care pays off sooner than expected. The catch of the start is the temptation to live large right away: a handsome office, expensive packaging, spending on comfort before the flow has become steady. Hence the swings between plenty and nothing. For the first six months spend only on what grows income, not on what decorates it.

captions.finIn: A plan, capital and the first big contract

items.meaning: A plan and the first big contract give you a base; decide in advance what each may spend without sign-off.
text: Here money begins with a plan. The Emperor draws up the scheme in advance: a business plan, start-up capital, a clear income structure, a first big contract that gives you a base. Slowness and rigidity hold the start back: decisions on the first expenses take a long time, everything is checked ten times over, and the opportunity has time to go to a competitor. Another trap is agreeing every trifle between the two of you. Agree which expenses each may make without the other's approval — that will speed up the start.

captions.finIn: Paperwork, approvals and recommendations

items.meaning: Income starts after the paperwork and approvals; allow time for them in the plan.
text: Money enters this deal through official doors. With the Hierophant the first income appears once everything has been done by the rules: the contract signed, the licence obtained, the approvals through, and a respected person's recommendation has opened the way to the first clients. Formalities and waiting slow the start: a month for approval, another for reworking documents, and the money is delayed though the work is already under way. Don't try to skip this stage — here it pays off. Better to allow time for it in the plan and not promise the first clients impossible deadlines.

captions.finIn: First orders from a warm circle

items.meaning: The first orders come through people you know; keep one price list for everyone and don't spread yourselves thin.
text: The first clients of this deal will most likely come through people you know. The Lovers open the way to money through a warm circle: friends, former colleagues, people who like you and your product. It is a quick and pleasant start, but there is a catch: it is awkward to charge acquaintances the full price, and even more awkward to ask them to pay on time. You also want to take on everything at once, and income gets scattered. It helps to keep one price list for everyone from the first order and decide which two or three lines you develop and which you set aside for now.

captions.finIn: Active selling from day one

items.meaning: Activity and sales get income going; start with one line of work, not all of them at once.
text: This deal gets off to a fast start in money. The Chariot earns its first money through activity: calls, trips, meetings, entering several platforms at once. Whoever acts, earns — waiting for clients to find you is pointless here. What usually lets you down is haste: you want to open everything at once, take a loan for expansion before the first profit, and spur each other on when someone slows down. It is safer to start with one line, bring it to a stable income and only then pick up speed.

captions.finIn: Order in the paperwork from the first invoice

items.meaning: The first money depends on order in the paperwork; write in prepayment and a late-payment penalty from the start.
text: The way into money here starts with paperwork. Justice hands the first receipts to the careful: a contract with a clear payment schedule, invoices without errors, accounts kept from day one rather than “we'll sort it out later”. Delays get in the way at the start: the client is slow to pay, the acceptance papers come back for correction, the bank asks for documents. All of it can be solved if you keep order from the very beginning. A good move is to write prepayment and a late-payment penalty into the very first contract, while both sides are still in a friendly mood.

captions.finIn: Long preparation and payment for knowledge

items.meaning: Income comes late and through knowledge; set a date after which the product goes on sale.
text: The money in this deal needs time to arrive. The Hermit prepares at length: studies the market, refines the product, looks for first clients who come through recommendation rather than advertising. The first money will be modest and tied to your knowledge — a consultation, expert advice, one-off craft work. Indecision gets in the way: you are ready to improve endlessly but not to name a price and put yourselves forward. It helps to set a date after which the product goes to market as it is.

captions.finIn: A lucky turn of circumstances

items.meaning: Early money may come by luck and stop just as suddenly; plan spending by the weakest month, not the best.
text: Early income here depends a great deal on timing. The Wheel of Fortune may bring money unexpectedly: a good order in the very first week, a client who found you on their own, a market that turned your way. But the flow can stop just as suddenly, and the opening period will come in fits and starts — feast one month, famine the next. The key is not to take the first stroke of luck for the rule and not to hand out promises against money you don't have yet. Plan start-up spending by the weakest month, not the first good one.

captions.finIn: First money through sheer persistence

items.meaning: The first income will be won by persistence; decide in advance how to count time invested, not only money.
text: The first income here has to be wrung out. Strength demands that you carry the launch, persuade the first clients, work more than agreed and not give up after the first refusals. But you have the character to get through this stage, and the first money comes precisely thanks to persistence. Such a start breaks down from overstrain: one takes on the main weight of the launch, the other feels like an assistant, and the argument about who put in more effort begins before the first profit. Agree in advance how invested time is counted, not just money.

captions.finIn: Investing up front and income that lags

items.meaning: Money will be late; set a date after which you change the approach instead of waiting longer.
text: The first money here will take some waiting for. With the Hanged Man you invest first — time, effort, money — and income arrives late: clients pay later, the project ripens longer than planned. Often the first orders involve helping people or an unconventional solution the market won't appreciate at once. The weak spot of the start is self-sacrifice: work “for the experience”, free trial services, money you feel awkward asking for. Set yourselves a deadline: if income hasn't started by then, it is time to change the approach, not to keep waiting.

captions.finIn: A new business where the old one closed

items.meaning: The new begins where the old has ended; close out past debts before you start.
text: In this deal, earning starts with shutting something down. Death clears the ground: a previous business, post or project has ended, and the strength and funds released go into the new venture. The first income arrives when you can get your bearings quickly and cut unnecessary costs. Loose ends from the past pull you back: debts and obligations carried into the new project, or a fear of letting go of the old for good that keeps one foot there. Settle your old accounts before the start — then the new venture begins clean.

captions.finIn: An even start and pooled resources

items.meaning: Income gathers strength gradually; set out each one's input from day one so the even start doesn't breed grievances.
text: Calmly and without leaps — that is how earning begins here. Temperance promises a gradual inflow of money as you set up processes step by step, gather the first regular clients and find your price. A combination of resources works well: one has capital, the other connections or skills. You can stumble over an imbalance: one puts in more money or time, and there is no agreement on how to account for it. Set out each one's input from day one, and the even start won't turn into grievances.

captions.finIn: High stakes and money with strings attached

items.meaning: A big start is possible, but check every source of money: what freedom do you give up in return?
text: Money comes in big here and demands a firm grip. The Devil plays for high stakes from day one: a large first order others wouldn't take on, an investor, a loan, entry straight into the expensive segment. You have energy and appetite enough, and the first sums can be impressive. Temptations lie in wait at the entrance: quick money through a dubious scheme, loans that bind you to the lender, the wish to grab everything at once. Test every source of start-up capital with one question: what freedom are we giving up in return?

captions.finIn: Renovation and a rebuild before income

items.meaning: A rebuild and investment come before the first money; build a reserve of at least a third into the start-up budget.
text: The start of the money story here resembles a renovation. The Tower first knocks down the old: the previous model has to be taken apart, you invest in premises or equipment and live through a period when costs flow and income is almost nil. The first money may arrive abruptly, once some barrier has been broken. Surprises are the danger: the estimate grows, a contractor lets you down, a client leaves at the last moment. Build a reserve of at least a third into the start-up budget, and don't begin until you have it.

captions.finIn: A talent it is time to put a price on

items.meaning: Talent and inspiration open the way to money; name your price at once rather than waiting for perfection.
text: The first money here comes from what you do best. The Star ties the start to an original product, a creative service, a project that inspires clients and draws attention. The first orders often come thanks to a publication, an exhibition, a word from a well-known person. The hardest part is turning talent into money: you can delight people for free for a long time, or spend the start-up capital on beautiful packaging. Name your price at once, even if the product still seems raw to you.

captions.finIn: Unexpected sources and unclear contributions

items.meaning: The first months will be unpredictable; a shared expenses sheet keeps the fog from thickening.
text: The first money in this deal comes from somewhere other than expected. The Moon makes the beginning unpredictable: the client you counted on drags their feet, while someone you never thought of pays, and the costs prove higher than planned. Intuition will tell you where to move, but it is not enough on its own. The hardest part is the lack of clarity: who put in how much, which costs are shared, what you are counting on in six months. Without written figures the fog thickens, and suspicion settles in easily. Start a shared expenses sheet right away.

captions.finIn: A bright launch and clients drawn by reputation

items.meaning: The launch will be bright; for the first three months put profit into the plan and reserve, not into showing off.
text: The start of this deal is a bright one. With the Sun the first money comes openly and on a grand scale: a visible launch, clients drawn by your reputation, first successes you want to tell everyone about. Faith in the business energises both you and those around you. The trap is overestimation: the first success seems a pledge of more to come, and you start spending on status — an office, presentations, entertaining — before the income has become stable. For the first three months let profit go into the plan and the reserve, not into a display of success.

captions.finIn: Clients from old connections

items.meaning: Old connections bring the first clients; sort out unsettled debts and grievances before launch.
text: The past feeds this deal from the first days. Judgement awakens old connections: former colleagues, previous clients, family and acquaintances who remember your work and recommend you. Sometimes money gets its start from a revived project or an asset inherited from a previous business. Old debts and grievances let you down: if questions with someone from the “past” remain unsettled, they will surface in the very first months. Deal with them before the launch, and agree how contributions from relatives and friends will be accounted for.

captions.finIn: Money from afar and a wide audience

items.meaning: Earnings may come from far away; don't let caution delay your step beyond the familiar.
text: From the very start, the earnings here look far afield. The World sets up a start aimed at a large audience: sales to other cities, online, foreign clients, partners from neighbouring industries. The first money may come from afar — from places you never planned to reach. Caution slows the way in: you want to master your own market down to the last client first, agree on every trifle and only then glance beyond the familiar limits. Set yourselves a date by which the first sales outside your own city should appear.

captions.finIn: A start with almost empty hands

items.meaning: You can start with almost no capital; open a separate business account before the first order.
text: You can start here with almost empty hands. The Fool needs only an idea and a little money to try, and the first orders come from unexpected places. Lightness helps — you are not afraid of mistakes and quickly try new things. The Achilles' heel of the start is carelessness: money goes through personal cards, nobody records expenses, and agreements on who put in how much remain just talk. Six months later such chaos turns into grievances. A separate business account, opened before the first order, spares you that.

captions.finTotal: Growth and plenty while there is peace between you

items.meaning: The deal brings growth and plenty, provided calm and agreement hold between the partners.
text: Harvest is the best word for the financial outcome of this deal. The Empress leads to growth: profit rises from season to season, and the business expands naturally, like a well-tended garden. The outcome depends on the atmosphere between you — this point also lies on the relationship line. In calm and agreement everything grows, while pressure, rivalry and loud disagreements can freeze the prospect at the root. Protect the peace — here it literally brings in money.

captions.finTotal: Predictable income and savings pots for each goal

items.meaning: The outcome will be solid and predictable, unless money becomes a battlefield for power.
text: The financial result of this deal is solid and predictable. The Emperor brings money into a system: in the end you have a stable income and savings pots for different goals, including a reserve for a rainy day. Failures are few, because no large expense is made in the heat of the moment. The weak spot is one-man rule: one decides for both, won't accept the other's ideas, and profit becomes a battlefield for power. At this point money and relationships meet, so dividing authority matters as much as the budget.

captions.finTotal: Steady income through knowledge and a name

items.meaning: A reliable rather than fast result: income grows on knowledge, reputation and keeping to the rules.
text: The money result here is reliable rather than quick. The Hierophant leads to income through knowledge, reputation and keeping to the rules: by the end of the deal you have regular clients who come back because they trust you, and a name others cite. Profit grows slowly but without slumps. What can hold it back is excess caution — fear of any extra expense, endless polishing of the product, arguments about “the proper way”. The outcome is best when you invest in training and in your name rather than skimping on everything.

captions.finTotal: Relationships that bring in money

items.meaning: Profit comes through relationships and referrals; set a limit on entertainment costs in advance.
text: Money in this deal flows through relationships. With the Lovers, income grows when clients love you, acquaintances recommend you and the partners enjoy working together — and the mood between you is tied to profit more closely than usual. The outcome is usually generous, but so is the spending: a handsome office, gifts, entertaining. What lets you down is discounts for “friends” and muddled accounts between you: who owes whom how much is remembered roughly, and after a quarrel each remembers it in their own favour. Set a limit on entertainment costs in advance, not as you go.

captions.finTotal: Fast turnover and constant motion

items.meaning: Money comes through pace and expansion, provided you lock in profit before funding the next push.
text: The financial outcome of the deal depends on whether you can keep up the pace. The Chariot keeps money moving: turnover is fast, projects follow one another, and earnings here come from work and planning, not from waiting. The weak spot is the urge to pour profit straight into the next push: revenue grows, the account stays empty, and the first late payment sends you off to borrow. A good outcome goes to those who bank their profit before chasing more.

captions.finTotal: Clean money and precise accounts

items.meaning: The financial outcome matches the work you put in; clean accounts pay better than any shortcut.
text: The outcome of the deal will be fair in the most literal sense: you get back as much as you put in of work and care. Justice gives neither gifts nor losses out of nowhere: the money is clean, the accounts between partners are transparent, and each can check their own part. Pleasant surprises are rare, but so are failures. Two extremes spoil the result: stinginess that cuts back on what matters, and an attempt to speed up profit with a dubious scheme — in this deal that costs most of all. Keep precise accounts, and the numbers will be on your side.

captions.finTotal: Quiet income from knowledge and a narrow niche

items.meaning: A solid rather than showy income; don't carry everything alone in silence, and ask now and then why not more.
text: Quiet but solid — that is the money outcome of this deal. The Hermit does not chase loud profit: you earn where you know more than others, with a small circle of clients, and such income is hard to take away. At this point money meets relationships: if each silently carries their own area and asks for no help, both the budget and the trust suffer. The weak spot is a lack of ambition: you can work for years for modest money, content with the first stable level. The outcome is helped by whoever asks from time to time: “Why not more?”

captions.finTotal: Good timing and unexpected income

items.meaning: The outcome may be very profitable if you don't borrow against future luck and set aside part of every profit.
text: How the deal ends in money will largely depend on well-chosen timing. The Wheel of Fortune promises unexpected income — a big order, a profitable resale, a rise in demand you caught before others — and equally unexpected pauses. Overall the venture can prove very profitable if you don't overrate the good months. What can spoil the outcome is loans taken against future luck and the hope of “winning it back” after a failure. One rule helps: set aside part of every large profit at once, and risk only a sum you can afford to lose.

captions.finTotal: Profit earned by force of character

items.meaning: Above-average profit is possible if persistence doesn't become pressure and disputes aren't settled by force.
text: Money here goes to the persistent. Strength brings good money to those willing to invest their character: to finish projects others have tired of and keep their word when it costs dear. Profit is usually above average, but earned by work, not luck. The same outcome is easily undermined by pressure: if disputes are settled by force rather than agreement, and giving way means losing, the deal's prospects collapse faster than they grew. Protect both the money and the respect between you.

captions.finTotal: Profit that ripens slowly

items.meaning: Income comes later than expected; say out loud what you expect in return for concessions.
text: The profit from this deal ripens slowly. The Hanged Man postpones the result: first investment, work for the future, deferred payouts — and only then stable income. But by that point you both know the value of money well and know how to manage it. A sense of unfairness is dangerous: if one feels they are sacrificing more, resentment eats up both the relationship and the gain. It helps to see your gain not only in money — experience, connections, reputation — and to say honestly what you expect in return for concessions.

captions.finTotal: Profit in a new place after renewal

items.meaning: Profit appears after renewal; revisit how money is split with every change of model.
text: Change is the key to money in this deal. Death leads to results through renewal: you close what loses money, change the model — and profit appears in a new place, sometimes not where you expected it at all. This point also lies on the relationship line, so money gets stuck here if only one of you is ready to change: they have already rebuilt their part of the business, while the other clings to the old agreements on income. Revisit how profit is split every time you change the model — then renewal feeds you both.

captions.finTotal: The golden mean and peace between partners

items.meaning: Stable income rests on peace between the partners; one-sided concessions destroy it.
text: No failures, no wild leaps — the result of this deal sits in the middle. Temperance leads to income without debts or shocks: money is divided calmly, spending is discussed without scenes, and a reserve lets you ride out a bad season. This point links money with relationships, and here that is especially visible: as long as there is peace between the partners, the outcome is stable. One-sided concessions spoil it: one agrees for years to a smaller share for the sake of calm, and then presents the bill for all the concessions at once.

captions.finTotal: A big outcome and clean rules of the game

items.meaning: Income can be high, provided profit doesn't become a tool of control.
text: Big money is a likely ending for this deal. The Devil raises the stakes to the limit: the sum you arrive at may change the scale of you both, and the clearer your shared goals and the more honest your accounts, the higher the outcome. At this point finances are interwoven with the relationship, and this is the deal's most vulnerable spot: if profit becomes a means of control, or one is forever dissatisfied with the other's contribution, the large sums begin to destroy the partnership. Clean rules of the game are worth more here than any profit.

captions.finTotal: A stress test and an outcome after the shake-up

items.meaning: A shake-up is unavoidable, but afterwards the business may earn more; in a crisis, review the plan, not the blame.
text: The money outcome of this deal will go through a stress test. The Tower promises no smooth road: at least once you will redraw plans on the go — after a price jump, a key person leaving or a forced move. But after the shake-up the business often ends up stronger and more profitable — especially if money went into the foundations (equipment, premises, systems) rather than the façade. This point also lies on the relationship line, so the outcome turns not only on economics but on how you act in a crisis: rescuing the project together or hunting a culprit. After every storm, review the plan, not the blame — then the shake-up works for profit.

captions.finTotal: The brighter the business, the more money

items.meaning: The more visible the business, the higher the income; expectations must not outrun the real figures.
text: The brighter the business, the more it earns — that is the money outcome with the Star. Income here comes from talent and a name, and in a good year it can noticeably exceed the plan. What gets in the way is expectations that outrun the real figures: each next project is planned on the best case, and an ordinary year feels like a failure. This point also lies on the relationship line: if the business's name goes to one partner while the costs and routine go to the other, money starts being divided with resentment. Mutual support shows directly in income here: inspired by each other, you earn more.

captions.finTotal: A riddle of an outcome and money in the fog

items.meaning: Money is hard to forecast; regularly checking the figures turns the riddle into a result and protects trust.
text: The Moon keeps the money outcome of this deal a riddle to the very end. Money here is hard to forecast: a creative project may bring in unexpectedly much, or may take a long time to pay off. The partners need more trust in each other than usual — and more transparency, because suspicion is born in fog. The outcome is eroded by unrecorded debts, hidden stashes, settlements “on a word” and a fear that stops you looking ahead. Regularly checking the figures turns the riddle into a clear result and protects the relationship.

captions.finTotal: Prosperity that grows with the warmth between you

items.meaning: The outcome is visible prosperity and success for both, unless you start competing over whose part brought in more.
text: This deal is one to be proud of — in money too. The Sun promises visible prosperity: steady growth, a reserve, each partner's own achievement and a shared success you won't be ashamed to share. This point also lies on the relationship line, and the sum in the account grows here along with the warmth between you. Comparisons spoil the outcome: whose part brought in more, which acquaintance has a bigger result — competition between you eats up both the warmth and the profit. Gratitude to each other pays off here quite literally.

captions.finTotal: Money that grows year by year

items.meaning: Income will grow over time; write down the rules for dividing shares from the very start.
text: Year by year this deal will bring in more. Judgement reveals the outcome gradually: the business adds something every year, connections and reputation work for you, and what you have built can be handed on or sold at a profit. The budget here is best planned together, discussing the risks openly. Disputes over shares spoil the outcome — especially if the rules for dividing them were not written down from the start — and so does reluctance to keep a joint account. The relationship line meets here too: a grievance left unspoken ends up costing money.

captions.finTotal: A long run and an asset that works on its own

items.meaning: Steady income builds up gradually, so long as routine doesn't freeze prices and clients for years.
text: In money terms this deal is built for the long run. The World puts the result together gradually: steady income and a shared asset that keeps earning even when you are busy with other things. You make the budget rules together and follow them patiently, so money doesn't leak away. Routine holds the outcome back: the same clients, the same prices, the same reports year after year, though the market changed long ago and nobody dares to propose a review. The wide view everything began with is worth keeping in money matters too.

captions.finTotal: Easy money in both directions

items.meaning: Money will come easily and go just as easily; settle old accounts before taking on anything new.
text: Nobody can say in advance how much this deal will bring. The Fool gives easy money in both directions: it comes unexpectedly, through bold decisions and unconventional moves, and leaves with the same ease. The outcome may surprise you — pleasantly or not — but you will always have the resourcefulness to start again. The weak spot is flight: when the result disappoints, it is easy to vanish or catch fire with something new without settling up on the old, and then both the wallet and the trust between you suffer. Freedom with money is fine as long as each answers for their own part.

items.meaning: Income grows through expansion and shared goals; open new outlets once the old ones have paid off.
text: This partnership's money grows outwards. The Empress leads to profit through expansion: more clients, more outlets, a product range that grows out of one successful item. Investment in people, quality and customer comfort works well. Money comes through shared goals: the more clearly you both see what you are growing, the faster one line gives rise to the next. Growing without counting is dangerous: new outlets open before the previous ones have paid off, and spending on growth outpaces growth itself.

captions.finWay: Income built to a blueprint, on a foundation

items.meaning: System and financial literacy lead to income; don't turn the plan into dogma.
text: This partnership builds its profit like a house: to a blueprint and on a foundation. The Emperor lays a system at the base of income: business processes, procedures, financial planning, stable contracts with clear terms. Every step is calculated, money has a purpose, and a reserve is planned in advance. Financial literacy and a clear division of responsibility for the budget help the partners. Rigidity can get in the way: a plan chosen once becomes dogma, new opportunities are brushed aside as “against the rules”, and growth freezes at what has been achieved.

captions.finWay: A community of like minds and recommendations

items.meaning: Money comes through like-minded people, long contracts and referrals; don't argue methods with those who bring you clients.
text: The road to profit here runs through a community. With the Hierophant money comes from those who share your views: regular clients, professional associations, institutions you sign long contracts with, mentors who pass your name on. Income grows not in leaps but because each deal opens the next. The path demands patience and respect for accepted rules. It is easy to step off it by arguing about methods with those who bring you clients, or by reshaping the product around personal convictions instead of what the market asks for.

captions.finWay: Referrals, collaborations and a precise choice

items.meaning: Referrals, collaborations and precise choices bring profit; decisions made on emotion cost dear.
text: Profit here grows through people. The Lovers earn on relationships: clients who bring their friends, collaborations with other brands, partnerships where both sides sincerely want to work together. What sells well is what is beautiful and made with heart. On this path you will have to keep choosing — between niches, clients, offers — and income depends on how precisely you choose. Mood can knock you off course: a decision to buy, hire or give a discount made on emotion costs more here than it seems.

captions.finWay: Profit on the road and sales discipline

items.meaning: Activity and expansion bring profit; rivalry between partners will scatter your resources.
text: The gain of this partnership lies in motion. The Chariot finds profit on the road: new regions, field sales, logistics, tenders won faster than competitors, several projects running in parallel. Speed turns into income rather than bustle when there is discipline: a sales plan, accounts, clear roles. Rivalry can knock you off course: if each pulls in their own direction, resources scatter, and instead of one strong push you get two weak ones.

items.meaning: Contracts, transparent accounts and fair prices lead to profit; verbal promises cost dear here.
text: The path to profit runs through order. Justice pays for care: properly drafted contracts, fair prices, transparent reporting, taxes paid on time. Clients and contractors come back to you because everything is clear with you, and that very reputation brings in money. The path is unhurried, with checks and approvals, and every late payment frays the nerves. What slows it down is the habit of doing business on a handshake: on this road every verbal promise sooner or later costs money.

items.meaning: Knowledge and one-off craft work bring income; check the product against what clients will pay for.
text: Knowledge paves the road to money here. The Hermit earns on narrow specialisation: consultations, research, one-off work of high precision, a product you spent a long time perfecting. Money comes slowly, but from clients who pay for quality and come back. Here it pays better to raise the price than to widen the flow: ten clients willing to pay for precision give more than a hundred chance ones. Insularity gets in the way — the habit of making a product you like yourselves without asking clients. Once a season it helps to go out to people and find out what they are willing to pay for.

captions.finWay: Profit at the market's turning points

items.meaning: Change and trends are your path to profit; don't mistake luck for strategy.
text: This partnership reaches money through change. The Wheel of Fortune pays for turning in time: picking up a trend, switching to a new product when the old one has stopped selling, making use of a chance meeting or a profitable offer. Income runs in cycles, so once a quarter it helps to sit down together and sort out which lines still feed you and which it is time to wind down. You can lose the path by chasing every opportunity in turn and mistaking luck for strategy: fortune favours the prepared, not the fussy.

captions.finWay: Hard tasks that others can't handle

items.meaning: Hard orders and persistence bring money; after every push, stop and do the sums.
text: Profit here is reached through persistence. With Strength, income is earned by character: you take on hard orders others turned down, see a problem more deeply and find an unconventional solution, save quickly and invest in the next step. The partners charge each other up, and it shows in the results. The road takes strength, and its main danger is working yourselves to exhaustion: everything goes into pushes, the accounts are a mess, and what you earned slips through your fingers. A pause after every big project to count and allocate the money helps keep the gain.

items.meaning: Profit comes late and not by the direct road; don't be afraid to widen the niche you found and raise the price.
text: Patience and an unaccustomed view are what lead this partnership to profit. The Hanged Man brings income neither at once nor by a straight road: through a product for those others overlook, through a service where care matters, through a solution found where everyone saw a dead end. Money is paid late, but reliably. Discipline helps, and so does the ability to refuse those who are forever asking for credit. Fear of growth gets in the way: you are afraid to widen the niche you found, or to sell your own idea for more than is “usual”.

captions.finWay: Renewal and cutting away the excess

items.meaning: By cutting the loss-makers the partnership makes room for profit; don't confuse renewal with change for its own sake.
text: This partnership finds money by cutting away the excess. Death leads to income through renewal: close what loses money, optimise costs, change the model in time, move to a new market when the old one dries up. The partners get their bearings quickly and don't regret what they had to let go. The opposite ruins the business — a fear of change that keeps you holding on to a project that stopped feeding you long ago, or, the other way round, change for its own sake, where nothing has time to bring in money.

captions.finWay: Step by step, with regular clients

items.meaning: A steady pace and regular clients lead to profit; haste breaks the rhythm, so settle profit-sharing in advance.
