text: Gradually, step by step — that is how this partnership reaches profit. Temperance leads to income without leaps: the same clients return for years, prices are revised a little at a time, and each new step is taken once the previous one has paid off. The ability to wait for the right moment and plan the budget helps. Haste breaks the rhythm: an attempt to speed up growth sharply — with a loan, price-cutting, a risky order — destroys what this income rests on. Agree on the proportion in which profit is split between development, reserve and payouts — and stick to it.

items.meaning: The premium segment and bold desires feed this partnership; decide in advance what you won't do for any money.
text: Ambition paves this partnership's road to profit. The Devil turns bold desires into income: a premium product, tough negotiations, a knack for selling what people truly want, parallel incomes and risky but profitable investments. The partners spur each other on, and that works for growth. The danger is a thrill with no brakes: one pushes the other towards a dubious step “for the sake of the business”, deals grow ever riskier, and honest rules start to feel like a hindrance. Agree in advance what you will not do for any money.

items.meaning: Income arrives in steps after bold change; the habit of expecting the worst holds you back from the step you need.
text: This partnership's money comes after a rebuild. The Tower opens up income in the wake of decisive change: a loss-making line closed, a new model, a move to a new platform — which then begin to pay off. Taking such a step is easier for two than for one: one sees that it is time to break, the other how to build anew. Income here comes in steps: after each rebuild a leap, then a plateau until the next. The danger is the habit of expecting the worst, which stops you from taking the steps you need.

items.meaning: Money comes through talent, a name and publicity; naive trust in attractive offers can take you off course.
text: Renown lights this partnership's way to money. The Star brings profit through talent and a name: an original product, publications and talks that bring in clients, creative projects that find sponsors and buyers. Money here knows how to come back: spend on development, and new opportunities open up. Naivety can let you down — taking attractive offers from sponsors and intermediaries at their word. Talents left idle cost money too: each unused one is profit missed.

items.meaning: Instinct and non-obvious niches lead to money; don't mix friendship and money.
text: Money here is found by instinct. With the Moon, profit comes from what doesn't lie on the surface: an unusual niche, a creative project, a product that guesses clients' unspoken wishes, a closed club for insiders. The partners sense where to move before the figures confirm it. The road, though, is foggy: income fluctuates, forecasts are vague, and it is easy to mistake hope for a plan. One rule keeps you on course: don't mix friendship and money — no loans to each other, no settling up “on trust”.

items.meaning: Income grows when success is visible to others; pride and deafness to criticism lead you astray.
text: Here you earn by making success visible. With the Sun, income grows in plain sight: one good case study brings the next client, publicity works for sales, and investment in people and quality comes back as growth. Honesty works: a real result shown as it is sells better than an embellished one, and exaggeration is quickly noticed here. Pride lets you down: the certainty that everything will work out anyway, and an unwillingness to hear criticism. Success that is never rechecked against the figures starts costing more than it brings.

captions.finWay: Former clients and a review of old terms

items.meaning: Income returns through old ties and former clients; review the terms even for the longest-standing ones.
text: Old ties lead this partnership to profit. Judgement brings money through the past: former clients who come back, people who remember your work, relatives and acquaintances who open the right doors, a project once shelved that can now be revived. Income grows steadily: work done conscientiously comes back as new orders a year or two later. What slows it is indiscriminate loyalty to the past — holding on for years to clients who pay less than the work is worth “because they've been with us from the start”.

items.meaning: Going beyond borders brings profit if you translate the product not only into another language but into other habits.
text: This partnership's main money lies beyond its familiar market. The World takes income across borders: clients in other cities and countries, online sales, international partners, orders from places you have never been. What keeps you on this path is a shared view of the future: you both understand why the business is going further and don't drag it back to the street next door. What slows it is the wish to work in a new market the old way: a product understood at home has to be translated there not only into another language but into other habits.

items.meaning: Bold experiments and new formats bring income if a minimum of discipline holds the improvisation together.
text: This partnership finds profit where no one has gone yet. For the Fool, money comes from bold experiments: a new format, a product the market does not yet understand, a project started almost from scratch with no ready-made scheme. Lightness saves you — you are not afraid to make mistakes, you try things fast and change course just as fast. The path winds, and it is easy to lose money on it through carelessness: a forgotten invoice, a promise without a contract, spending nobody recorded. A minimum of discipline — shared accounts and deadlines — turns improvisation into income.

captions.gain: Plenty, savings and an earning zone of one's own

items.meaning: Growing prosperity for both; each needs an area of earning of their own, and the budget needs clear rules.
text: This partnership holds the promise of prosperity for you both. The Empress fills the shared money box: savings grow, and there are funds for both development and comfort. At the same time each keeps their own area of earning and their own achievement — so growth doesn't turn into one depending on the other. The gain melts away through extravagance: expensive purchases for pleasure, spending on beauty before profit, an imbalance where one invests and the other enjoys. A joint budget with clear rules preserves the prosperity.

captions.gain: Stable income and protected property

items.meaning: Earnings will become stable and protected; share the management of money so the fortress doesn't become a prison.
text: The Emperor builds income like a fortress: systematic receipts, separate funds for development and for the unexpected, property that stays for a long time. Here nobody lends or borrows, and both of you gain confidence in tomorrow. The fortress becomes a prison when one partner manages the budget alone: the other has to beg for every sum, and new opportunities are dismissed as needless risk. Share the management of money, and both of you will hold the keys to the gate.

captions.gain: Reliability and savings by the rules

items.meaning: For both of you — stability and savings; just don't let caution turn into stinginess.
text: Materially you win on reliability. The Hierophant saves by the rules: a joint budget, savings for clear goals, equipment that is repaired and looked after rather than replaced every season. The partnership brings stability rather than leaps — but nothing you put in is lost. Every expense here is weighed with care, and that can be useful. The gain shrinks when caution grows into stinginess: you skimp on advertising and people, and one starts managing the other's share “because it's safer that way”.

captions.gain: Prosperity that is a pleasure to use

items.meaning: Gain comes through connections and is shared easily; agree what share of profit stays in the business.
text: Money in this partnership is shared easily — and spent just as easily. The Lovers give you both a prosperity that is pleasant to use: good income, beautiful things for the business, the means to invest in the comfort of the team and the clients. Money comes through connections and people's goodwill, and is usually split equally. The weak spot is the principle “we earn in order to spend”: purchases on a whim, spending on image, a constant sense that there could be more. Agree in advance what share of profit stays in the business — and don't revise it on emotion.

captions.gain: Earnings turned into assets

items.meaning: Earnings will quickly become equipment, vehicles and premises; trust the budget to one of you.
text: This partnership's gain is something you can touch. The Chariot gives you both earnings that quickly turn into working assets: equipment, vehicles, a warehouse, new premises. Each can develop their own line and be paid by their contribution, and the joint budget is best left to one of you — there is less tug of war that way. Hasty decisions eat the gain: a secured loan for the next push, a purchase nobody had time to work out, money taken out of circulation for personal ends. Every large purchase should answer the question of what it gives the business.

captions.gain: Transparent income and a reserve for a rainy day

items.meaning: Transparent income and a reserve protect you both; uneven bookkeeping quickly turns money talk into a trial.
text: The partnership brings you both money without surprises. Justice divides income by the rules: shares are written down, expenses recorded, and large purchases decided together and without haste. There is always a reserve and a plan B, so a bad month doesn't become a crisis. Uneven bookkeeping spoils everything: one keeps a stash “just in case”, the other thinks they carry more, and talk of money turns into a trial with accusations. A regular check of each one's contribution by the figures clears such grievances before they pile up.

captions.gain: Income without glitter and spending on mastery

items.meaning: Income will be careful and measured; don't let an unhurried pace turn into giving up on growth.
text: Income without glitter is what this partnership gives you both: careful, measured, with a reserve for the unexpected. The Hermit invests in mastery: big spending tends to go on training, books, tools, and each of you can earn on your own knowledge. Money decisions are made slowly — even a necessary purchase is mulled over for weeks. Trouble comes if the unhurried pace turns into austerity: nobody wants to ask for more, growth is put off, and the gain stays more modest than it could be.

captions.gain: Gain in waves and sharing sudden luck

items.meaning: Luck helps you earn more than you would alone; decide in advance how you split a sudden windfall.
text: In waves — that is how gain arrives in this partnership. The Wheel of Fortune tosses up luck: an unexpected client, a profitable acquaintance, a trend spotted in time. Together each of you can earn more than alone — if you can see opportunities and act fast. Money likes a joint budget and generosity towards each other. The gain leaks away through unjustified risk and envy: others seem luckier, and you want to catch up with a risky bet. Decide in advance how you share sudden luck — equally or to whoever caught it — and ride your own wave without chasing someone else's.

captions.gain: Good income for both, won by grit

items.meaning: Persistence brings good income; control over the money must not sit with one partner alone.
text: Strength of character is this partnership's main capital. Strength promises you both a good income — through persistence and a readiness to take on what others back away from. Money is not spared on development, tools and whatever gives energy: rest, hobbies, sport. A crack appears when control over the money concentrates in one pair of hands: the other is paid “by the rules”, feels like the junior and starts to envy or work at half strength. Open shared access to the figures preserves both the money and the respect.

captions.gain: Patience that pays off

items.meaning: At first you put in more than you take out; compare yourselves with a year ago, not with the neighbours.
text: The payoff here comes late, but it comes. The Hanged Man first asks you to put in more than you get: earnings go back into the business, and little is left for yourselves. Prosperity arrives with patience — and often all at once: the project that fed on your efforts for years begins to feed you. Envy gets in the way: competitors seem to have it easier and faster, while you have only waiting. Compare yourselves with where you were a year ago, not with the neighbours — that shows how much you have grown.

captions.gain: Money from renewal and streamlining

items.meaning: Income appears as you free yourselves of the excess; decide too what to grow in the space you clear.
text: Renewal is the source of gain for this partnership. Death frees money from the excess: you sell outdated equipment, close an unprofitable line, review costs. You both know how to save, find your bearings quickly in new conditions and always keep a reserve. The emptiness after clearing is dangerous: the loss-maker is closed, but nothing new has been launched, and the money just sits there until the next expense eats it. Every six months ask yourselves honestly: what is it time to let go of, and what should grow in the space it leaves?

captions.gain: Living within your means and calm confidence

items.meaning: A calm income within your means suits you both, if you agree on what each of you calls “enough”.
text: Within its means — that is how this partnership lives, and therein lies its strength. Temperance brings an income in proportion to the effort put in: no sharp rises, no debts and no race with competitors. The partners gain a calm confidence in tomorrow, and nothing superfluous is hoarded or bought here. The balance is upset when the partners handle money differently: one saves every penny, the other spends, and each is secretly irritated. Another trap is prosperity for show, to compare with others. A frank talk about what each considers “enough” removes both risks.

captions.gain: Big money with a temper

items.meaning: High income for both demands transparent accounts; greed and secretly recounting shares destroy the partnership.
text: The money here is big — and has a temper. The Devil opens access to high income for you both: each may gain their own line of earnings, and joint investments may yield a return neither dreamed of alone. Clear shared goals and honest accounts turn this energy into prosperity without debts. The gain starts to destroy the partnership when greed comes into play: each feels the other gets too much for too little, and shares start being recounted in secret. The bigger the sums, the more transparent the accounts must be — and the less often you should compare who brought in what.

captions.gain: Big investments that pay their way later

items.meaning: Large joint investments pay off in time; write down each one's share of joint property at once.
text: The material side of this deal is construction, literally and figuratively. The Tower calls for large joint investment: premises, renovation, equipment and a rebuild of the business first take money and then begin to feed you both. The gain goes to those who act systematically and keep discipline by rules invented together. You will argue over different attitudes to money: one is used to risk, the other to saving, and every large payment becomes a test. Write down at once what share of the joint property belongs to each — at the next rebuild this will save both money and nerves.

captions.gain: Earnings through talent and renown

items.meaning: Talent and renown bring you both money, as long as you don't spend it on image before the business.
text: Talent is the main source of money in this partnership. The Star pays for what you do better than others: a creative product, an original approach, a renown that brings in clients. Each of you always has a side job or a reserve, and the shared venture lets you both fulfil what you have long dreamed of. The weak spot is a taste for the high life: costly packaging instead of substance, new debts in place of the ones paid off, spending on image before the business.

captions.gain: A foggy start with room to grow big

items.meaning: The gain will be unclear at first and may unfold later; judge the project by the figures, not by mood.
text: At the start the material side of this deal may look foggy. The Moon often hides the prospect: for the first months it is unclear how much you will earn and when the project will pay off, and the figures alternately reassure and alarm. Often this is just the opening stage — a creative project, an idea that needs time to show itself and let you both think big. The danger lies elsewhere: fog suits things left unsaid — unrecorded costs and money that is “somewhere in circulation”. Don't drop a project that seems to lead nowhere yet, but don't drag it along blindly: after six months, judge it by the figures, not by mood.

captions.gain: Visible growth and status for both

items.meaning: Money and status grow for both if you compare shares by the figures, not by who shines brighter.
text: For both your wallets this is one of the most generous combinations. The Sun promises both of you visible growth: income that allows development, joint investment in people and equipment, status that brings clients by itself. Money here likes planning and accounting, and you are both ready to do it. Success is visible from outside — sometimes so much that competitors grow envious. The gain blurs when the partners start competing over whose share is “more visible”: each invests in their own shop window, and the shared venture gets the leftovers. Compare shares by the figures, not by who talks louder about success.

captions.gain: What has been built up: contacts, clients, assets

items.meaning: The partnership brings steady gain built on what you have accumulated; put on paper what each brings from the past.
text: Material gain here grows out of the past. Judgement draws on what has been built up: old contacts, a client base one of you spent years gathering, a family asset, a project revived after a pause. Above all the partnership gives you both stability — income you can plan and property that stays. The gain is eroded by other people's claims: a former member remembers their share, a relative remembers money once invested. Put on paper straight away everything each of you brings from the past: whose it is and on what terms it works for the shared venture.

captions.gain: A wide market and lasting gain for both

items.meaning: Material gain comes through scale and stability, so long as caution doesn't smother the new.
text: The gain from this partnership is measured in breadth. The World takes both your incomes beyond the usual limits: new markets, clients from other cities and countries, passive income from a shared asset. You win not on quick profit but on stability — things last, budget rules are made together, spending is thought through. Growth slows when the caution of “old is better than new” wins: a promising line is dropped out of fear, and every expense demands a report that takes more effort than the work itself.

captions.gain: Earnings from an idea and a bold format

items.meaning: Gain grows from a bold idea if you split profit at once rather than spending it before it builds up.
text: Materially this partnership grows out of an idea. The Fool earns where others see no money: a bold format, an unusual way of making a living, a project started out of curiosity that unexpectedly began to pay. You both find a way out quickly if something doesn't work, and you share easily. What scatters the gain is carelessness: profit is spent before it has time to build up, and one of you gets used to the other picking up the bill. Split the profit as soon as it comes in — part to each, part to the business — and the lightness won't turn into debts.

captions.hidden: Lavish spending and other people's money underneath

items.meaning: Generous spending and borrowed money at the root of the business may stay hidden; discuss limits and the source of capital.
text: Behind a warm welcome, how your partner handles money may stay out of sight. The Empress loves the good life, and they are unlikely to tell you about this side at once: a habit of spending lavishly, comfort costs that will land on the joint budget, or the fact that their business runs on other people's money — relatives', an investor's, a loan. Rivalry may also go unspoken: if your part of the project moves faster, your partner will find it hard to accept. It makes sense to discuss spending limits at once, find out where your partner's capital comes from and agree how profit is shared when the lines grow unevenly.

captions.hidden: A hidden chain of command and who owns the assets

items.meaning: Talk of equality may hide a hierarchy, and assets may be in one name; secure equal rights in writing.
text: What may be hidden here is how your partner sees the hierarchy. At the negotiating table you hear “we're equals”, but in the other side's head the Emperor's chain of command is already built, with them making the decisions. What may also go unspoken is in whose name the key assets are registered — the account, the domain, the equipment, the trademark — and which rules they intend to bring in once the business gets going. Clarity on paper protects you: equal rights in the articles or the contract, joint ownership of everything created together, and a decision-making procedure written down before the start.

captions.hidden: Who really signs off the decisions

items.meaning: The hidden factor may be a third voice — a mentor, a board or elders; find out whose signature comes last.
text: Ask who stands behind your partner — that is the main question the Hierophant raises. A decision may depend not on the person across the table but on their mentor, a senior partner, a board of directors or family, and you find out when an agreed contract suddenly comes back “for revision”. Something else may surface later: unwritten rules on how reports are kept, whom one may work with, which methods are acceptable. Before you start, find out who signs last, and talk through both sides' standards so you don't have to do it in the middle of the project.

captions.hidden: Parallel options and personal motives

items.meaning: You may be weighed against competitors while doubts go unspoken; discuss exclusivity openly.
text: You may well not be your partner's only option. The Lovers is the card of choice, and here the choice is made quietly: the other side may be talking to your competitor at the same time and drag out its answer while comparing terms, or decide not on the figures but on liking. Sometimes a personal motive stays unspoken: the venture is started for status, or to prove something to someone. Ask directly and without offence whether other options are on the table, discuss exclusivity and a deadline for an answer, and confirm in writing whatever was agreed over a friendly lunch.

captions.hidden: Other projects and a promised pace

items.meaning: Your partner may not mention other projects, or may overpromise on pace; break deadlines into checkpoints.
text: Your shared venture may turn out to be third in your partner's queue. The Chariot races down several roads at once, and you may not be told how loaded they are: two more projects on the side, plans to open a similar line of their own, thoughts of moving. Sometimes the pace stays unspoken too: the person promises a launch in a month, knowing the team is not ready. Before signing, find out how much time your partner really gives the project, break the deadlines into checkpoints and agree that they will not do the same work for your competitors.

captions.hidden: The small print and the clauses of the contract

items.meaning: What is hidden lies in the paperwork: read the whole contract, check the other party and never sign in a hurry.
text: The heart of this deal is hidden in the documents. Justice lives in wording: no one may point out the penalty clause, the termination procedure or a condition tucked into an appendix, and past lawsuits and debts may simply go unmentioned. Not necessarily out of malice: many people believe that if it is written down, it is clear enough. The preparation here is as concrete as it gets: read the whole contract, appendices included, show it to a lawyer, check the counterparty in public registers and sign nothing in a rush “by tonight”.

captions.hidden: Knowledge and problems kept to oneself

items.meaning: Your partner may keep knowledge and difficulties to themselves; agree on shared access to the business.
text: Surprises here come not from deceit but from silence. When the hidden side belongs to the Hermit, your partner is used to thinking alone: they may keep key contacts, product knowledge and doubts about the project to themselves — and bring them out once the decision has been made without you. A problem in their own area such a person will first try to solve alone, and report only when it has grown into a missed deadline. It is more habit than calculation. Shared folders, shared access and a short weekly report help: then knowledge of the business does not live in one head.

captions.hidden: How much your partner's business rests on luck

items.meaning: Your partner may not mention how shaky their business is; ask about past downturns and agree on an exit in advance.
text: Your partner will gladly show you a good year — the bad ones, hardly. Their affairs may depend on the Wheel of Fortune more than they are willing to admit: revenue rests on one big client, the last project closed in debt, or they are already eyeing a new direction. There may be no ill intent in this: the person simply believes the wheel will turn their way again. Ask how they got through past downturns, and before signing agree how each of you can leave the business if circumstances change sharply.

captions.hidden: A hidden wish to lead, and hidden fatigue

items.meaning: The other side may keep quiet about wanting to be in charge, or about overload; agree on who decides what in advance.
text: What tends to stay behind the scenes here is the question of power. Strength can look soft from outside: your partner may not show how much leading matters to them — they agree to equal footing, then quietly take decisions over, from choosing a contractor to running the joint account. The reverse happens too: a confident tone hides overload, and you learn they are out of steam when a deadline is missed. Before signing, write down who decides what and above what sum a second signature is needed, and from time to time ask not just “how are things?” but “are you coping?”

captions.hidden: Favours on credit and an inability to say no

items.meaning: Your partner's concessions may be an advance, with people they can't refuse behind it; ask what they expect in return.
text: What is hidden here is an expectation of something in return. The Hanged Man gives way easily, but the generosity is often an advance: your partner accepts unprofitable terms, takes on extra work, hands over a client — and quietly counts on you returning the favour one day with a share, a post, support in a dispute. If that doesn't happen, the resentment comes out all at once. What may also go unsaid is whom they cannot refuse: a relative promised a place in the project, an old client on a discount at your joint expense for years. Ask directly what they expect in return, and don't accept big favours without discussing their price.

captions.hidden: Changes and exit plans kept quiet

items.meaning: A reorganisation or a wish to leave may stay behind the scenes; set out in advance how the sides part ways.
text: Your partner may tell you about changes once they have already happened. The transition Death brings may stay behind the scenes: the other side's business is going through a reorganisation, a change of owner, the closure of a line — or your partner is already weighing an exit from the project. The past may go unmentioned too: a closed firm, a failed partnership that left obligations behind. In a businesslike way, without paranoia, ask about their plans for the year ahead, check the history of their companies and set out in the contract how the sides part if one wants to leave.

captions.hidden: Softened news and quiet disagreement

items.meaning: Bad news may arrive softened and disagreement stay silent; check plan against fact by the numbers.
text: This partner brings bad news softened. Temperance looks for the middle even in reports: a conflict with a supplier is presented as “a slight misunderstanding”, a cash shortfall as “a temporary imbalance”. Not out of cunning, but from a wish to keep the peace. Disagreement may be smoothed over in the same way: at the meeting they say “all right, let's do that”, and save their discontent for the moment when it is too late to change anything. A gentle habit helps: after every important decision ask what bothers them, and once a month check plan against fact by the numbers, not by feel.

captions.hidden: Someone else's interest and hooks in the obligations

items.meaning: Someone else's gain, or obligations that tie you down, may stay out of sight; always leave yourself a way out.
text: Watch what they could tie you down with. The Devil hides the other side's real interest deep: they may keep quiet about the commission they get from a supplier, their plans for your client base, or the fact that they need the deal mainly to cover their own debts. And the contract may hold hooks: open-ended exclusivity, penalties that hit only you, a loan that is hard to repay later. Coolly work out what each side gains, find out who else has a stake in the deal, and leave yourself a way out of any obligation.

captions.hidden: Cracks that open all at once

items.meaning: Bad news may surface all at once; don't tie the business to one party, and ask outright what could surprise you.
text: If something unpleasant surfaces here, it surfaces all at once. The Tower stands on cracks that cannot be seen from outside: your partner may keep quiet about them — debts, a conflict with a former co-owner, an inspection that is not yet over — hoping it will all blow over. You learn about it not gradually but in a single day, when the problem is already at the door. Prepare not for the worst but for the sudden: don't tie the whole business to one counterparty, write into the contract what happens if things change sharply, and ask the direct question yourself: “What could catch us out?”

captions.hidden: Gloss instead of figures, and secret expectations

items.meaning: The shop window may outshine the business, and expectations exceed what is said; ask for figures and compare plans.
text: Behind a beautiful presentation there may be less than meets the eye. The Star shines through its shop window: your partner may show the best cases and keep quiet about the failures, describe plans as if they had already come true — and sincerely believe in them. The other hidden theme is expectations: they may be counting on a result they don't say out loud — fast growth, a big launch — and be let down when the numbers turn out ordinary. Simple things protect you: figures instead of slides, a talk with your partner's former clients, and an honest discussion of what result each of you will call success.

captions.hidden: Fog around money and the true state of affairs

items.meaning: Your partner's position may be foggy even to them; don't enter the business until it clears.
text: The fog here wraps even your partner. The Moon blurs the picture: they may not fully understand their own position — where the money comes from, how much they really owe, what will happen in six months. Or they may embellish it — not out of guile, but for fear of looking weak. Reputation may stay behind the scenes too: rumours about past dealings that they consider unfair and so never mention, though your clients have already heard them. Expect things left unsaid rather than a trap: check facts against documents, ask mutual acquaintances, and don't enter the business until the fog lifts.

captions.hidden: A costly façade and the leading role for oneself

items.meaning: Behind your partner's bright success there may be heavy costs and a wish to be the star; put joint decisions in writing.
text: Behind a bright façade may lie what is never mentioned at presentations. The Sun loves the footlights, and a partner's success is sometimes put on show more than it exists in fact: a prestigious office, famous clients, and behind them costs that eat the profit. What may also go unsaid is the role they have in mind for you: next to such a person it is easy to end up as a supporting player to the hero, whose decisions are not up for discussion. Ask for financial figures rather than a list of big names, and set out which decisions are taken only by the two of you.

captions.hidden: Old scores and promises to former partners

items.meaning: Your partner's past — disputes with former associates and others' rights to the business — is worth checking early.
text: The most important thing here may lie in your partner's past. Judgement stirs up what has gone before: you may not be told about a long-standing conflict with a former associate, an unresolved dispute over shares or a promise made to someone before you — a right of first refusal, for example. Sometimes an old story returns at the most awkward moment: a former member makes a claim just when the business has taken off. Ask whom your partner worked with before and how it ended, check open court cases and find out whether there are obligations to third parties.

captions.hidden: Publicity, rights and ties in other markets

items.meaning: Plans for publicity, rights to what you create and other markets may stay hidden; fix them in the contract.
text: Anything to do with publicity and rights is easy to leave undiscussed here. The World takes the business onto a wide stage, so find out in advance how your partner plans to talk about your shared venture — in advertising, on social media, at conferences — and who will own the rights to texts, developments, the name. Ties outside your field of view may also go unmentioned: a foreign partner, another market where they plan to take the product without you. Before signing, set out intellectual property rights, agree rules on publicity and discuss what happens if the business enters new markets.

captions.hidden: Inexperience and a light touch behind a bold tone

items.meaning: Bold promises may hide improvisation and a casual attitude; list the duties point by point.
text: The unpleasant discovery here may be the absence of a plan. The Fool walks without a map, and your partner may take on things they have little experience in without saying so: a confident tone, bold promises, and behind them improvisation. Their attitude to the venture may also be unclear: for you it is a serious project, for them an interesting experiment they can easily leave if it gets boring. Ask without condescension what they have done on similar tasks, list the duties point by point and build exit and compensation terms into the contract.

captions.minus: Generous spending and reliance on one source

items.meaning: The downside is spending on comfort and reliance on one source; save in good months and look for a second.
text: This business likes to spend. The Empress brings costs for comfort, beauty and people that don't pay off at once: a good office, gifts for clients, generous bonuses, a renovation without which you “can't work”. There may also be reliance on one source — a large client, an investor or help from family, without whom the business can't yet stand. Periods of plenty will alternate with lulls, and in a lull spending will have to be cut. What saves you is the habit of setting aside part of income in good months and gradually looking for a second source of money.

captions.minus: A rigid hierarchy and control from above

items.meaning: The deal brings a strict hierarchy and little flexibility; settle at once where your partner's control ends.
text: A rigid chain of command is what you will have to accept. The Emperor makes the deal strict and hierarchical: decisions come from the top, rules are written once and for a long time, and your partner may insist on control over key questions — from the budget to hiring. There will be little flexibility, and initiative without sign-off risks earning a reprimand. Another downside is slowness: “measure twice, cut once” applies to every expense. You can live with this if you settle from the very start which decisions are yours and where your partner's control ends.

captions.minus: Procedures, sign-offs and lectures

items.meaning: Formality and lectures come with the deal; separate the rules you must follow from your own zone of freedom.
text: What you will have to accept is rules — other people's, and many of them. The Hierophant slows the deal down and surrounds it with formalities: sign-off at three levels, a procedure for every step, reports strictly to template. Your partner may take the stance of a mentor and explain the “right” way to run the business, even where you know better. Spending is discussed in picky detail, and new methods are accepted grudgingly. One thing helps: don't fight the whole system, but agree in advance which rules are binding and where each of you is free to decide.

captions.minus: Emotions in business and slow choices

items.meaning: The downside of this deal is emotion at work and slow choices; record every decision with a date and an owner.
text: In this venture much is decided by relationships, and not always in the venture's favour. Under the Lovers the partners' mood affects work more than you would like. Fall out — and for a week not even an invoice gets approved; warm to each other — and an important clause goes undiscussed. Another price is endless choosing: two good suppliers or two design options can be debated for a month. This is no reason to turn the deal down, but it is a reason to keep friendship and paperwork apart: warm talks separately, decisions with a date, an owner and a written record.

captions.minus: Constant rush and decisions on the go

items.meaning: The price of the deal is a race and decisions on the run; give yourself at least a day's pause before big spending.
text: The price of this partnership is the race. The Chariot drives on without stopping: deadlines are tight, business trips frequent, decisions made on the move, and there is almost no time to stop and do the sums. Some of what you start will have to be dropped because the market has already run ahead, and some mistakes will come from speed rather than poor judgement. There will be no calm rhythm, so admit it at once and always keep one brake on: big spending and loans only after a pause of at least a day, however hard your partner pushes.

captions.minus: A slow pace and strict paperwork

items.meaning: Slowness and exacting documents are the price of reliability; put verbal agreements on paper.
text: This deal has a heavy paper side. Justice cannot stand haste or imprecision: ideas will take shape more slowly than you counted on, the contract will need several drafts, and the acceptance papers and invoices may hold errors that surface during an audit. Check each clause against the law, and put verbal agreements on paper, even if your partner insists that “it's all clear anyway”. This is irritating, but it protects you: in a dispute you will have something to stand on.

captions.minus: Slowness, silence and working apart

items.meaning: The pace will be slow and contact scarce; urgent questions need their own channel and their own response time.
text: The pace here will be slow, and there will be less contact than you'd like. The Hermit makes cooperation unhurried: your partner thinks every step over at length, answers emails after several days and prefers to study first and act later. There will be little promotion and few loud launches, and the work will often go separately — each in their own area. If you need fast turnover, this will wear you down. It is easier to live with when deadlines are fixed in advance and urgent questions have a separate channel with a same-day answer.

captions.minus: Swings in orders and an unpredictable income

items.meaning: Income will jump about; don't budget on your best month, and keep a cushion for an empty season.
text: There will be no steady schedule in this venture. The Wheel of Fortune rocks the work: a month of orders gives way to a month of silence, a lucrative contract falls through for reasons neither of you controls, and plans have to be redrawn on the go. Some decisions will have to be made in uncertainty, and not every bet will pay off. This is the price of the flexibility the partnership gives. Don't build the budget on your best month, keep a cushion for at least one empty season, and don't blame each other when the market turns.

captions.minus: Pressure, overload and a hard tone

items.meaning: The deal will demand much strength and endurance; decide in advance where each of you has the final say.
text: This deal will take more strength than it seems at the start. Strength here means working at the limit: tough negotiations, deadline pressure, a strong-willed partner who finds it hard to give way even on trifles. One of you may end up carrying more than agreed and tiring in silence. Arguing with this is pointless, but you can prepare: decide in advance where each of you has the final say, agree on a tone — no shouting and no ultimatums — and don't turn every disagreement into a test of who is stronger.

captions.minus: Delays and working for the future

items.meaning: You will have to wait for results and invest up front; agree in advance how to make up for unequal input.
text: Learning to wait — that is what this deal will demand. The Hanged Man suspends the deadlines: payments arrive later, projects hang in approvals, results appear when you have already stopped expecting them. For a while you may have to work for the future, sacrificing current income or personal time, and not always equally with your partner. At times it will seem you give more than you get. Decide in advance how long you are prepared to wait, and agree how to make up for the input of whoever carried more.

captions.minus: Letting go of the old and sharp turns

items.meaning: You will have to give up part of the old and live through sharp turns; decide what is off-limits for you.
text: Something will have to be let go — that is the main downside of the deal. Death brings changes that are not always pleasant: part of the old — clients, familiar processes, even a whole line — will have to be given up, and the new will feel unfamiliar and shaky at first. Sharp turns are possible: your partner proposes rebuilding everything in a month, plans change faster than you can get used to them. There will be less of the stability you want. It is easier to accept if you decide in advance what is untouchable for you — and defend it, while agreeing to change in everything else.

captions.minus: Caution, half-measures and a middling pace

items.meaning: Caution and half-measures will slow the business; choose one or two areas where risk is allowed.
text: The deal will move more slowly and quietly than you would like. Temperance turns into caution in everything: decisions come after long approvals, bold ideas are diluted by compromise beyond recognition, and growth comes without the leaps you may have expected. Your partner avoids sharp corners, and some problems are handled with half-measures for years. The result may seem middling — not bad, but not brilliant either. The way out is to choose in advance one or two areas where you have agreed to take risks, and accept a calm pace in everything else.

captions.minus: Binding obligations and high pressure

items.meaning: Obligations will bind you tightly and the pressure will be constant; every obligation needs a term and an exit.
text: The tie with this partner will prove stronger than it seems. The Devil binds with obligations that are hard to get out of: long-term contracts, joint loans, dependence on your partner's money or connections. There will be a lot of work, the stakes are high and the pressure constant: your partner knows how to get their way, and not always gently. There will be temptations too — to cut corners, to turn a blind eye to something dubious for the sake of big profit. This is the price of serious money. One simple rule helps: every obligation needs a clear term and a way out, and you don't agree to anything dubious even under pressure.

captions.minus: Shake-ups, breakdowns and building anew

items.meaning: Shake-ups are inevitable; a reserve, a back-up supplier and an emergency plan make them bearable.
text: There is no getting through this deal without shake-ups. The Tower promises sudden turns: a broken contract, unexpected costs, an inspection, a move — after which part of the plans will have to be built anew. In a tense moment your partner may speak harshly and decide in the heat of the moment. There will be few calm periods, and illusions about a quick and smooth road will be dispelled in the very first months. Preparation protects you: a reserve for several months, a back-up supplier, an emergency procedure agreed while all was calm.

captions.minus: Beautiful plans that run ahead of reality

items.meaning: Expectations will exceed the result; halve them, and be glad if it turns out better.
text: Beautiful plans will run ahead of reality here. With the Star much in the deal will prove more modest than the presentations promised: deadlines will slip, the first figures will disappoint, and your partner's inspiration will sometimes stand in for a plan. Part of the budget will go on image — a website, photo shoots, packaging, events — that everyone likes but that doesn't pay off at once. You will also have to accept that the business will be talked about more than it yet earns. A sober view helps: halve all expectations and be glad if the result turns out better.

captions.minus: Fog, vagueness and swings of mood

items.meaning: Clarity will be scarce; put important things in writing and check the key figures yourself.
text: This deal will lack clarity. The Moon adds fog to the business: agreements are vague, figures have to be clarified several times, and your partner's mood shifts, taking the plans with it. Some information will reach you late or second-hand. Rumours may circulate around the business that you will have to refute. This is draining, especially if you are used to transparency. It is easier to bear if you put everything important in writing, check the key figures yourself and make no decisions on emotion — neither your own nor anyone else's.

captions.minus: Someone else's pride and the price of success

items.meaning: Your partner will reach for the lead role; agree on publicity in advance and don't measure your worth in mentions.
text: Someone else's pride is the price of this deal's brilliance. The Sun pulls your partner onto the stage: they will want to be in view — speaking for the shared venture, taking the main recognition, having the last word. Other costs of success are possible too — inflated expectations, harsh criticism when something goes off plan, spending on status that eats into profit. Your contribution may get less attention from outside than it deserves. Agree on publicity in advance and don't measure your worth by the number of mentions: your input is seen by those who count money, not headlines.

captions.minus: Someone else's past and third voices in decisions

items.meaning: Your partner's past and circle will influence the deal; put in writing that only the two of you decide.
text: Along with your partner, their past will come into the business. Judgement does not let it go: old obligations and connections will influence the deal — former associates with claims, relatives with opinions, long-standing agreements that cannot be broken. Decisions may drag because they have to be cleared with a circle of people you have never even seen. Paper disputes over shares and rights are possible too. It is easier to accept if from the very start you find out who else influences your partner, and write into the contract that decisions on the shared venture are made only by the two of you.

captions.minus: Conservatism, reports and distances

items.meaning: Conservatism and distance will slow the business; shared rituals and a yearly plan help.
text: Conservatism and distance — that is what you will have to accept in this deal. With the World the business will move more slowly than you hoped: your partner holds on to proven methods, demands reports and approvals, and the new is introduced grudgingly. If the deal involves other cities or countries, add time differences, long trips and paperwork for different jurisdictions. Sometimes it seems everything goes round in circles. Shared rituals help: one big weekly call where decisions are made, and a yearly plan with the new written in from the start.

captions.minus: Chaos, floating deadlines and changing plans

items.meaning: Chaos and floating deadlines are the price of freshness; a few firm rules should never be up for debate.
text: Order is not this venture's strongest side. The Fool brings chaos: plans change on inspiration, deadlines float, agreements live in chat threads, and your partner may catch fire with a new idea and forget the current one for a while. Don't expect predictability, and part of the work of keeping order will fall to you. This is the price of the freshness the partnership brings. A conscious role as the “anchor” helps: take it on by decision rather than with resentment, and agree on a few firm rules that are not up for debate even on the most creative day.

captions.plus: Knowing before others and trust without words

items.meaning: You will know more than your competitors and build a business people trust with their secrets.
text: A quiet advantage — that is what this deal will give. With the High Priestess you see deeper than others: you spot trends before competitors, know how to keep confidential information and build relationships on trust where much is understood without words. Out of this grows a business that works without noise — consulting, research, teaching, a closed club, a service for a narrow circle. The ability to hold a pause and listen works for your reputation: clients feel their secrets are in safe hands.

captions.plus: Growth, new products and care for people

items.meaning: The business will start to bear fruit: new products, clients, a team and income.
text: With this deal the business will start to bear fruit. The Empress brings a harvest: new products and lines appear, clients multiply, the team grows, and income grows with it. You know how to create what people like: beautiful, convenient, made with care. The business takes on a warm, almost family character, and clients come back because they feel that attitude. Projects connected with comfort, beauty, food, children, home and nature respond especially generously.

captions.plus: A sturdy structure and steady management

items.meaning: The business will become solid and manageable, with stable income and assets.
text: This partnership will build something that lasts for years. The Emperor gives it the ability to create a system: a clear structure, smoothly running processes, stable income, assets you can lean on. The business turns out solid and manageable, and clients and contractors see it as a reliable player. The partners join forces and defend what is shared as their own household. The partnership's strong suit is manufacturing, construction, property and anything where order and a long horizon matter.

captions.plus: Authority, a method and a school

items.meaning: You will become recognised experts: a method, a school, like-minded people and formal recognition.
text: The upside of this deal is authority. The Hierophant grows the partners into recognised experts in their field: you create a method, a school, a quality standard that gathers like-minded people and students around it. Together you teach others, gain formal recognition and clients who come on the advice of respected people. The business earns a reputation as reliable and honest. This shows most strongly in education, consulting, certification and work with traditions. Your rules serve people, not just order — and that is why others adopt them.

captions.plus: A business with taste and warm connections

items.meaning: You will build a business people like, and a network of contacts that brings orders for years.
text: The upside of this partnership lies in the people who will be drawn to you. With the Lovers you will build a business people like: a product with taste, a service where clients are treated as human beings, a brand people tell their friends about. You choose well — suppliers, staff, a niche — and can reach agreement with those others find difficult. A network of warm connections forms around the partnership and brings in orders for years. All of it rests on equality: decisions are made together, and each feels their voice in the business counts as much as the other's.

captions.plus: Speed, expansion and a well-drilled crew

items.meaning: The partnership will speed the business up: new cities, new projects and overtaking competitors.
text: The deal will give the business speed. With the Chariot you move faster than the market: you launch projects, enter new cities and countries, overtake competitors and take what others are still thinking over. You act like a well-drilled crew — each has a role, and both pull the same way. Logistics, sales, network expansion, sport and travel go especially well. And you set the goal together, so speed brings results rather than bustle.

captions.plus: An honest reputation and clean contracts

items.meaning: You will build a business with an honest reputation that no one can find fault with.
text: The main achievement of this deal is reliability. Justice gives the partnership what a long-lived business is built on: legally clean contracts, an honest reputation, transparent dealings with clients and contractors. Together you create a business nobody can find fault with, and that starts bringing in orders by itself — people want to work with you because you keep your word. Honesty works hardest when it becomes not only a rule between you but the face of the shared venture.

captions.plus: Depth, quality and expertise

items.meaning: A deep product and recognised expertise — what you will achieve by not hurrying.
text: This partnership can give birth to something truly deep. The Hermit reveals the partnership through quality: a product thought through to the smallest detail, expertise others cite, research or a method competitors don't have. You will achieve what requires patience and focus rather than noise. Knowledgeable people gather around such a venture, and so do clients who value substance over advertising. Time to think is not a luxury for you but part of the work — and it is exactly what makes the product better than that of hasty competitors.

captions.plus: Good timing and a turn for the better

items.meaning: The partnership came at a lucky moment: together you catch chances that would pass each of you by alone.
text: The partnership arrived at the right time — that is its main upside. With the Wheel of Fortune you find yourselves in the right place, catch a wave of demand, get orders that would have passed each of you by alone. The business can grow fast, and with it each partner's opportunities: new contacts, markets, offers you never thought of before. Setbacks are easier to bear because a new chance usually follows them. What matters is being ready when the chance comes: having spare resources and time to decide.

captions.plus: The team's stamina and drive

items.meaning: Together you take on tasks too tough for others and become a visible player in your niche.
text: Together you are stronger than any competitor on their own — that is the main upside of the deal. Strength gives the partnership stamina and drive: you take on tasks too tough for others, sit out long negotiations and get through difficulties without losing pace. The shared venture can become a visible player in its niche, and the ability to see a problem more deeply than others brings unconventional solutions. You energise each other, and the team around you picks up the mood. Where others give up — in hard tenders, neglected projects, markets with strong players — this partnership is only getting into its stride.

captions.plus: An unconventional solution and value for people

items.meaning: An unconventional view gives you a solution others miss, and a venture of real value to people.
text: Together you notice what competitors walk past. The Hanged Man turns your view of a task upside down, and you find a solution where others have hit a wall: an unusual product, a niche considered unprofitable, a way of working nobody had thought of. You are capable of a venture that is useful to people and for that very reason gathers devoted clients. The result does not come at once, but patience pays off: what you grow slowly proves sturdier than quick successes. You only need to give the idea time to ripen.

captions.plus: Renewal and a step into a new stage

items.meaning: Together you let go of what has outlived itself and dare changes each of you would put off alone.
text: This deal will help you both renew yourselves. Death gives the strength to close what was holding you back and begin a new stage: drop a loss-making line, rebuild the team, move the business onto a new model, break out of the stagnation each of you was stuck in alone. Together you dare changes you would each put off for years. The business becomes lighter and faster, and each of you frees up energy for what you never got round to before. And you are both ready to let go of the old — even what you put a great deal of effort into.

captions.plus: An alloy of different strengths

items.meaning: Different strengths combine into one, and the venture grows evenly, without last-minute rushes.
text: The strong side of this partnership is balance. Temperance blends different talents into one whole: one of you brings ideas, the other order, one talks to clients, the other does the sums — and together you get what neither would manage alone. Clients sense calm in your business and come back, and staff stay for a long time. Projects at a junction work out best — between two industries, two markets, two cultures.

captions.plus: Big income and weight in the market

items.meaning: The deal gives you leverage: large income, influence and boldness in what you want.
text: The deal opens access to big money and influence. The Devil leads to what pays most: the premium segment, a second and third income stream, investments that work for you. Together you are bolder in your desires and understand more precisely what clients want — and you know how to sell it. The partnership gives leverage: connections, weight in the market, the power to dictate terms rather than accept other people's. And when the money grows large, you have the generosity to invest in other people's projects and in charity too.

captions.plus: A breakthrough and the new in place of the old

items.meaning: Together you break what kept you from growing and rebuild the business stronger than before.
text: The old walls that kept you from growing can be torn down by the two of you. The Tower breaks what has outlived itself: an outdated model, a failed structure, the habit of working “as always”. You are capable of going through a crisis and coming out with a business rebuilt, stronger than before. Construction, renovation, relaunches, crisis management are your element. You make serious decisions quickly and don't lose your head when things go off plan. Destruction here serves building: you knock down only what you already know how to replace.

captions.plus: Development and a growing team and client base

items.meaning: Growth in every direction: more people, new skills, a broad client base and recognition.
text: The Star in the upside is one of the best promises a shared venture can have. The partnership brings growth in every direction: more staff, new skills for the team, a growing client base, projects that inspire both you and those who work with you. Together you unlock talents that would have stayed in draft form alone, and gain recognition — from clients, the professional community, the press. The business acquires a recognisable face. Dreams here reach the work: an inspiring idea quickly gets a deadline and someone responsible for it.

captions.plus: Imagination and a nose for hidden demand

items.meaning: Intuition and imagination help you create a product that anticipates what clients want.
text: The strength of this deal is imagination. The Moon brings what is born of intuition: a creative product, an unusual service, a brand with atmosphere, a solution that anticipates clients' wishes before they put them into words. You sense the market more finely than the reports show and find niches others don't notice. Your field is art, design, psychology, work with images and meanings. Ideas that come on a hunch you know how to test quickly with a small launch, and to see in time which one will take off.

captions.plus: Growth, renown and warmth around the business

items.meaning: The deal brings visible growth, renown and people who are glad of what you do.
text: Success that can be seen from outside is the main upside of this deal. The Sun gives the business growth, renown and warmth: clients come by recommendation, the team is proud of its work, and each of you gains your own achievement and a reason for pride. You do what makes people happy, and they respond with money and loyalty. You share success gladly — with the team, with clients and with each other — and that only makes it grow.

captions.plus: A second life for an old business, and a legacy

items.meaning: The old comes back to life, and what you create can be handed on.
text: What seemed finished will get a second life. With Judgement an old project is revived, former clients return, years of experience turn into a product, and a family craft into a business. Together you create a business to be proud of. People who trust you from the old days gather around the partnership, and that trust brings in orders. Tradition works as capital here, so family businesses, restoration and brands with a history come to you more easily than others.

captions.plus: Reaching a global scale

items.meaning: The business will move past familiar borders and come together into a whole system.
text: Scale is what the partners will achieve together. The World gives the deal a way beyond the familiar: new countries and regions, international contracts, a product people of different cultures understand, a network of contacts around the world. Together you see things through to the end and assemble the business into a whole system that works without constant manual control. The partnership gives you both breadth of view and a sense that the shared venture is bigger than either of you. Your territory is travel, export, online and projects that bring different markets together.

captions.plus: Freedom, daring and a lively new venture

items.meaning: Bold ideas will quickly become a living business, and a way out will be found from any situation.
text: The freedom to start again is what this partnership gives you both. The Fool pushes you to do what others don't dare: launch unusual formats, try without fear, turn a bold idea into a working project in a matter of weeks. You find a way out of any situation and keep your sense of humour when things go wrong. The result is a business that is lively, quick on its feet and attractive to people who feel cramped by templates. Start-ups, events, creative projects — everything new that has no name yet — that is where you belong.

captions.relCommon: Joy in growth and care for the business

items.meaning: A wish to grow and care unites you; each needs a plot of their own whose harvest they answer for.
text: A wish to grow things is what unites you. The Empress brings together people who love to see a business blossom: you are both glad when the first client brings a second, a newcomer settles into the team, and the product gets easier to use with every version. You both understand that people need care and results need protecting. This common soil is fertile, but rivalry grows on it easily: who put in more, whose line grows faster, who is the head gardener. It is good when each has a plot of their own and answers for its harvest.

items.meaning: Liking and shared taste bring you close; keep the right to argue without falling out.
text: You enjoy working together — and that is the main thing that binds you. The Lovers bring together partners who chose each other deliberately: you have similar taste, a shared view of people and one idea of what a good product should be. A meeting with both of you present usually goes more smoothly: you complement each other and pick up a thought half-spoken. This bond is vulnerable to hurt feelings: if liking becomes the main yardstick, business questions start being settled by mood, and disagreement is hidden for fear of spoiling the relationship. A good partnership needs the right to argue without falling out.

captions.relCommon: Interest in substance and respect for quiet

items.meaning: A passion for the substance of the work unites you; speak about what matters even when work runs smoothly.
text: The partners are bound by a passion for the subject itself. The Hermit brings together people who want to get to the bottom of things: you are both absorbed by the task, both ready to sit over it until you figure it out, and both respect each other's concentration. You don't need to talk much to understand each other, and your rare conversations are full of substance. Such a bond is strong but quiet, and therein lies its weakness: you can work side by side for months without knowing the other is disappointed or tired. The shared venture needs you to talk about what matters, not only about work.

captions.relCommon: Willingness to give way and be a shoulder to lean on

items.meaning: Patience and mutual support bind you firmly — until the giving way starts to run in one direction only.
text: The Hanged Man unites people who are ready to be a shoulder for each other to lean on. You can wait for a project to ripen, look at a problem from an unfamiliar angle and help without sending an invoice: one stays late to finish the other's part, the other hands over a lucrative client if that is better for the business. Often the shared venture is also a form of service for you: a useful product, helping people, work that is not only about money. The bond sags when the concessions flow one way: one carries more, says nothing and stores up resentment, while the other never even suspects it. Now and then, go over the favours out loud.

captions.relCommon: A shared appetite for big money

items.meaning: A shared hunger to earn is what binds you; just don't let it pull you into risky commitments.
text: What draws you together is appetite. The Devil unites people who are not shy about wanting something big: a major contract, their own share of the market, an income that is pleasant to say out loud. You never have to talk each other into working late or taking a heavy but well-paid order — the other is already working out the margin. That drive holds a partnership together more firmly than fine words about a mission. The danger is that two strong desires spur each other on: each new deal is riskier than the last, debts and personal sureties pile up, and neither of you dares to be first to say “this is where we stop”.

captions.relCommon: A shared instinct worth checking against the numbers

items.meaning: Intuition brings you together; test your shared instinct with figures so you don't both get it wrong at once.
text: What unites you is instinct. The Moon brings together partners who understand each other without long meetings: one notices a client wavering, the other has already rewritten the proposal. You are both drawn to unusual work — a niche with no rules yet, a project others find odd — and both know how to keep work secrets. The weak side of a shared intuition is that you go wrong together as readily as you guess right: you both fall for such a niche and miss the figures saying there is no demand there yet. Once a quarter, test your shared instinct against the numbers and show them to someone outside.

captions.relCommon: A wide horizon and a shared philosophy of business

items.meaning: A shared sense of scale and of the venture unites you; compare strategies before they split in two.
text: Scale is what connects you. The World brings together people who feel cramped in one city and one niche: you both think about new markets, foreign clients, a business that can be taken beyond its usual borders. Your philosophy of work is alike — duties split in half, rules made together, disputes settled by talking rather than pressure. The shared picture lets you down when each of you has already finished drawing their own: one insists on their vision of strategy, the other on theirs, and instead of a common plan you get two manifestos. Once a quarter it helps to check where you are really heading.

captions.relTerms: Generous terms under which both grow

items.meaning: Terms under which both of you grow work best; say plainly what you want and don't compete.
text: Generous terms pay off here. With the Empress, agreements work when both of you grow: each has an area of their own to develop, and one's success doesn't shrink the other's share. Trust grows from care and attention: invoices paid on time, comfortable conditions for meetings, interest in your partner's affairs not only when you need something. An open conversation about wishes works well: say plainly what you want from the cooperation. Rivalry and condescension towards whoever is earning less for now wear the partnership down, quietly but surely.

captions.relTerms: Order, divided areas and a firm word

items.meaning: Divide the areas of management and write down the rules; your partner respects responsibility, not titles.
text: Responsibility is what this partner values. The Emperor here demands order: rules that suit both are written down; areas of management are divided; the budget, hiring and strategy each have an owner or need two signatures. Your partner takes seriously someone who keeps their word, comes prepared and answers for their own area without reminders. It is best to speak to them in the language of plans and figures. What to avoid: a contest over who is in charge. As soon as each starts proving their right to command, order turns into trench warfare.

captions.relTerms: Work by the rules and keep your word

items.meaning: Agree formally, show what you know and keep your word; lecturing ruins respect faster than any mistake.
text: Respect here is won by loyalty to the rules. With the Hierophant, work under a formal contract, follow the agreed procedures and show knowledge rather than push: your partner takes seriously someone who knows the subject, draws on experience and does not go back on their word. Shared values work well — when both sides understand what the business is for and what you would not do for any money. The easiest way to spoil the relationship is lecturing: start explaining to the other how things should be done, and they stop hearing even sound advice.

captions.relTerms: Equality, attention and an honest tone

items.meaning: Work as equals and decide together; don't use liking as a lever, and don't put off hard conversations.
text: This partner is won over by attention and honesty. The Lovers need equality: decisions are made together, duties split equally, and the other's opinion is asked before acting, not after. Tone matters to your partner — how they are spoken to, whether agreements are remembered, whether help is thanked. Still, keep a clear business distance: don't discuss them with third parties, don't use liking as a lever, and don't put off an awkward conversation for the sake of good relations — that is exactly how relations go sour.

captions.relTerms: A clear goal, clear roles and a united front

items.meaning: Agree on the goal, deadlines and roles up front; respect here is earned by a plan delivered.
text: Work here on the terms of a clear goal and clear roles. The Chariot does not set off without a route: what result by what date, who leads which line, who talks to the client, who signs. Respect is earned by deeds — a plan delivered rather than promises — and by presenting a united front in public, even if you argued in private. A race for leadership is ruinous: the moment you start competing with each other rather than with the market, the team loses speed.

captions.relTerms: Equal terms, written down on paper

items.meaning: Terms that are equal and on paper; respect rests on precision and on owning your mistakes.
text: Terms with this partner are best made equal and written down. Justice demands clarity: who is responsible for what, how profit is shared, what happens when a deadline is missed — all of it on paper, not in memory. Respect here rests on precision: arrive on time, do what you promised, admit your own mistakes as plainly as you point out theirs. Your partner values disputes settled on facts, without appeals to pity and without hints. Don't cast yourself as judge: start passing verdicts on your partner, even fair ones, and business respect will give way to defence.

captions.relTerms: Time to think and respect for independence

items.meaning: Give your partner time to think and respect their independence; pressure will make them shut down.
text: It is best to negotiate here without haste. The Hermit asks you to give your partner time to think: don't demand an answer at the meeting, send materials in advance, leave room for independent work. Respect here is won by competence — a precise question, a well-thought-out proposal, knowledge of the subject — not by loud statements. Rare but substantial meetings and written agreements work well. Pressure and pushiness spoil the relationship easily: frequent calls “just to check in”, control over every step — and your partner shuts down.

captions.relTerms: Flexible terms with scheduled reviews

items.meaning: Review terms on a schedule, share risks in advance and keep your word in any month.
text: A rigid contract will hinder more than it protects here. The Wheel of Fortune will keep changing circumstances, so the terms are best made flexible: agree to review them at set times — once a quarter or after a major event — and decide in advance how you share risks if the market turns. What is valued here is someone who doesn't change with the weather: keep your word in a hard month as you would in a good one. What to avoid: blaming fate and each other when things go badly.

captions.relTerms: Calm firmness and separate areas of leadership

items.meaning: Stand firm and calm, divide the areas of leadership; pressure will turn your partner into a rival.
text: This partner's respect is not won by force; show your strength calmly instead. Strength suggests holding yourself confidently and evenly: stand firm on what matters, give way on small things and don't raise your voice even in a tough argument. Terms work well where each has their own area of leadership — one negotiates, the other runs production — and each recognises the other's strength on their own ground. Pressure breaks the relationship: an ultimatum or an attempt to force a decision through turns your partner into a rival.

captions.relTerms: Patience, flexibility and clear limits to help

items.meaning: Negotiate patiently and flexibly, with clear limits to your help; playing on pity will poison the partnership.
text: Here the one who wins is the one who can put themselves in the other's place. The Hanged Man advises negotiating patiently and flexibly: hear out what matters to your partner, find a solution where no one feels the loser, and don't rush them for an answer. Respect grows from a readiness to help in hard times — but with clear limits. State at once what you do beyond the contract and what you don't, and learn to refuse politely. The relationship is poisoned by playing on pity, acting the victim and reproaches like “after all I've done for you” — from either side.

captions.relTerms: An honest agreement on change and exit

items.meaning: Set out at once how you change terms and how you part; be first to speak about changes in your plans.
text: Here it matters to agree not only on the beginning but on the end. Set out at once how the sides change the terms and how they part if their paths diverge: who takes what, how the client base is divided, on what timeline. This is not distrust but respect — with such a contract it is easier to work openly. Your partner values decisiveness and honesty about plans: if something changes in your life or business, say so at once. The relationship is broken by imposed changes and abrupt exits without explanation — even the right decision, taken behind the other's back, looks like betrayal.

captions.relTerms: Calm compromise and a balance of interests

items.meaning: Look for a middle where both win; neither haste nor constant giving way works here.
text: The best terms here are born of compromise. With Temperance you negotiate calmly and without hurry: each side names what matters to it, and you look for a middle where both win. Your partner values tact, an even tone and a readiness to give way on small things for the sake of the main one. Agreements about balance work well: a share of profit that matches the contribution, a fairly distributed workload. Haste and pressure spoil the relationship — or, the other way round, the habit of always giving way: accumulated compliance will one day burst out as resentment.

captions.relTerms: Directness about money and equal levers

items.meaning: Name your interest at once and ask for the same; build terms so neither can tie the other down.
text: A direct conversation about money and desires pays better here than any diplomacy. The Devil advises naming your interest at once — how much you want to earn, what share you consider fair, what you expect in a year — and asking the same in return. Strength that doesn't hide behind politeness is valued, and so is honesty about ambition. Terms are best built so that neither can tie the other down — neither with debts nor with access to clients. Attempts to buy loyalty, pressure and playing on weaknesses destroy the relationship.

captions.relTerms: Directness and rules for when the storm hits

items.meaning: Decide in advance how you act in a crisis and how you leave; threats to walk out mid-argument are not forgiven.
text: Negotiate here with a storm in mind. Discuss at once what you will do if things don't go to plan: who makes decisions in a crisis, how you split losses, on what terms one can leave.
