Your partner respects directness — even an unpleasant truth is better told at once than hidden until it explodes. Draw up the working rules together and keep to them strictly. The worst thing you can do is threaten to break up in the middle of an argument: such words are not forgotten, and trust is hard to win back after them.

captions.relTerms: A shared dream, sincerity and support for ideas

items.meaning: Talk about what the venture is for and back your partner's ideas; ultimatums will silence them.
text: Inspiring works better here than persuading. The Star kindles with an idea, so talk to your partner about what the venture is for: what dream you are making real, what will change for clients, what you will be able to be proud of. They value sincerity — say plainly what you like and what you don't, and back their ideas even if you see things differently. Terms should be fixed, but without the red tape that kills interest. Ultimatums, comparisons with others and constant criticism work worst: your partner will shut down and stop offering ideas.

captions.relTerms: Clear words and respect for personal boundaries

items.meaning: Spell out the obvious and record the outcome of meetings; ask straight questions instead of guessing motives.
text: Only clear words disperse the fog in this relationship. Under the Moon, spell out everything that seems self-evident and record the outcome of every meeting: here it is easy to understand each other differently and take offence at what no one meant. Tact is valued too — your partner needs personal space and the right not to discuss what has nothing to do with the business. Trust grows gradually, with each promise kept. Second-guessing spoils everything: don't build theories about their motives — ask directly.

captions.relTerms: Openness and recognition shared fairly

items.meaning: Negotiate openly and warmly and share recognition fairly; comparisons and claiming credit will spoil everything.
text: Openness works here. Under the Sun people agree directly and warmly: they name shared goals out loud, share information, praise for results and divide recognition fairly — in a presentation for clients, in a report to investors, in a talk with the team. Your partner respects someone who is successful but not arrogant, and generous without calculation. Terms work well where each has their own field for achievement and shared wins. Comparisons and claiming others' credit spoil the relationship: once one starts to shine at the other's expense, warmth gives way to rivalry.

captions.relTerms: Long-term trust and owning your mistakes

items.meaning: Build the relationship for the long term: keep past promises, own your mistakes and don't look for culprits.
text: This partner is in it for years, and that is how to negotiate with them. Judgement builds relationships on trust and memory: keep past promises, remember agreements made a year ago, respect their connections and the people who recommended them. Terms are best discussed openly, with the risks laid out, and mistakes admitted before someone points them out. Your partner values a readiness to forgive a slip and start afresh. What works worst here is a hunt for the guilty and reproaches over old matters that resurface in every argument.

captions.relTerms: The big picture, equality and compromise

items.meaning: Start with the big picture and shared values; don't re-educate your partner or demand a report on every step.
text: Agreements about big things work better here than arguments over small ones. The World looks from above: start with the overall picture — where the business is going, what values you share, what markets you see ahead — and fit the details to it. Respect rests on equality and acceptance: your partner may have a different view of work, a different style of communication, and that is no reason to re-educate them. Disputes are settled by talking and compromise. Your partner will take an imposed worldview and demands to report on every step as control — and pull away.

captions.relTerms: Observe, influence gently and keep your distance

items.meaning: Watch more, influence gently and keep a business distance; manipulation is not forgiven here.
text: With this partner it is better to watch more than you talk. Notice how the person keeps their word, how they react to difficulties, what matters to them — and draw your own conclusions without hurrying. Influence here should be gentle: listen, find common ground, suggest rather than insist. At the same time, don't fix on them alone — keep a business distance and other options in play. What not to do under any circumstances: manipulate. Any game is visible to your partner and creates a tension that is hard to remove later.

captions.result: Plenty and a long, fruitful cooperation

items.meaning: Ahead lie a long horizon, growing income and enrichment for you both.
text: Plenty is the most likely outcome of this cooperation. The Empress gives a long horizon and lasting joint work: the business grows year after year, income increases, clients multiply, and each partner grows richer not only in money but in opportunities. This is a case where the partnership truly bears fruit — new products, new lines, new people. The benefit comes naturally if you cultivate it: invest in quality, the team, relations with clients. Generosity without extravagance helps keep the plenty — sharing is fine, squandering is not.

captions.result: A business that runs without heroics

items.meaning: You will gain a well-run system, stable income and assets — a base for years.
text: After this partnership you will be left with a solid, well-run operation. The Emperor leaves behind what the future can be built on: well-tuned processes, documents with which the business can be handed over or sold, a stable position in the market. The partners come out of the cooperation with a system that works without daily heroics. Such a result doesn't sparkle, but it holds for years and withstands crises. Guard one thing: that the system serves the business rather than turning into bureaucracy, where every decision needs three signatures and a week's wait.

captions.result: Reputation, a method and recognition

items.meaning: You will earn a name as people who know their trade, a proven method and loyal clients.
text: The outcome of this cooperation will be a name. The main thing you take from a partnership under the Hierophant is a reputation as people who know their business: a proven method, regular clients, recommendations, formal recognition such as accreditation or membership of a professional body. Working together often turns into teaching — a course, mentoring, a standard others start to work by. The benefit does not come in a rush, but it stays for a long time. For the result to take shape, keep to the agreed rules and don't trade principles for a one-off gain.

captions.result: Devoted clients and a well-matched team

items.meaning: Your main acquisition is people who choose you: clients, contacts and a team.
text: At the end of this cooperation you will have something that is hard to buy: people who choose you. Devoted clients, a strong network of contacts, a team that enjoys working together, a product or brand people grow attached to. You yourselves come away with the experience of an honest partnership: afterwards it is easy to see whom to keep working with and whom not. Such a result brings in money longer than any advertising. Only one thing destroys it: carving up the shared success into “mine” and “yours”.

captions.result: Goals reached and new markets

items.meaning: You come out of the partnership with goals reached, new markets and a business up to speed.
text: The result of this partnership is distance covered. The Chariot measures benefit in movement: new cities and markets, projects launched, tenders won, share taken from competitors. The partners come away with a business up to speed and the habit of setting goals and reaching them. Often the partnership becomes a launch pad for next steps — for each separately or together. To keep the result from falling apart, it matters not only to race to the next goal but also to stop and consolidate what you have won.

captions.result: Settled accounts and a clean reputation

items.meaning: A fair outcome: accounts are settled, and the business stays clean and protected.
text: By the end of your cooperation all accounts between you will be settled. Justice leaves order behind: each has received their share, obligations are fulfilled, documents are in order. This is a partnership that leaves a clean reputation, a legally protected business and a partner you can work with again. There may be no spectacular breakthroughs, but there will be no unpleasant surprises either. The result holds as long as the main principle is kept: agreements are honoured to the letter, even when they could be quietly sidestepped.

captions.result: Expertise and a place in a narrow niche

items.meaning: In the end you gain deep expertise and a firm place in your niche — if you don't keep quiet about it.
text: The main outcome of the cooperation is knowledge others don't have. The Hermit leaves the benefit in the form of depth: a product refined to high quality, expertise people travel far for, a place among recognised specialists in a narrow niche. You will come out of the partnership with experience and an understanding of your trade that won't lose value when fashions change. The money result may be more modest than that of noisy competitors, but more dependable. One thing helps secure it: talk about your expertise rather than waiting for people to find it.

captions.result: A lucky turn and new opportunities

items.meaning: This cooperation may become a lucky turn: the outcome can be unexpected, yet valuable.
text: This cooperation may become your lucky turn. The Wheel of Fortune brings benefit through opportunities: a project that opened a new market, an acquaintance that led to a big order, a decision made in time. After the partnership things usually go uphill, and you both come out of it more flexible and bolder about change. The result may be unexpected — not what you started for, but more valuable. Memory helps keep it: write down which decisions brought luck, and you will recognise the next chance sooner.

captions.result: Resilience and real standing in the market

items.meaning: You will both grow stronger and gain standing in the market — as long as you recognise each other's strength.
text: By the end of this cooperation you will be stronger — each of you and together. The benefit of Strength is resilience: a business that has withstood pressure, a team that can handle any rush, a reputation as partners who can be trusted with the hardest jobs. You will reach goals that seemed too big and earn standing in the market. Such a result rests on mutual respect: as long as each recognises the other's strength, the partnership is solid. But if wins start being shared on the principle of “who is stronger”, the fortress cracks from within.

captions.result: A delayed but valuable result

items.meaning: The gain comes later but proves sturdier than quick success; money follows meaning.
text: Here the result arrives later than you would like, but it is worth the wait. The Hanged Man prepares a benefit that is hard to make out at first: a product useful to people, loyal clients who value your care, a solution competitors will reach only years from now. You both learn to look at the business from another angle — and learn a patience that pays off more than once. Money follows meaning. Don't devalue the result by comparing it with the quick successes of others: yours takes longer to grow and lasts longer.

captions.result: Change with no way back, and a new level

items.meaning: The partnership will lift the business out of stagnation to a new level; give the new order time to take root.
text: The main result of this partnership is change after which there is no way back. Death turns renewal into benefit: the business breaks out of stagnation, the loss-makers close, processes are rebuilt, and both partners find themselves at a new point — with a different scale, product or market. Sometimes the best outcome is a project brought to a dignified close that freed resources for the next one. Change gives you resilience and the ability to rebuild fast. Stability after the storm helps keep the result: give the new order time to take root before you change anything again.

captions.result: Even growth without strain

items.meaning: The business will grow at an even pace, with no crunches and no burnout.
text: The most valuable thing this partnership will give you is balance. Temperance delivers results without strain: the business grows evenly, clients are satisfied, the team doesn't burn out, and profit comes without crunch periods. The partners learn to combine different approaches and find the middle, and that skill stays with both for a long time. Such a partnership seldom brings loud breakthroughs, but it hardly knows failure. To keep the result, don't rush events and don't try to sharply speed up what works well at its own pace.

captions.result: Money, influence and ambitions fulfilled

items.meaning: The partnership may bring money and influence; keep the freedom to run the business rather than serve it.
text: Money and influence — that is how this partnership may end. The Devil gives a benefit that is hard to miss: high income, weight in the market, a seat at the table where the industry makes decisions, goals that once felt awkward to say out loud. The partners achieve what they really wanted — without false modesty. Such a result calls for a sober head: the more power and money, the stronger the temptation to cling to them at any cost. The gain lasts as long as you run the business, not the business you, and as long as each keeps the freedom to leave.

captions.result: A business rebuilt with a margin of strength

items.meaning: The cooperation will rebuild the business on solid ground and free you from what has outlived itself.
text: This deal will turn much in both your businesses upside down — and for the better. The Tower delivers results through rebuilding: old schemes collapse, and in their place grows a business built on truth and with a margin of strength. The partners go through a trial that would have split others up and come out with a sturdy system and the ability to act in a crisis. Sometimes the main benefit is release: from a loss-making project, illusions about the market, habits that don't work. After the storm, finish what you have started building rather than rushing off to break something else — then the rebuild will pay off.

captions.result: Recognition and a name people know

items.meaning: The outcome is recognition and a known brand; put quality above publicity.
text: People will start talking about you — that is the outcome of this partnership. The Star pays here in recognition: a well-known brand, a project held up as an example, publications, invitations, clients who come because your work inspired them. The partners unlock their talents and get what they dreamed of when they started. Money follows the name, and there is sometimes more of it than planned. So that fame doesn't outrun substance, put quality above publicity: a loud name fades fast if there is no real work behind it.

captions.result: A result that develops gradually

items.meaning: The gain will show itself slowly and may prove unexpected; check expectations against the figures.
text: The fruits of this partnership will not show at once. The Moon here is like a photograph developing slowly: at first it is hard to say what has come out, and in time it becomes clear — you have found a niche nobody knew about, created a product that guessed clients' unspoken wishes, or gathered a circle of people who trust you without reservation. The gain here is often creative and intangible, but over time it turns into money. The key is not to deceive yourselves: soberly check expectations against the figures and don't mistake what you want for what you have achieved.

captions.result: A victory visible from outside

items.meaning: Visible success and growth await you both, if recognition is shared fairly.
text: From outside this partnership will look like a victory. The Sun promises success in the plainest sense: rising income, recognition, status in the market, a team proud to work with you. Each partner comes out stronger than they went in — with their own achievement and shared wins. The atmosphere of success draws new clients and offers. The warmth of success lasts as long as recognition is shared fairly: victories that one partner claims for themselves put it out faster than any crisis.

captions.result: A business that can be handed on

items.meaning: The result will be a business able to last and be handed on — provided mistakes are reviewed honestly.
text: The outcome of this partnership will outlive the deal itself. Judgement leaves something that can be handed on: a business able to run without you, a name known through recommendations, client relationships that last for years. Often people remain after the partnership too — apprentices and staff who carry the business on by your rules. And also a sense that you did something important together. Honesty about your mistakes protects the result: admit them, and don't turn a review of failures into a hunt for the guilty.

captions.result: A new scale and a big project completed

items.meaning: The business will move beyond its old borders, and a big project will be seen through to the end.
text: This partnership can take the business to another scale. The World promises a benefit that goes beyond the old borders: clients in other regions and countries, a big project completed that you can talk about for years. You both gain a sense of wholeness — the business is assembled, finished and working. Such a result does not come quickly and demands patience in spending. After that the main thing is not to get stuck in a formula found once, and to let the business keep developing.

captions.result: New doors and the freedom to start from zero

items.meaning: The result is hard to predict but will open new doors; record good ideas while you're fired up by the next.
text: The outcome of this deal is hard to predict — and that is its charm. The Fool gives benefit in the form of new doors: an unexpected product, a fresh format, a market you never thought of at the start, an experience after which both of you can confidently start anything from scratch. You come away from the partnership with lightness and freedom — the ability to try without fear and laugh at mistakes. The money may come unevenly, but opportunities come along with it. Good finds are worth writing down: they are easy to forget once you are fired up by the next idea.

captions.trouble: Rivalry in growth and disputes over spending

items.meaning: Friction will come from uneven growth and spending; acknowledge each one's contribution out loud.
text: Growth itself becomes the cause of friction here. Where the Empress is, so is the question of who brings in more: if one line grows faster, its owner starts looking down on the other, who takes offence and competes. You also argue about spending: one cares about investing in comfort, beauty and people, the other finds it wasteful. An imbalance in routine smoulders too: one handles the clients and the attractive tasks, the other the paperwork and the warehouse, and it is rarely talked about. Acknowledging each one's contribution out loud, and a budget set aside in advance for “the nice things”, smooth the sharp edges.

captions.trouble: A struggle for power and rigid rules

items.meaning: Only a written division of authority defuses the struggle for power and control.
text: The dispute over who is in charge — that is where the difficulties start here. The Emperor brings together two masters, each used to building their own way: one writes the rules, the other doesn't recognise them, decisions are made over the other's head, and control of the budget becomes the ground for a cold war. The tone itself can be harsh — orders instead of requests, nit-picking over details, refusal to explain decisions. What eases the tension is not one side giving way but a clear division of authority — who answers for what and where both must agree — written down and signed.

captions.trouble: Disputes over the right way to run the business

items.meaning: You will argue about principles and methods; write down the shared rules together at the outset.
text: You will argue about the right way to do things. The Hierophant shifts conflict from money to principles: each of you has their own idea of how to keep accounts, deal with clients and build processes, and each is sure their way is the only correct one. A conversation quickly turns into a lecture, and a lecture into resentment. Third parties add fuel: one partner's mentor, the other's relatives, investors with opinions of their own. Friction eases if you write down the rules together at the very start and don't revise them in the heat of an argument.

captions.trouble: Hurt over tone and working swings

items.meaning: Conflicts are born of words and tone; settle sharp questions by voice, not in writing.
text: Friction here starts with tone, not figures. The Lovers sharpen sensitivity to words: a curt line in a message, a forgotten “thank you”, a decision taken without the other — and yesterday's ally is hurt. Conflicts swing back and forth: complete agreement one week, a cold week of silence the next. Gossip feeds them — what one said about the other to a client or a mutual acquaintance — and so does resentment if someone has started working with someone else as well. It helps to discuss sharp questions in person or by phone rather than in chat, and not to air disagreements in public.

captions.trouble: Two at the reins and a fight over direction

items.meaning: The difficulties lie in a struggle for leadership and in haste; divide the areas where each of you leads alone.
text: The main difficulty is two people at the reins of one Chariot. A dispute over direction is inevitable here: each wants to lead, each is sure they know the shorter road, and decisions are sometimes taken alone “while the other is still thinking”. Conflicts flare on the move, over trifles, because you are both tired and in a hurry. Another trigger is work dropped halfway: one is already caught up in a new project while the other finishes the old one. It helps to divide the areas where each steers alone and agree that decisions above a set sum are taken only together.

captions.trouble: Loose ends and delays under the contract

items.meaning: Disagreements will grow out of what the contract left out, and out of delays; put everything important in writing.
text: The difficulties of this cooperation hide between the lines of the contract. Justice holds to the letter, and you will argue about what the contract left out: “but we agreed verbally”, “that was implied”, “there was no such clause”. Every delay — of a payment, a delivery, an answer — turns into an inquiry into who is to blame. Sometimes there is a temptation to cut a corner around the rules, and that becomes the cause of the most serious conflict. Discipline in paperwork protects the relationship: everything important in writing, deadlines with dates, disputed points to a lawyer rather than into resentment.

captions.trouble: Silence, closedness and working alone

items.meaning: Each of you shuts yourself away in your own area, and the other's help feels like meddling; meet regularly to air worries.
text: Difficulties here grow in silence. The Hermit leads each of you off to your own area: tasks are solved alone, information is shared reluctantly, and sometimes you learn about the other's work from clients. One may want to do everything alone to prove they are right, and then the other's help is taken as meddling. Instead of an open argument there is nit-picking at each other's work. A regular meeting with one rule helps defuse this: each names what is bothering them, even if it seems a trifle.

captions.trouble: Streaks, mutual blame and shifting plans

items.meaning: Friction will arrive with the bad streaks; agree how to act in a downturn while things are going well.
text: Conflicts here come in waves. The Wheel of Fortune spins the mood too: in a good month you are of one mind, in a bad one each sees the cause of failure in the other's decisions. Plans change so often that agreements have no time to settle, and unresolved questions are left to drift in the hope that everything will turn round by itself. It is also hard that you see risk differently: one wants to seize the chance, the other to wait it out. What smooths the swings is a rule: discuss how you will act in a bad season while the season is still good.

captions.trouble: Two egos and a contest for the lead

items.meaning: Friction comes from pride and inflated expectations; being first to admit the other is right is worth more than winning.
text: The stumbling block here is pride. Strength pits two strong characters against each other: each has their own truth, each finds it hard to admit the other is right, and an ordinary working disagreement becomes a contest of wills. Expectations of each other can be inflated — you expect the same stamina and standard from your partner as from yourself — and irritation breaks out in sharp words. Overload only sharpens the dispute: when you are both working to exhaustion, there is no patience left. The conflict dies down faster if at least one of you can be first to say “You're right, let's do it your way” — and not count it a defeat.

captions.trouble: Uneven load, guilt and reproaches

items.meaning: An uneven load will turn into reproaches; count contributions honestly and let each other say “no”.
text: Unspoken sacrifices are the hardest thing here. The Hanged Man brings an uneven load into the cooperation: someone takes on more than others, stays late, carries other people's tasks, and then stores up resentment and reproaches. Guilt, pity and accusations of passivity come into play, and deadlines slip because nobody wants to take responsibility for a decision. Honest accounting of contributions and the right to say “no” set the balance straight: let each say plainly how much they are ready to carry, and promise no more.

captions.trouble: Different speeds of change and the shadow of the past

items.meaning: One pushes for change, the other holds on to stability; agree on what you change and how often.
text: What trips you up here is a different speed of change. Death calls for rebuilding everything at once, but usually only one of you hears the call, while the other needs stability — and takes every new proposal as a threat. Add to this comparisons with former partners and projects, nit-picking over trifles, swings of mood. Sometimes one partner's past experience — a failed partnership, a closed business — makes them expect the worst from this one too. An agreement on pace helps: how many changes you introduce per quarter and what stays fixed until the new has taken root.

captions.trouble: Suppressed disagreement and one-sided concessions

items.meaning: The difficulties hide in what is left unsaid; a small argument today beats a big split a year from now.
text: The difficulty of this partnership lies in what goes unargued. Temperance makes the partners too protective of the peace: sharp questions are skirted, discontent is smoothed over, and one keeps giving way while the other doesn't even notice. Over time the common language fades — each speaks politely, but about their own thing. Decisions are put off because nobody wants to press. The way out is regular conversations about hard things, where disagreement counts as normal rather than a threat: better a small argument today than a big split a year from now.

captions.trouble: A fight over the levers and manipulation

items.meaning: Control will be the main subject of disputes; divide the levers in advance: accounts, clients, exit rules.
text: The sharpest issue in this cooperation is control. The Devil unleashes a struggle over who holds the levers: money, clients, access, the deciding vote. Manipulation appears — hints, pressure, playing on weaknesses — and each listens to the other less and less. Money becomes a way to tie someone down, and leaving the business a threat. Drama inflates every trifle. The partnership stays strong where the levers are divided in advance: equal access to accounts and the client base, clear exit rules, and no one able to keep the other “on the hook”.

captions.trouble: Sudden outbursts and threats to walk away

items.meaning: Quarrels will flare suddenly, especially in a crisis; no decisions about splitting up on the day of a row.
text: Conflicts here are like a thunderstorm: they build for a long time, then crash. Clashes under the Tower are sharp — irritation, harsh words, threats of “then I'm out of the business”. The explosion most often comes in a crisis: when something goes wrong, the partners look in different directions and blame each other instead of saving the project. Another detonator is unshared responsibility: nobody knows whose task it was. What saves you is an agreement made in calm times: no decisions about splitting up on the day of a quarrel, and the debrief only the next day.

captions.trouble: Inflated expectations and ultimatums

items.meaning: Disappointments will grow out of perfect pictures; set goals with figures and deadlines.
text: Inflated expectations turn into disappointments here. The Star makes the partners idealists: each paints a brilliant future for the shared venture and is upset when reality proves more modest. Hence criticism, comparisons with more successful competitors, ultimatums of “either this, or I'm leaving”. Sometimes one enjoys the inspiring side of the project and leaves the routine and responsibility to the other. A sober plan brings you back to earth: goals with figures and deadlines you can check against — then disappointment gives way to a correction of course.

captions.trouble: Guesswork, suspicion and things left unsaid

items.meaning: Guesswork and secrets breed suspicion; voice any doubt the same day.
text: The hardest conflicts here are born of guesswork. The Moon prepares the ground for suspicion: one leaves something unsaid, the other fills in the gap, and a week later both are sure of a version that never happened. Anxiety makes you double-check, and double-checking gives offence. Secrets spoil the relationship too — information held back “just in case” — and so do disappointments over trifles blown up to the size of betrayal. One rule clears the air: voice any doubt the same day, and never draw conclusions about the other's motives without asking them first.

captions.trouble: Rivalry for attention and credit

items.meaning: Publicity and credit will become grounds for disputes; decide in advance who represents the business where.
text: The struggle for the spotlight — that is where friction begins. Under the Sun there is a rivalry for attention: who speaks at the conference, whose name appears in the interview, whom clients write to directly. Comparisons, harsh criticism and one partner's habit of claiming shared successes sharpen the dispute. The reverse happens too — one buries themselves in work, and the other feels left out. What lowers the heat is publicity divided in advance — who represents the business in which situations — and the habit of acknowledging each one's contribution out loud.

captions.trouble: Old grievances and the hunt for someone to blame

items.meaning: Old slips will resurface in new disputes; see every conflict through to the end in conversation.
text: The past will not let go in this partnership. Judgement gives the partners long memories for grievances: an old slip resurfaces in every new dispute, the culprit is sought longer than the solution, and admitting one's own mistake proves hardest of all. There can be a sharp cooling too: after one serious mistake the other speaks dryly and only about work for months. Sometimes the past steps in in person — a former associate of one of you with an unfinished story of their own. It helps to see every conflict through to the end in conversation: what happened, what we change — and never to return to it.

captions.trouble: Two worldviews and attempts to re-educate

items.meaning: Conflicts will be about the philosophy of the business; before objecting, ask why your partner sees it differently.
text: Two finished views of the business collide here. Each of you has a World of your own: your own strategy, your own work culture, your own idea of “how things are done”, and each tries to re-educate the other. The arguments are not about figures but about philosophy, and so they drag on. The atmosphere is heated by mockery of the partner's plans, secrets that build up over years, and a routine in which nobody has changed anything for a long time. Respect for the other's experience reconciles the partners: before objecting, ask why your partner sees things differently.

captions.trouble: Blurred roles and a game without rules

items.meaning: Grievances will grow out of uncertainty; formalise roles, deadlines and exit terms.
text: Uncertainty is the main source of friction in this partnership. The Fool turns it into a game without rules: roles are not fixed, obligations are vague, one makes a decision on a hunch and the other learns of it after the fact. One treats the venture seriously, the other as an interesting adventure, and that breeds grievances. When problems begin, it is easy to dodge the conversation, laugh it off or vanish for a week. Simple formalisation helps: who is responsible for what, by when, and what happens if someone wants to leave — without it, freedom quickly turns into chaos.

captions.view: Reserve, and the trust that secrets bring

items.meaning: It is you whom people trust with secrets, and that is an advantage; don't keep your position to yourself too long.
text: Reserve is the first thing your partner notes in you: you know more than you say. The High Priestess makes you a keeper of knowledge and secrets: you listen carefully, notice hidden motives, can read between the lines of a contract and never let others' secrets out. Trust is your main trump card: people discuss with you what they won't tell others, and important news reaches you first. The same reserved manner can put people on guard. If you keep quiet about your position for long or answer evasively, your partner will start guessing what you are hiding and whose side you are on.

captions.view: A person of plenty, around whom things grow

items.meaning: A gift for growing and caring is your trump card; show that you can do the sums as well.
text: Growth and care are what you bring to the business, and your partner notices it first. The Empress gives you the image of a person of plenty: you look after clients, create comfort, know how to make a product beautiful and warm, and your generosity wins people over. Your advantage is the ability to grow things: a team, a client base, a project from zero to profit. The downside of this image is a suspicion of extravagance. Spend more on entertaining than on the business, or dodge a hard decision for the sake of a good atmosphere — and your partner will doubt that you can manage money.

captions.view: In command, with everything under control

items.meaning: Solidity and control are your strength; the key is not to come across as the boss.
text: To the other side you are the one in command. The Emperor paints you as someone who has everything under control: structure, a plan, resources, clear answers to “who, when and with whose money”. Solidity works for you: it feels safe to invest alongside you, because you don't abandon what you start and you stand by your words. But that solidity can also scare people off. If you speak in a commanding tone, leave the other no room for decisions or keep your distance too rigidly, your partner will see in you not a support but a boss they will have to obey.

captions.view: The authority of an expert taken at their word

items.meaning: Your partner sees you as an expert and mentor; your trump card is expertise, as long as it doesn't talk down.
text: In your partner's eyes you are a person of authority. The Hierophant makes you someone whose word is trusted: you know the subject, draw on experience, keep agreements and understand how the rules of the industry work. Next to you the other side feels the business will be run honestly, and readily asks your advice. This is a strong card in negotiations. It turns against you when expertise sounds condescending: a mentor's tone, “I know better”, a lecture instead of an answer — and your partner starts to see you not as an adviser but as an inspector.

captions.view: Charm and a gift for winning people over

items.meaning: Your advantage is charm and taste; keep your decisions firm so you aren't taken for a creature of mood.
text: You are pleasant to deal with — that is how your partner sees you. The Lovers give you charm, a gift for winning people over and good taste: you easily find common ground with clients, know how to present a product and turn a business meeting into a conversation people want to continue. This is your main advantage — people choose you. The flip side of the image is doubt about your decisiveness: a long choice between options and hurt at business criticism will convince your partner that deals with you go through mood, not figures.

captions.view: The engine that gets the business moving

items.meaning: Your trump card in your partner's eyes is speed and drive; don't let them turn into pressure.
text: You are the one who gets things moving. Your partner sees the Chariot in you — someone who takes a task and drives off with it: you answer quickly, don't shy away from business trips, bring a launch in on time and defend the joint project before anyone. Your advantage is speed and drive, and your partner values it. The downside of the same image is a sense that you rush and push. If you demand an answer “by tonight” or start deciding for both, the other side may feel it is being driven somewhere without being asked the route, and resist out of sheer stubbornness.

captions.view: Reliability, precision and honest dealing

items.meaning: To your partner you are a person of your word and of the document; make sure precision doesn't look like distrust.
text: Next to you, your partner feels safe about documents and money. Justice makes you reliable in their eyes: you read contracts, deliver what you promise on time, count carefully and judge disputes on facts rather than liking. That is your advantage — with you it is not frightening to sign for a large sum. The same image can seem cold: if you haggle over every comma and check every figure three times, the other side will feel distrusted. Sometimes it helps to show that behind the precision lies not suspicion but respect for the shared venture.

captions.view: An expert who says little, but to the point

items.meaning: Depth and independent judgement are your strength; explain your decisions so as not to seem closed.
text: Your partner sees you as an expert who says little but to the point. The Hermit gives you a reputation as someone who has dug deeper into the subject than others: you don't rush to answer, but your advice is considered and your analysis holds up. Knowledge and independent judgement are your capital in negotiations: you are hard to talk into anything dubious, and that inspires trust. The flip side is an air of being closed. Vanish for a week, answer in monosyllables, leave a decision unexplained — and the other side is already guessing what you are thinking and suspecting coldness where there is none.

captions.view: A person of luck and flexible decisions

items.meaning: Your partner values your flexibility and sense of timing; consistency in small things keeps their trust.
text: Your partner links good luck with you. The Wheel of Fortune in your image makes you the one who brings chances: you know where an opening has appeared, adapt the plan easily to new conditions and don't panic when things go off script. The other side values your flexibility and feel for the moment — around you, things seem to move by themselves. But flexibility is easily mistaken for inconstancy: if you often change decisions, move meetings or catch fire with a new idea every month, you will be seen as someone who cannot be relied on for the long haul.

captions.view: Will, composure and the ability to take a blow

items.meaning: Composure and will make you a pillar; don't let confidence sound like superiority.
text: The first thing your partner reads in you is force of character. Strength marks you as someone who can take a blow: you are confident, can organise people, take the initiative and keep your composure in hard negotiations. Your advantage is stamina and will: you can be relied on when a project is on fire. This image is easy to overdo. If confidence sounds like superiority and initiative like a wish to control everything, the other side will go on the defensive: bargain harder, keep their distance, look for where you are weaker. A softer tone does not diminish strength; it makes it acceptable.

captions.view: Listening well and finding a way out of a deadlock

items.meaning: Flexibility and the gift of listening serve you in talks; don't let your willingness to yield look like weakness.
text: You can look at the business through your partner's eyes — and they notice it. The Hanged Man gives you patience, flexibility and a rare quality: a readiness to hear the other side and propose a solution that benefits both. You don't press, don't rush and find an unexpected way out where negotiations have reached a deadlock. This is a strong advantage until it is taken for weakness. Concessions made too readily, work beyond what was agreed, a price you never named — and your partner gets used to the idea that you need not be reckoned with.

captions.view: Fresh ideas and the courage to change

items.meaning: Your partner expects renewal and bold ideas from you; don't break agreements without explanation.
text: A fresh wind — that is how the other side perceives your arrival. Death shows you to your partner as a source of renewal: you bring new ideas, are ready to put them into practice at once, are not afraid of risk and stay confident while others hesitate. Your trump card is the courage to change: with you it is possible to close what has outlived itself and start anew. The danger of this image lies in abruptness. If you break the usual order without explanation or drop agreements too easily for the sake of a new idea, your partner will begin to fear that one day they will be dropped just as easily.

captions.view: Calm, measure and diplomacy

items.meaning: Your diplomacy helps find the middle ground; don't agree to everything for the sake of peace.
text: Calm is the first thing the person across the table feels in you. Temperance gives you the role of a person of measure: you don't raise your voice, you look for compromise, can reconcile different interests and don't rush events. Your advantage is diplomacy: where negotiations stall, you find a middle ground that suits both. The price of such softness is the risk of seeming too accommodating. If you agree to everything for the sake of peace and never name your limits, your partner will stop treating your opinion as a position that has to be taken into account.

captions.view: Grip, magnetism and boldness with money

items.meaning: Your drive brings deals to signature; don't let it look like you're playing your own game.
text: Grip is what your partner values in you — and is a little wary of. The Devil gives you magnetism and ambition: you know how to persuade, aren't shy about discussing big money and know what the people on the other side of the table want. Drive and boldness are prized here: you bring deals to signature where others backed off. The same magnetism arouses caution. If you press, play your own game too obviously or promise the earth, your partner will start looking for a catch and double-checking your every word.

captions.view: The one people call when everything is collapsing

items.meaning: In a crisis you can be relied on; in calm times, don't break what still works.
text: You are the one people call when everything is falling apart. The Tower casts you as the crisis headquarters: while others look for someone to blame, you are already counting losses and sketching a plan, and you tell an unpleasant truth at once rather than waiting for it to surface by itself. Your advantage is resilience and directness: with you, a hard period is not frightening. But in calm times such decisiveness can alarm. When you cut too hastily, break what still works or speak too harshly, your partner starts to expect from you not rescue but a new explosion.

captions.view: Inspiration, talent and vision

items.meaning: Your vision inspires; back your fine plans with figures and deadlines.
text: After the first meeting people say of you: inspiring. The Star presents you as a person with an idea — sincere, talented, able to infect both clients and the team with your vision. You can show what the shared venture could become and draw attention to it — that is your advantage. Publicity, presentations and working with an audience come easily to you. The danger is being taken for a dreamer: beautiful plans without figures and deadlines, promises that outrun capabilities — and your partner starts taking your words with a pinch of salt.

captions.view: Intuition and a feel for the unspoken

items.meaning: Intuition works for you; explain your conclusions so your air of mystery doesn't look like a double game.
text: You are hard to read completely — and that is your strength. The Moon surrounds you with the aura of someone who senses more than they say: you guess the mood of a negotiation, notice what others miss and offer solutions that seem glimpsed from the future. Your partner values your intuition and creative eye. Only, from outside, an air of mystery looks like secrecy. If you don't explain where your conclusions come from, dodge direct questions or change position without warning, your partner will begin to suspect a double game where there is none.

captions.view: The charm of success and generosity

items.meaning: Your success draws people in; make sure your partner doesn't feel like the background.
text: The success you radiate is noticeable from the doorway. The Sun draws people to you: you are open, confident, generous with ideas and praise. Your advantage is energy and the charm of success: clients remember you, investors trust you, the team enjoys working with you. The image loses warmth when there is too much of you in it: stories of your own victories, a habit of taking the floor at meetings, condescension towards those who are less successful for now. Then your partner begins to feel like the background.

captions.view: A person with a history, a reputation and connections

items.meaning: You are trusted for your reputation and loyalty; don't let the past slow your decisions.
text: You are seen as a person with a history. Judgement shows your partner a past that can be trusted: reputation, recommendations, old connections, loyalty to your own people. What works for you is the reliability of someone who holds on to long relationships and doesn't drop what they start halfway. People want to work with you for years. The image fades if the past starts getting in the way of the present: you appeal to “how it used to be”, are slow to decide, and consult your own circle longer than you consult your partner.

captions.view: A broad outlook and an eye for the whole

items.meaning: Scale and diplomacy work for you; leave room for someone else's picture of the world.
text: Your partner notices your broad outlook at once. The World makes you, in their eyes, someone who sees the whole picture: you have connections beyond one market, experience with different people and the ability to negotiate without pressure. Scale and diplomacy are what you are valued for: with you the business can be taken beyond its usual borders and seen through to the end. What can let you down is the impression that you have already decided everything for yourself. If you set out your picture of the world too confidently and leave no room for theirs, your partner will feel like a pupil rather than an equal.

captions.view: Fresh solutions and freedom from templates

items.meaning: Your lightness and fresh ideas are valuable as long as you are reliable in what matters.
text: Lightness is what your partner finds in you and lacks themselves. With the Fool you are, to your partner, a person of fresh solutions: you are not afraid to start from zero, you suggest unexpected moves, defuse tension with a joke and get on with people easily. Freedom from templates is the main thing you bring: where others see risk, you see an interesting opportunity. This image lets you down on serious matters. One late arrival, one forgotten agreement, a joke where a serious answer was expected — and the other side will decide you can't be relied on in what matters.
